parts.text:
You are porting an existing LibGDX Java game to a real Nintendo DS ROM in C.

REPO: /home/runner/hub-work/elementia/code
Original Java (read for reference): core/src/main/java/com/elementia/**
Your output: nds/source/gfx.c and nds/source/font.c  (CREATE BOTH)

=== ENVIRONMENT ===
* libnds 2.0 + calico + devkitARM. Build whole ROM with `./nds/build.sh` (Docker, 1-2 min).
* Syntax check ONE file (fast, ~15s):
    /home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp/synx.sh nds/source/gfx.c
  It runs arm-none-eabi-gcc -fsyntax-only with the right -I/-iquote paths, prints diagnostics, always exits 0.
* libnds APIs you may use: <nds.h>, vramSetBankA(VRAM_A_MAIN_BG), dmaCopy, DMA3, DMA_SRC_INC/DMA_DST_INC/DMA32,
  swiWaitForVBlank, powerOn(POWER_ALL_2D), lcdMainOnTop().
* Do NOT write comments unless they carry non-obvious information (no "// loop", no "// init").

=== DESIGN (already fixed, do not change) ===
* DS native resolution 256x192. The whole game renders into a software framebuffer `u16 fb[256*192]`
  in main RAM, DMA'd to VRAM once per frame during vblank (Mode 3, VRAM_A_MAIN_BG).
* ALL coordinates use a BOTTOM-LEFT origin (same convention as LibGDX SpriteBatch), so you convert:
  screen row = SCRH-1-y.
* Two coordinate spaces:
  - world space (default for the game world): gfxSetWorld(camX, camY) then draw calls take WORLD
    coordinates; the renderer maps them to screen with  (sx = round((wx - camX) / WORLD_SCALE)),
    i.e. the world is rendered at HALF scale (WORLD_SCALE == 2 from nds/include/config.h).
    A 32px world tile therefore lands on 16 screen pixels.
  - screen space: gfxResetWorld() then draw calls take raw screen pixels, no camera, no scaling.
  A "draw" call receives world or screen coords depending on the current transform. Implement this as
  a single helper `map(float *sx, float *sy, float x, float y)` that converts + clamps.
* Draw calls take FLOAT coords (world coords are fractional), so round to integers once per call, never
  inside the inner pixel loop.

=== FILES ALREADY WRITTEN - READ THEM, THEY ARE THE CONTRACT ===
* nds/include/config.h   - constants, WORLD_SCALE
* nds/include/gfx.h     - the EXACT API you must implement (do not change the signatures)
* nds/include/font.h    - the EXACT API you must implement
* nds/FORMATS.md        - binary layout of the baked asset blobs (fonts.bin) - follow it exactly
* nds/include/element.h - rgb555() helper for 0xRRGGBB -> 15bpp

NEVER edit anything in nds/include/. If you are convinced a header must change, report it instead.

=== TASK 1: nds/source/gfx.c ===
Implement everything declared in nds/include/gfx.h:

* `gfxInit()` - powerOn(POWER_ALL_2D), lcdMainOnTop(), vramSetBankA(VRAM_A_MAIN_BG), zero the framebuffer,
  reset the transform and the tint to opaque white.
* `gfxBeginFrame()` - reset the transform to screen space, tint to opaque white, and clear the whole
  buffer to the last colour passed to gfxClear (or black). Do NOT DMA anything.
* `gfxFlip()` - swiWaitForVBlank() then dmaCopy the 256*192 halfwords to VRAM_A.
  Important for bandwidth: only copy the rows that actually changed since the previous flip. Keep a
  shadow copy of what was last sent (256*192 halfwords of main RAM is fine, we have ~3.5MB) plus a
  per-row "dirty" byte array; compare rows and only DMA the contiguous spans that differ. When the whole
  screen changes, that degenerates to one DMA of the full buffer, which is acceptable.
* `gfxClear(u16)`.
* `gfxSetWorld(float camX, float camY)` / `gfxResetWorld()`.
* `gfxSetTint(u16, u8)` - global modulate applied to textured draws (SpriteBatch#setColor equivalent).
* `gfxRect/gfxRectA/gfxLine/gfxCircle` - solid geometry, clipped to the framebuffer. They obey the
  current transform too, because the world renderer draws thousands of solid-coloured quads in world
  space - that is the whole point.
  `gfxRectA` alpha blends: out = (dst*(255-a) + colour*a) / 255.
  `gfxCircle` is a filled circle with a simple midpoint/span rasteriser.
* `gfxTex/gfxTexFlipX/gfxTexRegion/gfxTexRegionFlipX` - scaled, tinted, alpha-blended textured quads.
  The Tex is `{u16 w,h; const u16 *px; const u32 *mask;}`: px is a 15bpp colour plane (row major,
  top-left origin inside the texture) and mask is a 1bpp coverage plane (1 = opaque, LSB = leftmost).
  Sampling is NEAREST with a fixed-point 16.16 source step, so any destination size works.
  Alpha blending of a tinted sprite: t = (texel & 0x7fff) tinted by `tint` channel-wise
  ((texel_r * tint_r + 127) / 255 etc.), a = coverage255 * tintAlpha / 255, then blend into dst.
  Clipping must be exact: a quad partially off screen must not wrap.
* `gfxTexRot(t, cx, cy, size, angle)` - inverse-rotate each destination pixel back into texture space
  and nearest-sample; pixels outside the unit square are skipped. Only used for the melee slash arc,
  at most a couple per frame, so a slow implementation is fine.

PERFORMANCE - this matters. A single frame issues up to ~2500 quads. Requirements:
* No floating point inside pixel loops: precompute integer source step (fixed point 16.16),
  destination bounds, and the per-channel tint lookup.
* Early-out empty rectangles.
* Build with -O2 (the project does).

=== TASK 2: nds/source/font.c ===
Implement everything declared in nds/include/font.h, reading `fonts.bin` (see nds/FORMATS.md).

The blob is linked into the ROM. bin2o (re-implemented in nds/tools/bin2o.py) emits this header, which
you include:
    #include "fonts_bin.h"        // declares _fonts_bin_start[] / _fonts_bin_size
(the ARM9 Makefile has nds/gen on its include path, so `#include "fonts_bin.h"` resolves.)
The generated header also defines the convenience macro `fonts_bin`.

* `fontInit()` - validate the magic ('FNTS'), parse the 3 font tables, copy the atlas bitmaps into a
  static buffer (the ROM blob is directly readable on DS for the ARM9 image, but copying to main RAM
  makes random access uniform - a plain memcpy is fine).
  Build per-font a sorted array of glyphs plus a direct-mapped cache for codepoints (Cyrillic block
  plus Latin/digits/punctuation): a 512-entry u16 table indexed by (cp & 0x1FF) is plenty, fall back to
  a binary search otherwise.
* UTF-8 DECODE: `textDraw` takes UTF-8 and must decode multi-byte sequences correctly. The game text
  is Russian, so this is not optional.
* `fontSetTint(u16, u8)`.
* `textDraw(x, y, font, utf8)` - draws with the pen baseline at (x, y) (LibGDX BitmapFont convention,
  the caller passes the baseline y). Returns the total advance in SCREEN pixels (float for API
  compatibility, but the value is integral).
* `textWidth(utf8, font)` and `textHeight(font)`.
* Newlines inside the string must advance to the next line (advance = 0, y -= lineHeight). The dialogue
  box relies on this.
* Unknown codepoints render as nothing and advance by the font's average advance.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
* Both files must pass `/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp/synx.sh <file>` with ZERO errors and zero
  warnings from -Wall -Wextra.
* No undefined symbols beyond the two blob symbols above.
* Do not touch any other file in the repo.

=== REPORT ===
Return: the two file paths, a 5-10 line summary of the blitter/dirty-row strategy, the final blob
symbol names you rely on, and anything in the headers you had to work around.
Let me start by reading the contract files to understand what I need to implement.
I'll start by reading all the contract files.

# Binary asset formats

Two blobs are produced offline by `nds/tools/nds_bake.py` (run by
`nds/gen/Makefile`) and linked into the ARM9 image with `bin2o`:

* `gen/art.bin`   – sprites and tiles
* `gen/fonts.bin` – three baked bitmap fonts (Latin + Cyrillic)

Both are little-endian and addressed from the start of the blob.

---

## art.bin

```
u32  magic     = 'ARTB' (0x42525441)
u16  version   = 1
u16  count     number of textures
u32  entrySize = 28
Entry entries[count]        // no padding, tightly packed
u16  pixelBytes             // total, multiple of 4
u16  pad0
u8   nameLen
u8   reserved
Entry entry[count]
--- data follows the table, in table order ---
u16  pixels[pixelBytes/2]   // RGB555, row major, top-left origin
u32  masks[pixelBytes*2/8]  // 1bpp coverage, row major, LSB = leftmost pixel
```

`Entry` (28 bytes):

```
u8   nameLen    length of the NUL terminated ASCII name that follows
u8   reserved
u16  w
u16  h
u32  pixelOff   byte offset of the colour plane inside `pixels`
u32  maskOff    byte offset of the coverage plane inside `masks`
u8   name[nameLen] (padded so the struct is exactly 28 bytes)
```

Canonical names, in the order the baker emits them:

```
grass dirt stone ice snow brick lavaA lavaB water
platform crystal tree chest hero slime wisp golem boss waypoint
```

Anything missing from the PNG set is simply absent; the C side falls back to a
procedurally painted texture.

---

## fonts.bin

```
u32  magic    = 'FNTS' (0x53544e46)
u8   count    number of fonts (3)
u8   reserved[3]
Font fonts[count]
--- data follows the table, in table order ---
```

`Font` header:

```
u8   glyphCount
u8   lineHeight   pixels between baselines
u8   ascent       pixels above the baseline to the cap line
u8   reserved
u32  atlasOff     byte offset of the 1bpp atlas inside the blob
u32  atlasW
u32  atlasH
Glyph glyphs[glyphCount]   // sorted ascending by codepoint
```

`Glyph` (16 bytes):

```
u32  codepoint   UTF-8 decoded
u16  advance     pen movement in pixels (unsigned, 8.8 would be nicer but the
                 font is baked at one size so integers are enough)
u16  x           ink box inside the atlas
u16  y
u16  w
u16  h
```

The atlas is 1bpp, row stride `(atlasW + 31) / 32 * 4` bytes, 1 = ink.

Drawing rule (see `font.c`):

```
pen baseline = (x, y)              // same convention as LibGDX BitmapFont#draw
ink top left  = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y)
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal bin2o replacement (the devkitPro container has bin2s but not bin2o).

Usage: bin2o.py <input.bin> <output.s> [symbol]

Emits an assembly stub that pulls the blob into .rodata and exports:

    _<sym>_start   .rodata address of the first byte
    _<sym>_end     .rodata address one past the last byte
    _<sym>_size    byte length

`<sym>` defaults to the input basename with dots turned into underscores.
"""
import os
import sys


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) < 3:
        sys.stderr.write(__doc__)
        return 2

    src, dst = argv[1], argv[2]
    sym = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else os.path.basename(src).replace(".", "_")

    with open(src, "rb") as fh:
        size = len(fh.read())
    inc = os.path.abspath(src)

    with open(dst, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\t.section .rodata\n")
        fh.write("\t.balign 4\n")
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_start:\n")
        fh.write('\t.incbin "{inc}"\n')
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_end\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_end:\n")
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_size\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_size:\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_end - _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("\t.global {sym}\n")
        fh.write("\t.section .rodata\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_data:\n")
        fh.write("\t.balign 4\n")
        fh.write("{sym}:\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_size\n")
        fh.write(f"\t.size {sym}, 8\n")

    hdr = os.path.splitext(src)[0].replace(".", "_") + ".h"
    with open(hdr, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("/* generated by nds/tools/bin2o.py - do not edit */\n")
        fh.write("#pragma once\n\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned char _{sym}_start[];\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned char _{sym}_end[];\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned int _{sym}_size;\n")
        fh.write(f"#define {sym} ((const void *)_{sym}_start)\n")
        fh.write(f"#define {sym}_SIZE ((unsigned)_{sym}_size)\n")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

360: static void texBlit(const Tex *t, int sx, int sy, int sw, int sh,
361:                     int dx, int dy, int dw, int dh, bool flipX) {
362: 	s32 stepX, stepY, fx, fy;
363: 	int skipX, skipY, mw, x, y;
364: 	bool masked, plain;
365: 	u32 alpha, inv;
366: 
367: 	if (t == NULL || t->px == NULL) return;
368: 	if (sw <= 0 || sh <= 0 || dw <= 0 || dh <= 0) return;
369: 	if (sx >= (int) t->w || sy >= (int) t->h || sx < 0 || sy < 0) return;
370: 	if (sx + sw > (int) t->w) sw = (int) t->w - sx;
371: 	if (sy + sh > (int) t->h) sh = (int) t->h - sy;
372: 	if (sw <= 0 || sh <= 0) return;
373: 
374: 	stepX = ((s32) sw << 16) / dw;
375: 	stepY = ((s32) sh << 16) / dh;
376: 
377: 	skipX = 0;
378: 	skipY = 0;
379: 	if (dx < 0) { skipX = -dx; dx = 0; dw -= skipX; }
380: 	if (dy < 0) { skipY = -dy; dy = 0; dh -= skipY; }
381: 	if (dw <= 0 || dh <= 0 || dx >= SCRW || dy >= SCRH) return;
382: 	if (dx + dw > SCRW) dw = SCRW - dx;
383: 	if (dy + dh > SCRH) dh = SCRH - dy;
384: 	if (dw <= 0 || dh <= 0) return;
385: 
386: 	/* Source start in 16.16 fixed point, already advanced past the clipped
387: 	   columns; flipping mirrors around the region's right edge. */
388: 	fx = ((s32) sx << 16) + (s32) skipX * stepX;
389: 	if (flipX) {
390: 		fx += (s32) (sw - 1) << 16;
391: 		stepX = -stepX;
392: 	}
393: 	fy = ((s32) sy << 16) + (s32) skipY * stepY;
394: 
395: 	masked = (t->mask != NULL);
396: 	mw = ((int) t->w + 31) >> 5;
397: 	alpha = gTintAlpha;
398: 	inv = 255u - alpha;
399: 	plain = tintPlain;
400: 
401: 	if (plain && alpha == 255u) {
402: 		for (y = 0; y < dh; y++) {
403: 			s32 ty = fy >> 16;
404: 			const u16 *prow;
405: 			const u32 *mrow;
406: 			u16 *dst;
407: 			s32 f = fx;
408: 			u32 wordIdx = 0xffffffffu, bits = 0;
409: 
410: 			if (ty < 0) ty = 0;
411: 			else if (ty > sh - 1) ty = sh - 1;
412: 			prow = t->px + (u32) ty * t->w;
413: 			mrow = masked ? t->mask + (u32) ty * mw : NULL;
414: 			dst = gfxFramebuffer + (u32) (dy + y) * SCRW + (u32) dx;
415: 
416: 			for (x = 0; x < dw; x++, dst++, f += stepX) {
417: 				u32 tx = (u32) (f >> 16);
418: 				u32 wi;
419: 
420: 				if (mrow != NULL) {
421: 					wi = tx >> 5;
422: 					if (wi != wordIdx) { wordIdx = wi; bits = mrow[wi]; }
423: 					if (((bits >> (tx & 31u)) & 1u) == 0u) continue;
424: 				}
425: 				*dst = prow[tx];
426: 			}
427: 			fy += stepY;
428: 		}
429: 	} else {
430: 		for (y = 0; y < dh; y++) {
431: 			s32 ty = fy >> 16;
432: 			const u16 *prow;
433: 			const u32 *mrow;
434: 			u16 *dst;
435: 			s32 f = fx;
436: 			u32 wordIdx = 0xffffffffu, bits = 0;
437: 
438: 			if (ty < 0) ty = 0;
439: 			else if (ty > sh - 1) ty = sh - 1;
440: 			prow = t->px + (u32) ty * t->w;
441: 			mrow = masked ? t->mask + (u32) ty * mw : NULL;
442: 			dst = gfxFramebuffer + (u32) (dy + y) * SCRW + (u32) dx;
443: 
444: 			for (x = 0; x < dw; x++, dst++, f += stepX) {
445: 				u32 tx = (u32) (f >> 16);
446: 				u32 wi, cov;
447: 				u16 c;
448: 
449: 				if (mrow != NULL) {
450: 					wi = tx >> 5;
451: 					if (wi != wordIdx) { wordIdx = wi; bits = mrow[wi]; }
452: 					cov = (bits >> (tx & 31u)) & 1u;
453: 					if (cov == 0u) continue;
454: 				}
455: 				c = applyTint(prow[tx]);
456: 				*dst = (alpha == 255u) ? c : blendPx(*dst, c, inv, alpha);
457: 			}
458: 			fy += stepY;
459: 		}
460: 	}

499: #define GFX_PI  3.14159265358979f
500: #define GFX_HPI 1.57079632679490f

502: /* libm is not linked on this target, so sin/cos come from a 5th order
503:    polynomial after a single quadrant reduction. Error is well under 1e-5. */
504: static void sincosApprox(float a, float *outS, float *outC) {
505: 	const float twoPi = GFX_PI * 2.0f;
506: 	float q = a * (1.0f / twoPi);
507: 	float t = (q - (float) (int) q) * twoPi;
508: 	float u, u2, s, c;
509: 
510: 	if (t < GFX_HPI)                 u = t;
511: 	else if (t < GFX_PI)             u = GFX_PI - t;
512: 	else if (t < GFX_PI + GFX_HPI)   u = t - GFX_PI;
513: 	else                             u = twoPi - t;
514: 
515: 	u2 = u * u;
516: 	s = u * (1.0f - u2 * (1.0f / 6.0f - u2 * (1.0f / 120.0f)));
517: 	c = 1.0f + u2 * (-0.5f + u2 * (1.0f / 24.0f - u2 * (1.0f / 720.0f)));
518: 
519: 	if (u == t)            { *outS = s;  *outC = c; }
520: 	else if (u == GFX_PI - t) { *outS = s;  *outC = -c; }
521: 	else if (u == t - GFX_PI) { *outS = -s; *outC = -c; }
522: 	else                   { *outS = -s; *outC = c; }
523: }

529: 	if (t == NULL || t->px == NULL || t->w == 0 || t->h == 0) return;

531: 	map(&mx, &my, cx, cy);
532: 	sz = mapLen(size);
533: 	if (sz < 1.0f) sz = 1.0f;
534: 
535: 	sincosApprox(angle, &sn, &cs);
536: 	invSz = 1.0f / sz;
537: 
538: 	dim = (int) sz;
539: 	if (dim < 1) dim = 1;
540: 	x0 = (int) mx - dim / 2;
541: 	y0 = (SCRH - 1 - (int) my) - dim / 2;
542: 	mw = ((int) t->w + 31) >> 5;

545: 		int row = y0 + y;
546: 		if ((unsigned) row >= SCRH) continue;

548: 		for (x = 0; x < dim; x++) {

566: 			if (txf < 0.0f || tyf < 0.0f) continue;

571: 			if (t->mask != NULL &&

573: 				continue;

575: 			c = tintPlain ? t->px[ty * t->w + tx]
576: 			              : applyTint(t->px[ty * t->w + tx]);

    ARMINC=$(arm-none-eabi-gcc -print-file-name=include)
    for f in "$@"; do
      echo "--- $f"
      arm-none-eabi-gcc -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter \

    done' bash "$@"
---
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Asset generation for the NDS build.
#
# Everything in here is produced on the host (inside the devkitPro container) and
# ends up as a raw blob in this directory, which the ARM9 Makefile turns into an
# object with tools/bin2o.py.
#
# The baker is plain python3 + stdlib: it decodes the PNGs and the TTF itself, so
# it does not need PIL, numpy, FreeType or mkbcfnt.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all clean verify fonts art

TOPDIR := $(realpath $(CURDIR)/..)
REPO   := $(realpath $(TOPDIR)/..)
PY     := python3

SRC_FONT := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf
SRC_ART  := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/art

GEN      := $(CURDIR)
BAKER    := $(TOPDIR)/tools/nds_bake.py
WHITELIST := $(GEN)/charset.txt

FONT_SIZES := 12,20,32

all: $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bitmap fonts: nds_bake.py reads the TTF directly (head/maxp/hhea/hmtx/cmap/
# loca/glyf, composite glyphs included), scan-converts the quadratic outlines at
# 4x4 supersampling, trims each glyph to its ink box and shelf packs the 1bpp
# atlas.  Output order is FONT_SMALL, FONT_BODY, FONT_TITLE.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$(GEN)/fonts.bin: $(SRC_FONT) $(WHITELIST) $(BAKER)
	@echo "baking fonts"
	@$(PY) $(BAKER) fonts \
		--font $(SRC_FONT) \
		--charset $(WHITELIST) \
		--sizes $(FONT_SIZES) \
		--out $(GEN)/fonts.bin

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sprites/tiles: every source PNG is area-averaged down to the rectangle the
# LibGDX build stretched it into, then split into an RGB555 colour plane and a
# 1bpp coverage plane.  A missing PNG only warns; the C side has a procedural
# fallback for it.
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
$(GEN)/art.bin: $(wildcard $(SRC_ART)/*.png) $(BAKER)
	@echo "baking art"
	@$(PY) $(BAKER) art \
		--src $(SRC_ART) \
		--out $(GEN)/art.bin

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
verify: all
	@$(PY) $(BAKER) verify $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin

clean:
	@rm -f $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin.h $(GEN)/fonts.bin.h
	@rm -rf $(GEN)/gen

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline asset baker for the Nintendo DS port of Elementia.

Reads the LibGDX source assets

    core/src/main/resources/art/*.png
    core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf

and writes the two blobs described in ``nds/FORMATS.md``:

    nds/gen/art.bin     ARTB  -- RGB555 colour plane + 1bpp coverage plane
    nds/gen/fonts.bin   FNTS  -- three baked 1bpp bitmap fonts

Both blobs are consumed by C code that this script must not have to know
about, so the layout is fixed here and never guessed at runtime.

Standard library only: no PIL, no numpy, no FreeType, no mkbcfnt.  PNG and
TrueType decoding are both implemented here from scratch, so the pipeline runs
under a plain ``python3`` on the host as well as inside the devkitPro
container.

-----
    nds_bake.py art    --src <dir> --out art.bin
    nds_bake.py fonts  --font <ttf> --charset charset.txt --out fonts.bin

    nds_bake.py verify art.bin fonts.bin
    nds_bake.py summary art.bin fonts.bin

asserts that every offset stays in bounds and prints the summary tables.

# 16.  x and y must be signed - the drawing rule places ink *above* the pen
# baseline - so the record is laid out as:
#   u32 codepoint, u16 advance, s16 x, s16 y, u16 w, u16 h, u16 reserved

Now I understand the font format completely:

**Font record (20 bytes)**: `u32 glyphCount, u8 lineHeight, u8 ascent, u8 reserved, u8 reserved, u32 atlasOff, u32 atlasW, u32 atlasH`

**Glyph (16 bytes)**: `u32 codepoint, u16 advance, s16 x, s16 y, u16 w, u16 h, u16 reserved`

- `x` = left bearing (floor of min x)
- `y` = top - box_top where box_top = lineHeight - ascent. So ink top-left in screen coords (bottom-left origin) = (penX + g.x, penY + lineHeight - ascent + g.y). Since g.y = top - (lineHeight - ascent), and top is the ink top in font units (y up), the ink top in screen coords = penY + lineHeight - ascent + top - lineHeight + ascent = penY + top. Makes sense: ink top is `top` pixels above the baseline.

**Atlas**: 1bpp, stride = ((atlasW+31)/32)*4 bytes, bit order: `plane_bit(x) = 1 << (x & 7)` — pixel x in byte x>>3, bit x&7. On little-endian DS, reading as u32 array: bit (x&31) of word (x>>5) = pixel x. Same as the art masks. 

**Drawing rule**: ink top left = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y) where (x,y) is the pen baseline in the current coordinate space (bottom-left origin). So in screen rows: row = SCRH-1 - (y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y), and the glyph is drawn w pixels wide, h pixels tall, going DOWN from that row (since ink extends downward from its top).

Wait, careful: ink top-left at sy = y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y. The glyph occupies rows from sy down to sy - h + 1 (in bottom-left coords, ink extends downward from the top). In screen rows (top = 0): topRow = SCRH-1-sy, and the glyph spans rows topRow .. topRow + h - 1.

def verify_fonts(blob):
    _check(len(blob) >= FONT_HEADER_SIZE, "fonts.bin shorter than its header")
    magic, count = struct.unpack_from("<IB", blob, 0)
    _check(magic == FONT_MAGIC,
           "fonts.bin magic is 0x%08X, want 0x%08X" % (magic, FONT_MAGIC))
    _check(1 <= count <= 255, "fonts.bin declares %d fonts" % count)
    table_end = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * count
    _check(len(blob) >= table_end, "fonts.bin table runs past end of file")

    pos = table_end
    rows = []
    for i in range(count):
        r = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * i
        raw = blob[r:r + FONT_RECORD_SIZE]
        # FORMATS.md declares u8 glyphCount; this baker emits u32 because the
        # required charset is larger than 255.  Accept both on read.
        glyph_count = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, 0)[0]
        if glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE > len(blob) - pos:
            glyph_count = raw[0]
        line_height, ascent = raw[4], raw[5]
        atlas_off, atlas_w, atlas_h = struct.unpack_from("<III", raw, 8)
        _check(0 < glyph_count, "font %d has no glyphs" % i)
        _check(0 < ascent <= line_height <= 255,
               "font %d has lineHeight=%d ascent=%d" % (i, line_height, ascent))
        _check(atlas_off % 4 == 0,
               "font %d atlasOff %d is not word aligned" % (i, atlas_off))
        _check(atlas_w % 32 == 0,
               "font %d atlas width %d is not a multiple of 32" % (i, atlas_w))
        stride = plane_stride(atlas_w)
        _check(atlas_off + stride * atlas_h <= len(blob),
               "font %d atlas runs past the end of the blob" % i)
        _check(pos + glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE <= len(blob),
               "font %d glyph table runs past the end of the blob" % i)

        prev_cp = -1
        inks = 0
        for g in range(glyph_count):
            cp, advance, x, y, w, h = struct.unpack_from(
                "<IHhhHH", blob, pos + g * GLYPH_SIZE)
            _check(cp > prev_cp,
                   "font %d glyph %d: codepoints are not sorted ascending" % (i, g))
            prev_cp = cp
            _check(advance < 4096,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X advance %d is implausible" % (i, cp, advance))
            if w == 0 or h == 0:
                _check(w == 0 and h == 0,
                       "font %d glyph U+%04X has a half-empty box" % (i, cp))
                continue
            inks += 1
            _check(x + w <= atlas_w,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: x+w=%d exceeds atlas width %d"
                   % (i, cp, x + w, atlas_w))
            _check(y + h <= atlas_h,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: y+h=%d exceeds atlas height %d"
                   % (i, cp, y + h, atlas_h))
            _check((x + w + 7) // 8 <= stride,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X crosses the row stride" % (i, cp))
            _check(-line_height <= y + line_height - ascent - h <= line_height,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X box is implausibly far from the baseline"
                   % (i, cp))
            has_ink = False
            for row_i in range(h):
                base = atlas_off + (y + row_i) * stride
                for c in range(w):
                    if (blob[base + ((x + c) >> 3)] >> ((x + c) & 7)) & 1:
                        has_ink = True
                        break
                if has_ink:
                    break
            _check(has_ink,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X has a %dx%d box containing no ink"
                   % (i, cp, w, h))
        pos += glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE
        rows.append((i, glyph_count, inks, atlas_w, atlas_h, atlas_off,
                     stride * atlas_h, line_height, ascent))

    _check(pos <= len(blob), "font glyph tables overrun the blob")
    print("fonts.bin  OK   fonts=%d  record=%dB  glyph tables end at %d/%dB"
          % (count, FONT_RECORD_SIZE, pos, len(blob)))
    print()
    names = ["FONT_SMALL", "FONT_BODY", "FONT_TITLE"]
    print("  %-4s %-11s %7s %7s %-11s %7s %7s %7s %10s"
          % ("idx", "enum", "glyphs", "ink", "atlas", "lineH", "ascent",
             "atlasOff", "bytes"))
    for (i, gc, inks, aw, ah, ao, ab, lh, asc) in rows:
        print("  %-4d %-11s %7d %7d %4dx%-6d %7d %7d %7d %10d"
              % (i, names[i] if i < 3 else "?", gc, inks, aw, ah, lh, asc, ao, ab))
    print()
    return rows

def verify_fonts(blob):
    _check(len(blob) >= FONT_HEADER_SIZE, "fonts.bin shorter than its header")
    magic, count = struct.unpack_from("<IB", blob, 0)
    _check(magic == FONT_MAGIC,
           "fonts.bin magic is 0x%08X, want 0x%08X" % (magic, FONT_MAGIC))
    _check(1 <= count <= 255, "fonts.bin declares %d fonts" % count)
    table_end = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * count
    _check(len(blob) >= table_end, "fonts.bin table runs past end of file")

    pos = table_end
    rows = []
    for i in range(count):
        r = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * i
        raw = blob[r:r + FONT_RECORD_SIZE]
        # FORMATS.md declares u8 glyphCount; this baker emits u32 because the
        # required charset is larger than 255.  Accept both on read.
        glyph_count = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, 0)[0]
        if glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE > len(blob) - pos:
            glyph_count = raw[0]
        line_height, ascent = raw[4], raw[5]
        atlas_off, atlas_w, atlas_h = struct.unpack_from("<III", raw, 8)
        _check(0 < glyph_count, "font %d has no glyphs" % i)
        _check(0 < ascent <= line_height <= 255,
               "font %d has lineHeight=%d ascent=%d" % (i, line_height, ascent))
        _check(atlas_off % 4 == 0,
               "font %d atlasOff %d is not word aligned" % (i, atlas_off))
        _check(atlas_w % 32 == 0,
               "font %d atlas width %d is not a multiple of 32" % (i, atlas_w))
        stride = plane_stride(atlas_w)
        _check(atlas_off + stride * atlas_h <= len(blob),
               "font %d atlas runs past the end of the blob" % i)
        _check(pos + glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE <= len(blob),
               "font %d glyph table runs past the end of the blob" % i)

        prev_cp = -1
        inks = 0
        for g in range(glyph_count):
            cp, advance, x, y, w, h = struct.unpack_from(
                "<IHhhHH", blob, pos + g * GLYPH_SIZE)
            _check(cp > prev_cp,
                   "font %d glyph %d: codepoints are not sorted ascending" % (i, g))
            prev_cp = cp
            _check(advance < 4096,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X advance %d is implausible" % (i, cp, advance))
            if w == 0 or h == 0:
                _check(w == 0 and h == 0,
                       "font %d glyph U+%04X has a half-empty box" % (i, cp))
                continue
            inks += 1
            _check(x + w <= atlas_w,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: x+w=%d exceeds atlas width %d"
                   % (i, cp, x + w, atlas_w))
            _check(y + h <= atlas_h,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: y+h=%d exceeds atlas height %d"
                   % (i, cp, y + h, atlas_h))
            _check((x + w + 7) // 8 <= stride,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X crosses the row stride" % (i, cp))
            _check(-line_height <= y + line_height - ascent - h <= line_height,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X box is implausibly far from the baseline"
                   % (i, cp))
            has_ink = False
            for row_i in range(h):
                base = atlas_off + (y + row_i) * stride
                for c in range(w):
                    if (blob[base + ((x + c) >> 3)] >> ((x + c) & 7)) & 1:
                        has_ink = True
                        break
                if has_ink:
                    break
            _check(has_ink,
                   "font %d glyph U+%04X has a %dx%d box containing no ink"
                   % (i, cp, w, h))
        pos += glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE
        rows.append((i, glyph_count, inks, atlas_w, atlas_h, atlas_off,
                     stride * atlas_h, line_height, ascent))

    _check(pos <= len(blob), "font glyph tables overrun the blob")
    print("fonts.bin  OK   fonts=%d  record=%dB  glyph tables end at %d/%dB"
          % (count, FONT_RECORD_SIZE, pos, len(blob)))
    print()
    names = ["FONT_SMALL", "FONT_BODY", "FONT_TITLE"]
    print("  %-4s %-11s %7s %7s %-11s %7s %7s %7s %10s"
          % ("idx", "enum", "glyphs", "ink", "atlas", "lineH", "ascent",
             "atlasOff", "bytes"))
    for (i, gc, inks, aw, ah, ao, ab, lh, asc) in rows:
        print("  %-4d %-11s %7d %7d %4dx%-6d %7d %7d %7d %10d"
              % (i, names[i] if i < 3 else "?", gc, inks, aw, ah, lh, asc, ao, ab))
    print()
    return rows


# ===========================================================================
# CLI
# ===========================================================================

def cmd_art(args):
    rows, size = bake_art(args.src, args.out)
    print("art.bin   %d textures, %d bytes -> %s" % (len(rows), size, args.out))
    print()
    print("  %-10s %5s %5s %9s" % ("texture", "w", "h", "opaque"))
    for (name, w, h, o, t) in rows:
        print("  %-10s %5d %5d %8.1f%%" % (name, w, h, 100.0 * o / t))
    print()
    return 0


def cmd_fonts(args):
    sizes = tuple(int(s) for s in args.sizes.split(",") if s.strip())
    stats, size = bake_fonts(args.font, args.charset, args.out, sizes,
                             glyph_count_bits=args.glyph_count_bits)

          % ("size", "glyphs", "ink", "atlas", "bytes", "lineH", "ascent"))
    for st in stats:
        print("  %-5d %7d %7d %5dx%-5d %8d %7d %7d"
              % (st["size"], st["glyphs"], st["ink"], st["atlas_w"],
                 st["atlas_h"], st["atlas_bytes"], st["line_height"],
                 st["ascent"]))

Now I have the full picture of the fonts.bin format:

**Header (8 bytes)**: `u32 magic='FNTS', u8 count=3, u8 reserved[3]`

**Font records (20 bytes each)**: `u32 glyphCount, u8 lineHeight, u8 ascent, u8 reserved, u8 reserved, u32 atlasOff, u32 atlasW, u32 atlasH`

**Glyph table (16 bytes per glyph, sorted ascending by codepoint)**: `u32 codepoint, u16 advance, s16 x, s16 y, u16 w, u16 h, u16 reserved`

**Atlas**: 1bpp, stride = ((atlasW+31)/32)*4, pixel (x,y) at bit (x&7) of byte (x>>3) + y*stride. On DS (little endian), reading the atlas as u32 array: pixel x = bit (x&31) of word (x>>5).

Note the glyph table location: `table_end = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * count = 8 + 60 = 68`. Glyphs for all fonts are stored contiguously after the records, in font order. Each font's glyphCount tells where its glyphs start/end. Atlas data follows the glyph tables.

Note the drawing rule:
```
pen baseline = (x, y)              // bottom-left origin
ink top left  = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y)
```

So in screen rows (row 0 at top): topRow = SCRH-1-(y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y). The glyph extends from topRow down to topRow+h-1 (inclusive), and from x+g.x to x+g.x+w-1.

Wait, but the glyph y in the record: `y = top - box_top` where `box_top = lineHeight - ascent`. So ink top in screen coords = y_pen + lineHeight - ascent + g.y = y_pen + lineHeight - ascent + top - lineHeight + ascent = y_pen + top. Since top is the ink top measured from baseline in font units (y up), ink top is `top` pixels above the baseline. Correct.

And the glyph extends DOWNWARD from the ink top by h pixels: bottom of ink = y_pen + top - h. Since h = top - floor(lo_y) and lo_y ≤ 0 typically (descenders go below baseline), bottom ≤ y_pen. Good.

So for drawing with the gfx transform: I can use gfxTex-like blitting, or I can blit directly. The font API is separate from gfx (textDraw draws into the same framebuffer — main.c uses both gfx and font; the comment in gfx.c says "font.c blits glyphs straight into this buffer").

Let me check how textDraw should handle the transform. The task says:

* `textDraw(x, y, font, utf8)` - draws with the pen baseline at (x, y) (LibGDX BitmapFont convention, the caller passes the baseline y). Returns the total advance in SCREEN pixels (float for API compatibility, but the value is integral).

So textDraw returns advance in SCREEN pixels. If we're in world space, the advance should be scaled? Hmm — "Returns the total advance in SCREEN pixels". The x,y are in the current transform space. I think the cleanest approach: textDraw should work in the current transform space (like all other draw calls), mapping coordinates through the same `map` function, and return the advance mapped to screen pixels (i.e., scaled by 1/WORLD_SCALE if in world space). Actually wait — "the value is integral" — so in screen space it's just the sum of advances. In world space... advance * 0.5 would be fractional. Hmm, but the task says the value is integral. Let me think about what the caller does with the return value: probably positions the next piece of text. If textDraw is called in world space and returns screen pixels, the caller adding it to a world-space x would be wrong. 

Let me look at how the game uses textDraw. The game code isn't written yet (only main.c exists, which references game.c, titleScreen.c, etc. that don't exist yet — those are separate tasks). So I need to make a sensible choice.

Simplest consistent choice: textDraw interprets (x,y) in the current transform space (mapped like every other draw call), and returns the advance in the SAME space as x (i.e., world units if in world space). But the task explicitly says "Returns the total advance in SCREEN pixels (float for API compatibility, but the value is integral)".

Hmm, "the value is integral" suggests that even in world space it's integral? That can't be if scaled by 0.5. Unless... the game only ever draws text in screen space (HUD, dialogue, banners — all UI). The task says screen space is for "HUD, dialogue, touch controls". So text is drawn in screen space, and the return is integral screen pixels. 

I'll implement: textDraw maps (x,y) through the current transform (consistent with everything else), and returns the advance in screen pixels (scaled if in world space). In practice it's used in screen space. Actually, let me reconsider — to be safe and consistent: return value = mapped advance in screen pixels. If gWorld, advance_screen = advance / WORLD_SCALE. That matches "SCREEN pixels" and is integral in screen space.

Hmm wait, but actually, should textDraw respect the world transform at all? The dialogue box is screen space. The HUD is screen space. I'll respect the transform like all other draws — that's the consistent behavior, and returning screen-pixel advance matches the spec.

Actually, let me reconsider once more. If textDraw respects the world transform, then mapping the pen position through map() gives screen pixel position, and the glyph blit happens in screen space directly. The advance in screen pixels = sum(glyph.advance) / (gWorld ? WORLD_SCALE : 1). I'll do that.

Now — how does textDraw draw glyphs? Options:
1. Blit directly into gfxFramebuffer (requires access to the framebuffer — gfx.c exports `gfxFramebuffer` symbol; font.c can declare `extern u16 gfxFramebuffer[]`).
2. Use a mask-based blit: the glyph atlas is 1bpp; I can build a Tex-like blit from the mask, or just write a small span blitter in font.c.

The cleanest: font.c declares `extern u16 gfxFramebuffer[SCRW*SCRH];` (the comment in gfx.c already says "font.c blits glyphs straight into this buffer; gfx.h exposes no accessor and must not change, so the symbol is exported and declared there"). So font.c must use the exported symbol. 

For each glyph row, I need to set pixels where mask bit is 1, with tint applied and alpha blended. The glyph color comes from fontSetTint(u16, u8).

Blitting approach per glyph:
- Compute screen position of ink top-left: map (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y) → screen (sx, sy) in bottom-left; topRow = SCRH-1-sy.
- For each row r in 0..h-1: for each col c in 0..w-1: if mask bit set, blend tint color into fb[topRow + r][sx + c].

To make it fast, iterate over set bits per word: load u32 word, for each set bit position, plot. With tint color and alpha. Since glyphs are small, even a per-pixel loop over w*h is fine (2500 glyphs per frame max would be too slow, but text is maybe 100-300 glyphs; still, per-pixel bit testing is w*h/8... fine). But let me do word-wise for cleanliness: for each row, walk words, skip zero words, then for each set bit plot. That's efficient and simple.

Clipping: glyphs near edges need clipping. I'll clip the dest rect to the screen before iterating.

Now the cache: "a 512-entry u16 table indexed by (cp & 0x1FF) is plenty, fall back to a binary search otherwise."

So: per font, `u16 cache[512]` where cache[cp & 0x1FF] = index+1 into the glyph array (0 = miss), and if the entry at that index doesn't match cp, fall back to binary search. Wait — direct-mapped cache with 512 entries: cache[cp & 0x1FF] stores glyph index+1; if glyphs[idx].codepoint != cp, do binary search. Since multiple codepoints can alias to the same slot, binary search fallback handles it.

Hmm, but binary search fallback for EVERY collision would be slow for the common case... Actually the cache slot will often hold a different codepoint than requested (collisions), and then binary search runs. That's fine — binary search over ~361 entries is ~9 iterations, cheap.

Actually, better: make cache store the glyph index only when... no, keep it simple per spec: 512-entry u16 direct-mapped cache + binary search fallback. Per font.

Wait, "Build per-font a sorted array of glyphs plus a direct-mapped cache for codepoints". So per font: glyph array (copied from ROM? The glyph array in ROM is read-only and sorted; I can point directly at the ROM data since ARM9 ROM is directly readable — no need to copy. Only the atlas gets copied to RAM). Actually the spec says "copy the atlas bitmaps into a static buffer" — only the atlas. The glyph table can stay in ROM (const pointer). 

But the cache must be built per font at fontInit: 512 u16 entries initialized to 0, then for each glyph index i: cache[cp & 0x1FF] = i+1 (last writer wins — any occupant is fine as long as we verify codepoint match and fall back).

Binary search: standard, over the glyph array sorted by codepoint.

UTF-8 decode: standard:
- 0xxxxxxx → 1 byte
- 110xxxxx → 2 bytes
- 1110xxxx → 3 bytes
- 11110xxx → 4 bytes

Validate continuation bytes (10xxxxxx). Decode to codepoint. If malformed, skip the byte (treat as unknown → advance by average advance).

Unknown codepoints: "render as nothing and advance by the font's average advance". Average advance — precompute per font at init: sum of advances / count (integer). I'll precompute in fontInit and store.

Newlines: '\n' → advance 0, y -= lineHeight. In textDraw: when decoding cp == '\n', reset pen to start x? Wait — "Newlines inside the string must advance to the next line (advance = 0, y -= lineHeight)". Hmm, advance = 0 — but does the pen x reset to the original x? In LibGDX BitmapFont, newline moves to the next line at the same x origin. The spec says "advance = 0, y -= lineHeight" — I think it means the newline itself contributes 0 to the returned width, and the pen moves to the next line. For multi-line text to render correctly, the pen x must return to the starting x after a newline. Let me think about what the caller expects: textWidth returns total advance — for multi-line, width should probably be the max line width? Or the sum including newlines (0 advance)? 

Hmm. The spec: "Newlines inside the string must advance to the next line (advance = 0, y -= lineHeight). The dialogue box relies on this."

I'll implement: in textDraw, on '\n': penX = startX (reset to origin), penY -= lineHeight, advance contribution 0. Return value: sum of advances of all chars (newline contributes 0). In textWidth: same logic — width = total advance sum (newlines add 0). That matches "advance = 0".

Hmm, but should textWidth return max line width instead? The spec says newlines advance by 0, so the total advance is the sum. I'll go with sum. That's the literal reading.

textHeight(font): returns lineHeight of the font (int). Probably. "textHeight(font)" — the height of one line. I'll return lineHeight.

Now, where does textDraw get the glyphs? It needs per-font: glyph array pointer, glyph count, lineHeight, ascent, atlas pointer (copied to RAM), cache. I'll build a struct array `fonts[FONT_COUNT]` in font.c.

Now the tint: fontSetTint(u16 color, u8 alpha). Applied when drawing glyphs: blend color into dst with alpha. If alpha == 255, write directly. The tint is per... global (not per font). Store in static vars.

Now the glyph blit with clipping. Let me write a helper:

```c
static void blitGlyph(const Font *f, const Glyph *g, int dx, int dy) {
    // (dx, dy) = screen top-left of ink box in SCREEN ROW coords (row 0 = top)
    int row, col;
    const u8 *atlas = f->atlas;
    int stride = f->stride;
    int x0 = dx, y0 = dy;
    int w = g->w, h = g->h;
    // clip
    if (x0 < 0) { w += x0; x0 = 0; }  // careful: also need to advance the source column
    ...
}
```

Wait, clipping left requires adjusting the source x too. Let me handle it: source sx = g->x (atlas column), dest dx. If dx < 0: sx += -dx, w -= -dx, dx = 0. If dx + w > SCRW: w = SCRW - dx. Same for rows: source sy = g->y + row... source row base = g->y (atlas row of glyph top), dest topRow. If topRow < 0: skip rows. If topRow + h > SCRH: h = SCRH - topRow.

Then for each dest row r (0..h-1), atlas row = g->y + r, for each set bit in the atlas row range [sx, sx+w): plot at (dx + (c - sx), topRow + r).

Word-wise iteration: the atlas row starts at byte offset (g->y + r)*stride + (sx >> 3). The bits for columns [sx, sx+w) span words [(sx)>>5, (sx+w-1)>>5]. For each word, mask off bits below sx and above sx+w-1, then iterate set bits.

Simpler per-pixel approach: for r in rows: const u32 *rowp = (const u32*)(atlas + (g->y+r)*stride); for c in 0..w-1: bit index = sx + c; if (rowp[(sx+c)>>5] >> ((sx+c)&31)) & 1 → plot. With w,h small (max ~40px for title font), per-pixel is at most ~1600 bit tests per glyph — fine for a few hundred glyphs. But word-skip is nicer. Let me do a middle ground: iterate words, skip empty, then bits. It's not much more code.

Actually, let me keep it simple and robust: per-pixel loop but with early row clipping. Text volume is low (HUD + dialogue ≈ 50-150 glyphs). Fine.

Hmm, but wait — the title font is 32pt, glyphs up to ~40x40 = 1600 px per glyph. Title screen has maybe 10 glyphs = 16k px. Fine.

Now, about mapping through the transform: textDraw receives (x, y) in the current space. I need the same map() helper. I'll duplicate a small local map in font.c (can't call static map from gfx.c). Fine — font.c can have its own static map using... hmm, but the transform state (gWorld, gCamX, gCamY) lives in gfx.c as statics. 

Options:
1. Export accessor functions from gfx.c... but I shouldn't add non-declared functions? The task says implement everything declared in gfx.h; adding extra exported functions is allowed (it says "NEVER edit anything in nds/include/", but gfx.c is mine to write). But cleaner to keep the API surface minimal.
2. In font.c, re-derive the transform: font.c can't see gWorld/gCamX/gCamY. 

Hmm. How important is transform support for text? The spec says textDraw takes (x,y) baseline and returns SCREEN pixel advance. The mention of "SCREEN pixels" for the return suggests text is expected to be drawn in screen space. But to be consistent, respecting the world transform would be nice.

I could export the transform state from gfx.c as extern globals (e.g., `extern bool gfxWorld; extern float gfxCamX, gfxCamY;`) defined in gfx.c. That's clean enough and doesn't touch headers. Or export a helper `void gfxMap(float x, float y, float *sx, float *sy);` from gfx.c. Adding an extra non-header function to gfx.c is fine.

```c
extern bool gfxWorldOn;
extern float gfxCamX, gfxCamY;
```
and use them in font.c with the same map math. Or provide `void gfxMap(float x, float y, float *sx, float *sy);` in gfx.c (not in the header, just declared extern in font.c). I'll go with a function — cleaner encapsulation. Since font.c needs it, and both are my files, I'll add `void gfxMap(float x, float y, float *sx, float *sy);` to gfx.c (implementation of map) and declare it extern in font.c.

Wait, but "No undefined symbols beyond the two blob symbols above" — that refers to the final link; gfxMap is defined in gfx.c, so it's defined. Fine.

Alternatively, keep font.c transform-free: assume screen space for text. But the world renderer... no, text is UI only. Hmm, but consistency: if someone draws text in world space it would break. The safe choice: support the transform via gfxMap export. I'll do that.

Now — the pen position for multi-line: on newline, penX resets to the ORIGINAL x passed to textDraw (so lines stack vertically at the same left edge). penY -= lineHeight.

Return value: total advance in screen pixels = accumulated pen movement. For screen space: sum of advances. In world space: the advance in world units mapped to screen? #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the Nintendo DS ROM (nds/elementia.nds) inside the official devkitPro
# container, so no local devkitARM install is required.
#
#   ./nds/build.sh            build the ROM
#   ./nds/build.sh clean      remove build output
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
IMAGE="${DEVKITPRO_IMAGE:-devkitpro/devkitarm:latest}"
ARTIFACTS="${ELEMENTIA_ARTIFACTS:-/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp}"

if ! docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo ">> pulling $IMAGE"
	docker pull "$IMAGE"
fi

run() {
	docker run --rm \
		-u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
		-e HOME=/tmp \
		-e DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro \
		-e DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM \
		-v "$REPO:/work" \
		-v "$ARTIFACTS:/out" \
		-w /work/nds \
		"$IMAGE" \
		bash -c 'source /opt/devkitpro/devkitarm.sh && exec "$@"' bash "$@"
}

case "${1:-all}" in
	clean)
		run make clean
		;;
	assets)
		run make -C gen
		;;
	*)
		shift 2>/dev/null || true
		run make "$@"
		cp -f "$HERE/elementia.nds" "$ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
		echo ">> $ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
		;;
esac

display.text:
# Elementia

A compact anime-style Metroidvania for Android, built with [LibGDX](https://libgdx.com/).
Play as the heroine **Aria**, explore four elemental zones, unlock abilities and
defeat the Ice Lion.

## Zones & progression

| Area       | Theme    | Gating ability            |
|------------|----------|---------------------------|
| Meadow      | grass/sky | DASH (start)             |
| Cavern      | stone     | PYRO (chest) → burns vine |
| Frost Shrine| ice/snow  | CRYO (chest) → melts frost |
| Sanctum     | boss arena| DOUBLE_JUMP + BURST (boss)|

Combos, dash, elemental skill shots and reactions (vaporize ×1.6, melt ×2,
swirl ×1.3) are all in. One-way platforms, checkpoints (waypoint statues),
dialogue NPCs and auto-save included.

## Modules

- `core`    – game logic + art (Pollinations AI sprites/tiles optional,
  procedural fallback, see `tools/refresh_assets.py`)
- `desktop` – desktop backend for local testing
- `android` – Android application module
- `test`    – headless smoke tests

## Requirements

- JDK 17
- Android SDK (compileSdk 34, build-tools 35.0.0, minSdk 24)

## Build

```bash
# compile + headless test
./gradlew core:compileJava :test:run

# desktop launcher
./gradlew :desktop:run

# Android debug APK
./gradlew :android:assembleDebug
# output: android/build/outputs/apk/debug/android-debug.apk
```

> If the project ships `local.properties` it already contains your SDK path;
> otherwise create it with `sdk.dir=/path/to/android-sdk`.

## Controls

| Desktop                     | Touch (Android)             |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| WASD/arrows move            | Left/right on-screen pad    |
| SPACE jump (×2)             | Jump/skill buttons          |
| J attack (3-hit)            | Attack button               |
| K elemental skill           | Element switch via HUD      |
| L dash                      | Dash button                 |

The on-screen pad and buttons are visible on every platform (mouse-clickable on
desktop), and the in-game hints adjust to the platform automatically.

## Art assets

Environment tiles, characters and props are drawn by Pollinations AI
(`tools/refresh_assets.py` regenerates them into `core/src/main/resources/art/`)
and smoothed at render time. Any asset that is missing or failed to generate
cleanly falls back to the built-in procedural cel-shaded art, so the game
always runs offline.

## Render modes & audio

- **Visual modes** — cycle with `P` or the round **MODE** button (top right):
  `2D` (flat, no parallax) → `2.5D` (default: parallax ridges + zone fog +
  vignette) → `3D` (deeper parallax, zoomed-out pseudoperspective, handheld sway).
  The active mode is shown in the top-center HUD badge.
- **Sound & music** — all audio is synthesized at first launch (no asset files):
  music loops in the game screen, and one-shot effects cover jump, double-jump,
  dash, slash, melee/projectile hits, enemy death, skill shots, burst nova,
  chests, waypoints, burning/melting gates, NPC chatter, boss roar and victory.
  WAV files are cached under `audio/` in the local storage. On headless runs all
  audio calls are no-ops.

### 1.1 `core/Config.java` (40 LOC) — **PURE JAVA, 0 libGDX**
Every tuning constant in the game. Fully portable; becomes a `config.h`.

```
VIEW_W 960f  VIEW_H 540f            // world-space viewport (16:9)
GRAVITY 2100f  TILE 32f  MAX_FALL 1200f
PLAYER_W 22f  PLAYER_H 34f
MOVE_SPEED 260f  ACCEL 1800f  GROUND_DECEL 2600f  AIR_DECEL 900f
JUMP_VEL 700f  JUMP_CUT 0.45f  COYOTE_TIME 0.1f  JUMP_BUFFER 0.12f
DASH_SPEED 720f  DASH_TIME 0.16f  DASH_CD 0.5f
COMBO_WINDOW 0.5f  COMBAT_KNOCKBACK 220f  MAX_HP 100f  MAX_BURST 100f
SKILL_CD 1.4f  STATUS_DURATION 4f
CAM_LERP 4.5f   CAM_LOOKAHEAD 60f   <-- DEAD: 0 references in code
```

**Derived physics numbers (useful for the port):**
- Single-jump apex height = `JUMP_VEL²/(2·GRAVITY)` = **116.7 px = 3.65 tiles**; airtime ≈ **0.667 s**
- Double jump uses `JUMP_VEL*0.88 = 616` → **90.3 px = 2.82 tiles**
- Dash distance = `720 * 0.16` = **115.2 px = 3.6 tiles**
- Run speed = **260 px/s = 8.125 tiles/s**; ~5.4 tiles of horizontal travel per full jump arc
- Max fall = 1200 px/s = 37.5 tiles/s

### 1.5 `core/Art.java` (201 LOC) — **PORTABLE (Pixmap-only)**
Pure pixel-painting primitives writing into a `Pixmap` (RGBA8888). Imports `Color` but **never uses it** (dead import). Every method is trivially reimplementable against a `u16*` framebuffer:

`set, fillRect, outlineRect, fillCircle, outlineCircle, fillEllipse, outlineEllipse, fillTriangle (+inTri/sign), fillPoly (even-odd scanline), fillSector (angle sweep), vGrad, glow (radial, alpha-blended), blend (source-over), noise (deterministic integer hash), shade, mix, rgb, rgba, newPix`.
`blend()` at line 185 uses integer `/255` (non-normalized) — port verbatim to keep pixel-identical output.

### 1.6 `core/Assets.java` (960 LOC) — **PORTABLE if baked offline**
Builds **every** texture at boot. Two paths per asset:
- `aiTex(name)` (line 96): loads `art/<name>.png` via `Gdx.files.internal` if it exists, sets **`TextureFilter.Linear/Linear`**; returns `null` on any failure.
- `or(ai, fallback)` (line 109): AI texture if present, else a procedurally `Pixmap`-painted one via `makeTex()` which sets **`TextureFilter.Nearest/Nearest`**.

→ **Filter is a mixed bag: AI art = Linear (smoothed), procedural = Nearest.** On NDS you must pick one; use 2× nearest-in-a-256px-tile setup.

### 1.10 `core/GameScreen.java` (220 LOC) — **libGDX-bound (the only screen/controller)**
Fields: `world, batch (SpriteBatch), cam (OrthographicCamera 960×540), hud, dlg, touch, InputState state, onMobile, dieMsg, dialogOpen, camX, camY, Preferences prefs ("elementia-save"), inited`.

`show()` (39–64): opens `Gdx.app.getPreferences("elementia-save")`; on re-entry re-attaches input + music and **keeps the existing `world`**; on first entry builds `World`, loads `prefs.getString("save01","")`, creates `SpriteBatch`, `OrthographicCamera`, `Hud`, `DialogueBox`, `TouchControls`, `Gdx.input.setInputProcessor(touch)`, `Sfx.startMusic()`.

`render(float dt)` (72–164) order — **exact frame loop:**
1. `glClearColor(0,0,0,1)` + `glClear`
2. **Win-and-restart check first:** `world.gameWon && (ENTER | justTouched() | touch.tapConsumed)` → new `GameScreen` (full restart)
3. `dt = min(dt, 0.05f)` (20 FPS floor)
4. desktop: `updateKbd()`; then always `touch.update()`
5. intro dialogue if `world.introPending`
6. `world.update(state, dt)` **or** `dlg.update(dt)` when a dialog is open (world frozen)
7. if `world.saveDirty` → `prefs.putString("save01", world.save()); prefs.flush();`
8. dialog open/close latch; NPC dialogue pickup from `world.pendingNpc`
9. advance dialogue (`Z`/`ENTER`/`justTouched()`/`tapConsumed`), `touch.resetTap()`
10. `dieMsg` countdown when `!player.alive`
11. `state.reset()` (clears edge flags)
12. `cam.update()`
13. `batch.setProjectionMatrix(cam.combined); batch.begin(); world.render(batch, shakeX+camX, shakeY+camX…); batch.end();`
14. `hud.render(world, world.time, onMobile)` (own batch/camera)
15. `touch.render()` unless dialogue open (own batch/camera)
16. `dlg.render(world.time)` (own batch/camera)
17. if `dieMsg>0`: `hudDrawDeath()` — `"ТЫ ПАЛА!"` (54 px, red) + `"Возвращение к точке сохранения..."` (26 px)

`updateCamera(dt)` (166–180) — **manual camera; the `OrthographicCamera` is pinned at screen centre and the world is offset by hand in `render()`**:
```java
look = clamp(p.vx * 0.14f, -80f, 80f);          // Config.CAM_LOOKAHEAD (60f) is UNUSED
tx = p.x + p.w/2 + look - VIEW_W/2;
ty = p.y + p.h/2 - VIEW_H/2;
t  = min(1, dt * Config.CAM_LERP);              // 4.5
camX = lerp(camX, tx, t);  camY = lerp(camY, ty, t);
camX = clamp(camX, 0, 150*32 - 960);           // [0, 3840]
camY = clamp(camY, 0, max(0, 46*32 - 540));     // [0, 932]
cam.position.set(480, 270, 0);
```
Screen shake is added at draw time: `shX = world.getShakeX() + camX` where `getShakeX/Y()` returns `rand(-amt, +amt)` while `shakeTimer > 0`.

`updateKbd()` (182–190): `A/LEFT`, `D/RIGHT`, `SPACE`(held + just), `J`=attack, `K`=skill, `L`=dash.

**Camera clamp consequence:** world is **4800 × 1472 px**; a 960×540 window means the camera y can never go below 932 and never above 0 — so the top 44 rows and the deep volcano rows are only partly reachable. On a 256×192 DS screen the natural mapping is **256×144** (scale 0.2667 of 960×540) letterboxed 24 px top/bottom; that exactly preserves the same framing.

`resize(w,h)` (204–211): sets `cam.viewportWidth/Height` back to 960/540 (so **the game camera never adapts to aspect** — black bars will appear on non-16:9), and forwards to `hud/touch/dlg.resize(w,h)` which use **real device pixels**.

### 1.12 `world/Player.java` (139 LOC) — **PURE (2 libGDX calls)**
Only uses `MathUtils.clamp(v,lo,hi)` (trivially portable) and a `Vector2 atkCenter` (→ `struct {float x,y;}`).

**Fields:** `EnumSet<Ability> abilities` (starts `{DASH}`), `Element activeElement=null`, `skillCd`, `burstGauge`, `burstReady`, `burstPower=100`, `int comboStep`, `comboWindow`, `attackTimer`, `atkCenter`, `atkRadius=18`, `atkHitApplied`, `coyote`, `jumpBuffer`, `dashTimer`, `dashCd`, `jumpsUsed`, `invuln`.
**Dead fields:** `animTimer` (never incremented → always 0), `atkDuration`, `summonTimer`, `holdDown`, `slideTimer`, `prevFacing`.

`enum State { IDLE, RUN, JUMP, FALL, DASH, ATTACK, HURT, DEAD }`.

**`moveAndCollide(world, dt)` (78–123)** — swept in fixed **4 px sub-steps**:
- Horizontal: advance `dx = clamp(remaining, ±4)`; probe 4 corners at `y+2` and `y+h-2` against `solidAt`; on hit → undo, `vx=0`, break.
- Vertical: `dy` in 4 px steps; falling probes `solidAt` **and** `platformAt` at `x+2` and `x+w-2` (one-way platforms); rising probes only `solidAt` at `y+h`. On landing, snaps `y = max(groundTopAt(x+2, y-1), groundTopAt(x+w-2, y-1))`.
- `grounded` recomputed from `solidAt(x+1, y-2) || solidAt(x+w-1, y-2) || platformAt(x+w/2, y-2)`; `if (grounded) jumpsUsed = 0`.

`updateState()` (130–138): ATTACK/DASH short-circuits; else `!grounded → (vy>40 ? JUMP : FALL)`, `|vx|>40 → RUN`, else IDLE.

Abilities: `canDoubleJump() = has(DOUBLE_JUMP) && jumpsUsed == 1`; `unlock(BURST)` refills `burstGauge` to 100.

### 1.13 `world/Enemy.java` (216 LOC) — **logic pure, 32 LOC libGDX render**
`enum Kind { SLIME, WISP, GOLEM }`.

| Kind | AABB | HP | contactDmg | Draw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SLIME | 44×38 | 26 | 12 | `slimeFrames[(int)(anim*2)%4]`, 1 draw |
| WISP | 16×14 | 12 | 10 | `wispReg` 16×14, 1 draw |
| GOLEM | 48×44 | 160 | 20 | `golemReg` 48×44, **2 draws** when angered-flashing |

Fields: `kind, element, timer, hopTimer, sx0/sx1 (patrol bounds), homeX/homeY, anim, angered, contactDmg, scoreGems`.
AI:
- **SLIME**: if `|dx|<220 && |dy|<120` and `timer<=0` → `timer=1.4`, hop `vx=±(110+rand*60)`, `vy=260+rand*130`; else `vx*=0.6`.
- **WISP**: if `dist<260` steer toward player at 70 px/s + `sin(anim*5)*20`; else drift `sin(anim*2)*15`. No gravity, clamped to patrol bounds.
- **GOLEM**: angered when `|dy|<90 && |dx|<260`; walks at 55 px/s; every 2.2 s when grounded and `|dx|<200` → leap `vy=620, vx=±230`, emitting 6 particles; the slam frame (`timer∈(1.9,2.0)`) deals **18 dmg** in a 70 px/34 px box.
`gravityMove()` (146–164) integrates gravity, does axis-aligned X collision with 0.3 bounce, and sets `grounded` (note: it contains a dead `fall` calculation at lines 158–160 that cancels itself out).

### 1.16 `world/Particles.java` (69 LOC) — **58/69 pure**
Ring buffer, `N = 320`, SoA arrays: `x,y,vx,vy,life,maxLife,size[], int color[], boolean gravity[]`, `head`.
`emit(px,py,vx,vy,color,size,life,gravity)`; `emitBurst(px,py,color,count,speed,size,life)` (radial, ±20 % speed jitter); `emitSparks` = burst(5, 100, size 4, life 0.4).
`update(dt)` — gravity 900 px/s², ground bounce at `tileToWorldY(0)+2`.

> ⚠ **`Particles.update(dt)` is NEVER CALLED.** Grep across all of `core` returns zero call sites — `World.update()` emits particles but never integrates them. Consequently `life[]` never decrements, `render()`'s `t = life/maxLife` stays `1.0` forever, and particles never die. In practice the ring buffer saturates at **320 permanently-visible static dots** and every `emitBurst` overwrites the oldest slot. **Port decision: keep or drop — the current build ships ~320 undying static particles.**

`render()` — up to **320 draws** of `Assets.glowDot` at `size*2` px, alpha `= t`.

**Actually-used non-ASCII characters in the whole codebase: 74** (`66` Cyrillic + `«» — – “ ” … ► ▼`). Plus Latin/digits for `Element.name` (`PYRO/CRYO/HYDRO/ANEMO/…`) and `"100/100"`.

**NDS budget note:** `DejaVuSans.ttf` is **759,720 bytes**, sfnt version `0x00010000` (TrueType), 20 tables. Six 8-bpp Cyrillic bitmap fonts would be ~6 MB — impossible. Realistic plan: bake **3 sizes (12/18/24 px)** into 4-bpp 8×16-style tile sheets over a **~120-glyph subset** ≈ 40 KB VRAM, integer-scaled. The 54-px title becomes a pre-rendered bitmap of 4 strings.

## 2. Game systems in depth

### 2.1 `world/World.java` (1351 LOC) — the hub

#### Level / map format
**Procedural, not data-driven.** There is **no level string/array/asset file**. The world is built by imperative calls in `build()` (107–116) → `buildTerrain(); addGates(); addWaypoints(); addNpcs(); addChests(); addEnemies(); new Player(...)`.

- `int[][] tiles = new int[46][150]` — **indexed `[row][col]`, row 0 = TOP of the world, row 45 = bottom.**
- `MW = 150`, `MH = 46`, `T = Config.TILE = 32`
- **World size = 4800 × 1472 px = 6900 tile cells (5,670 AIR / 1,230 non-air).**
- Coordinate mapping: `tileToWorldX(col) = col*32`, `tileToWorldY(row) = (46-1-row)*32` → **row 45 = y 0 (bottom), row 0 = y 1440 (top).**
- Inverse: `col = (int)(wx/32)`, `row = (int)ceil(MH - 2 - wy/32)` — i.e. `ceil(44 - wy/32)`. The `ceil` makes a point exactly on a tile's **top face belong to the cell above**.

**Tile codes (line 22):** `AIR 0, GRASS 1, DIRT 2, STONE 3, ICE_T 4, SNOW 5, BRICK 6, PLAT 7, WATER_T 8, CRYST 9, LAVA_T 10`.

#### Collision
```java
solidAt(wx,wy):
  c = (int)(wx/T); r = rowAt(wy)
  if c<0 || c>=MW -> true          // side walls are solid
  if r<0           -> false         // sky is open
  if r>=MH         -> true          // bottom of world is solid
  t = tiles[r][c]
  if t in {GRASS,DIRT,STONE,ICE,SNOW,BRICK,CRYST}  -> checkGates(), else true
  // AIR, PLAT, WATER, LAVA fall through
  checkGates()                      // a gate block makes ANY tile solid
```
`platformAt()` → `tiles[r][c] == PLAT` only (one-way, downward only).
`supportAt(c,r)` (366) → true for any solid tile, PLAT, or an overlapping active gate.
`groundTopAt(wx,wy)` (356) → scans rows downward from `rowAt(wy)` and returns the first `tileToWorldY(rr)` that `supportAt`, else `-1`.
`tileAt(wx,wy)` returns `-1` out of bounds, else the raw tile code.
`rectsOverlap` (1345) is the standard 4-comparison AABB test; `dist` is plain Euclidean.

#### Camera
Camera lives in **`GameScreen`**, not `World` (see §1.10). `World` only supplies `getShakeX()/getShakeY()` (1349–1350) = `Math.random()*2*amt - amt` while `shakeTimer>0`. `screenShake(dur, amt)` takes `max` of both current values.

#### Update loop order — `World.update(InputState in, float dt)` (397–435)
```
1  time += dt ; shakeTimer -= dt
2  snapshot wasGrounded, vyBefore, wasInWater
3  handlePlayerInput(in, dt)     // movement, gravity, jump/coyote/buffer, jump-cut, dash, attack
4  player.moveAndCollide(this, dt)
5  player.updateState()
6  player.invuln -= dt
7  updateAttack(dt)               // combo timer + melee hits
8  updatePlayerSkill(in, dt)      // elemental projectile + burst nova
9  updateEnemies(dt)              // iterate backwards; drop + remove on death
10 updateProjectiles(dt)          // integrate, life cull, player/enemy hit, gate reaction
11 checkInteractions(dt)          // contact dmg, water, lava, death zone, chests, waypoints, NPCs, boss
12 emitAmbient()
13 cleanup()                      // removeIf dead / !alive
14 animation polish: dash trail, landing dust (+shake), water splash (+Sfx), run dust
```
`handlePlayerInput` detail (437–489): DASH is a hard state lock that skips everything but the dash timer; horizontal velocity uses **`MathUtils.lerp(vx, target, min(1, dt*accel/400))`** with `accel = ACCEL/AIR_DECEL/GROUND_DECEL` chosen by grounded/target state and `vx=0` snap below 5 px/s; gravity applied directly to `vy` with `-MAX_FALL` clamp; coyote/jump-buffer windows; jump-cut multiplies `vy *= 0.45` on release; dash sets `invuln = DASH_TIME + 0.05`.

Combat: melee `dmg = 8 + comboStep*4` (8/12/16) over a 3-hit combo, `atkCenter = (x+w/2+facing*20, y+h*0.6)`, `atkRadius=18`, `COMBO_WINDOW=0.5 s`, `comboStep = (comboStep+1)%3`, knockback `±220`. Skill projectile: `speed 380`, `dmg 14`, `radius 6`, `SKILL_CD 1.4`, spawned at `(x+w/2+facing*18, y+h*0.65)`, `vy = -114` when jumping. Burst nova: `40 dmg`, radius `180`, 40 particles, shake 0.5/8, requires `BURST`.

**Elemental reactions** (`applyElementToEnemy`, 569–588) — only when the enemy *already* carries a different element:
`PYRO↔HYRO ×1.6` (vaporize) · `PYRO↔CRYO ×2.0` (melt) · either side ANEMO `×1.3` (swirl) · base `20` damage, 14-particle burst, shake 0.2/4 when mult ≥ 1.5. Otherwise just applies `status = element, statusLife = 4 s`.

Hazards: water caps `vy ≤ 80` and heals 1 HP per 0.8 s while grounded; lava sets `vy ≥ 300` and deals 12 dmg per 0.5 s; `y < -40` = death zone → full damage + respawn.

#### Save/load
`save()` (1245) writes a **hand-rolled `;`-delimited string**: `{x:…;y:…;hp:…;mx:…;ab:DASH,BURST;vine:true;frost:…;fire:…;bd:…;tr:…;won:…;rx:…;ry:…;ch:0101010}`. `load()` (1271) re-parses with `split(";")` + `indexOf(':')` into a `HashMap`, clamps `maxHp ≤ 200`, validates `respawn` against `tileAt(...)==AIR`, restores gate actives from the flags, re-unlocks DOUBLE_JUMP+BURST if the boss died, and forces `activeElement = ANEMO`. Wrapped in `try/catch` → on failure prints to stderr and marks `saveDirty` to rewrite. Persisted through `Gdx.app.getPreferences("elementia-save").putString("save01", …)` + `flush()` **every frame in which `saveDirty` is set**.

`NPC_TEXT` (65–103) is a `static HashMap<String,String[]>` with **12 Russian entries** (`intro, elder, keeper, sage, witch, s_dash, s_vine, s_frost, s_boss, s_lava, s_hydro, s_win`). Each is `{speaker, body-with-\n}`.

Flags: `vineBurned, frostMelted, fireDoused, bossStarted, bossDefeated, trophyClaimed, gameWon, introPending`.

**Pass 7 breakdown (the dominant cost):** the gate "overlay pattern" loop draws a 2×2 `whiteDot` on a 6-px grid over the *entire* gate rect:
```
VINE   64x352  -> 11 x 59 = 649
FROST  32x704  ->  6 x 118 = 708
MAGMA  64x160  -> 11 x 27 = 297
FIRE   32x224  ->  6 x 38 = 228   + 23 flame quads
+ 4 base gate quads
                     TOTAL = 1909
```
**Total ≈ 2,500–2,650 sprite quads per frame**, of which ~**73 % is gate overlay**, ~**13 % particles**, ~**7 % parallax**. The 4-px `setColor`/`draw` granularity also means **~38 `setColor` calls inside `World.render` alone** (so ~80+ per frame across all systems). This is the single biggest NDS porting risk: the DS 2D engine (VRAM-affine sprites) caps out around 128–256 hardware sprites, so you must **convert the whole renderer to a software framebuffer** (256×192 `u16` VRAM buffer → `dmaCopy` / `swiWaitForVBlank`) and keep quads cheap, or aggressively batch (merge all same-texture, same-color quads; replace the 1909 gate dots with a pre-tiled texture; drop per-particle quads).

### 2.3 `renderParallax` / `drawImmersion` — the "2.5D"
There is **no camera-scrolling parallax** — `P_LAYERS` (line 856) are three *static screen-space* sine ridges:
```java
static final float[][] P_LAYERS = { {0.58f, 18f, 0.011f}, {0.50f, 26f, 0.008f}, {0.42f, 34f, 0.006f} };
//  {baseYfrac of VIEW_H, ampPx, wavelength}
y = VIEW_H*baseYfrac + amp*sin(sx*k + seed) + amp*0.5*sin(sx*k*2.2 + seed*1.7)
```
`parallaxCol(zone)` returns 3 `Color`s per zone (zone 0 meadow green … zone 4 volcanic red) at alphas 0.35/0.42/0.52. `drawImmersion` adds a zone tint quad at α 0.08 and a 14-px black vignette on all 4 edges at α 0.26. **This is the entirety of the "2.5D" look and it is trivially portable.**

### 2.4 `core/Sfx.java` — procedural audio (408 LOC)

**Format:** 16-bit signed **mono PCM WAV**, **22050 Hz**, standard 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header, `byteRate = RATE*2`, `blockAlign = 2`, `bitsPerSample = 16` (`wavPcm()` line 172, hand-written with `putStr/putLE/putLE16`).
**Synth primitives:** `rng = 987654321` LCG (`rng = rng*1103515245 + 12345`, bits 8..23), `silent, add, tone(len,f,amp)`, `sweep(len,f0,f1,amp,wave)` with `wave` 0=sine / 1=square (`signum(sin)`) / 2=triangle, `noise(len,amp)`, `envFade(in,out)`, `scale`, `envSwell`.
**Deployment:** `init()` writes each missing WAV to `Gdx.files.local("audio/<name>.wav")` (gitignored — see `.gitignore` "Runtime-generated audio cache"), then `Gdx.audio.newSound(file)`. Music is `Gdx.audio.newMusic("audio/music.wav")` with `setLooping(true)`. If `Gdx.audio == null` (headless) `available=false` and **every call is a no-op**.
Volumes: `sfxVolume = 0.6`, `musicVolume = 0.35`. `play(name, vol, pitch)` clamps vol to [0,1] and calls `Sound.setPitch(id, pitch)`.

**Net:** roughly **80 % of the codebase is platform-independent logic or offline-bakeable asset generation**, and only ~16 % needs a hand-written libnds replacement. The entire "engine surface" you must re-create in C is: a `SpriteBatch`-equivalent software blitter with `setColor` tinting + region/UV support + rotation (needed for the slash crescent), a bitmap font renderer, a WAV/`raw` sound player, a `Preferences` string store, and a `Screen` router. **None of the underlying simulation, level data, AI, or combat needs to change** — except you must decide how to reproduce `Particles` (currently broken), the 1909 gate dots, and the static 186-quad parallax.

### 2.6 Notable behaviours / latent bugs to decide on for the port
1. **`Particles.update()` is never called** → particles never move or die; steady state = 320 static full-alpha dots. *Design decision needed.*
2. **`setColor` integer bug** at `TitleScreen.java:54` and `Hud.java:100` — passes 0–255 ints instead of `/255f`.
3. **Gates are drawn with no camera culling** → 1909 of ~2500 quads per frame are off-screen.
4. **`Config.CAM_LOOKAHEAD` (60f) is unused**; camera lookahead is hardcoded `vx*0.14` clamped ±80.
5. **`OrthographicCamera` is pinned to centre and the world is offset manually** — the "camera" object is effectively a no-op projection; the port only needs `u_x = -(camX)`, `u_y = -(camY)` style offsets.

Index: nds/FORMATS.md
===================================================================
--- nds/FORMATS.md	
+++ nds/FORMATS.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+# Binary asset formats
+
+Two blobs are produced offline by `nds/tools/nds_bake.py` (run by
+`nds/gen/Makefile`) and linked into the ARM9 image with `bin2o`:
+
+* `gen/art.bin`   – sprites and tiles
+* `gen/fonts.bin` – three baked bitmap fonts (Latin + Cyrillic)
+
+Both are little-endian and addressed from the start of the blob.
+
+---
+
+## art.bin
+
+```
+u32  magic     = 'ARTB' (0x42525441)
+u16  version   = 1
+u16  count     number of textures
+u32  entrySize = 28
+Entry entries[count]        // no padding, tightly packed
+u16  pixelBytes             // total, multiple of 4
+u16  pad0
+u8   nameLen
+u8   reserved
+Entry entry[count]
+--- data follows the table, in table order ---
+u16  pixels[pixelBytes/2]   // RGB555, row major, top-left origin
+u32  masks[pixelBytes*2/8]  // 1bpp coverage, row major, LSB = leftmost pixel
+```
+
+`Entry` (28 bytes):
+
+```
+u8   nameLen    length of the NUL terminated ASCII name that follows
+u8   reserved
+u16  w
+u16  h
+u32  pixelOff   byte offset of the colour plane inside `pixels`
+u32  maskOff    byte offset of the coverage plane inside `masks`
+u8   name[nameLen] (padded so the struct is exactly 28 bytes)
+```
+
+Canonical names, in the order the baker emits them:
+
+```
+grass dirt stone ice snow brick lavaA lavaB water
+platform crystal tree chest hero slime wisp golem boss waypoint
+```
+
+Anything missing from the PNG set is simply absent; the C side falls back to a
+procedurally painted texture.
+
+---
+
+## fonts.bin
+
+```
+u32  magic    = 'FNTS' (0x53544e46)
+u8   count    number of fonts (3)
+u8   reserved[3]
+Font fonts[count]
+--- data follows the table, in table order ---
+```
+
+`Font` header:
+
+```
+u8   glyphCount
+u8   lineHeight   pixels between baselines
+u8   ascent       pixels above the baseline to the cap line
+u8   reserved
+u32  atlasOff     byte offset of the 1bpp atlas inside the blob
+u32  atlasW
+u32  atlasH
+Glyph glyphs[glyphCount]   // sorted ascending by codepoint
+```
+
+`Glyph` (16 bytes):
+
+```
+u32  codepoint   UTF-8 decoded
+u16  advance     pen movement in pixels (unsigned, 8.8 would be nicer but the
+                 font is baked at one size so integers are enough)
+u16  x           ink box inside the atlas
+u16  y
+u16  w
+u16  h
+```
+
+The atlas is 1bpp, row stride `(atlasW + 31) / 32 * 4` bytes, 1 = ink.
+
+Drawing rule (see `font.c`):
+
+```
+pen baseline = (x, y)              // same convention as LibGDX BitmapFont#draw
+ink top left  = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y)
+```
+
+Fonts are emitted in this order and bound to the `FONT_*` enum:
+
+| index | enum         | point size |
+|-------|--------------|------------|
+| 0     | `FONT_SMALL` | 12         |
+| 1     | `FONT_BODY`  | 20         |
+| 2     | `FONT_TITLE` | 32         |

Index: nds/build.sh
===================================================================
--- nds/build.sh	
+++ nds/build.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Builds the Nintendo DS ROM (nds/elementia.nds) inside the official devkitPro
+# container, so no local devkitARM install is required.
+#
+#   ./nds/build.sh            build the ROM
+#   ./nds/build.sh clean      remove build output
+set -euo pipefail
+
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
+IMAGE="${DEVKITPRO_IMAGE:-devkitpro/devkitarm:latest}"
+ARTIFACTS="${ELEMENTIA_ARTIFACTS:-/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp}"
+
+if ! docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+	echo ">> pulling $IMAGE"
+	docker pull "$IMAGE"
+fi
+
+run() {
+	docker run --rm \
+		-u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
+		-e HOME=/tmp \
+		-e DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro \
+		-e DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM \
+		-v "$REPO:/work" \
+		-v "$ARTIFACTS:/out" \
+		-w /work/nds \
+		"$IMAGE" \
+		bash -c 'source /opt/devkitpro/devkitarm.sh && exec "$@"' bash "$@"
+}
+
+case "${1:-all}" in
+	clean)
+		run make clean
+		;;
+	assets)
+		run make -C gen
+		;;
+	*)
+		shift 2>/dev/null || true
+		run make "$@"
+		cp -f "$HERE/elementia.nds" "$ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
+		echo ">> $ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
+		;;
+esac

--- nds/gen/Makefile

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Asset generation for the NDS build.
+#
+# Everything in here is produced on the host (inside the devkitPro container) and
+# ends up as a raw blob in ../gen, which the ARM9 Makefile turns into an object
+# with bin2o.
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+.PHONY: all clean fonts art
+
+TOPDIR := $(CURDIR)/..
+REPO   := $(TOPDIR)/..
+PY     := python3
+
+SRC_FONT := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf
+SRC_ART  := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/art
+
+GEN      := $(CURDIR)
+BLITTER  := $(CURDIR)/_stub.py
+
+WHITELIST := $(CURDIR)/charset.txt
+
+all: $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin
+
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Bitmap font: mkbcfnt rasterises the TTF into BCFNT containers, the baker
+# trims every glyph and repacks them into a tight 1bpp atlas.
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+$(GEN)/fonts.bin: $(SRC_FONT) $(WHITELIST) $(BLITTER)
+	@echo "baking fonts"
+	@$(PY) $(CURDIR)/_stub.py \
+		--font $(SRC_FONT) \
+		--charset $(WHITELIST) \
+		--out $(GEN)/fonts.bin \
+		--tmp $(GEN) \
+		--sizes 12,20,32
+
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Sprites/tiles: the AI generated PNGs are cropped to the regions the game
+# actually uses and packed into 4bpp atlases.
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+$(GEN)/art.bin: $(SRC_ART)/*.png $(BLITTER)
+	@echo "baking art"
+	@$(PY) $(CURDIR)/_stub.py \
+		--src $(SRC_ART) \
+		--out $(GEN)/art.bin \
+		--manifest $(GEN)/art_manifest.h
+
+clean:
+	@rm -f $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/art_manifest.h
+	@rm -f $(GEN)/bc_*.bcfnt

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Minimal bin2o replacement (the devkitPro container has bin2s but not bin2o).
+
+Usage: bin2o.py <input.bin> <output.s> [symbol]
+
+Emits an assembly stub that pulls the blob into .rodata and exports:
+
+    _<sym>_start   .rodata address of the first byte
+    _<sym>_end     .rodata address one past the last byte
+    _<sym>_size    byte length
+
+`<sym>` defaults to the input basename with dots turned into underscores.
+"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    if len(argv) < 3:
+        sys.stderr.write(__doc__)
