@@ -0,0 +1,1420 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Offline asset baker for the Nintendo DS port of Elementia.
+
+Reads the LibGDX source assets
+
+    core/src/main/resources/art/*.png
+    core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf
+
+and writes the two blobs described in ``nds/FORMATS.md``:
+
+    nds/gen/art.bin     ARTB  -- RGB555 colour plane + 1bpp coverage plane
+    nds/gen/fonts.bin   FNTS  -- three baked 1bpp bitmap fonts
+
+Both blobs are consumed by C code that this script must not have to know
+about, so the layout is fixed here and never guessed at runtime.
+
+Standard library only: no PIL, no numpy, no FreeType, no mkbcfnt.  PNG and
+TrueType decoding are both implemented here from scratch, so the pipeline runs
+under a plain ``python3`` on the host as well as inside the devkitPro
+container.
+
+Usage
+-----
+    nds_bake.py art    --src <dir> --out art.bin
+    nds_bake.py fonts  --font <ttf> --charset charset.txt --out fonts.bin
+                      [--sizes 12,20,32]
+    nds_bake.py verify art.bin fonts.bin
+    nds_bake.py summary art.bin fonts.bin
+
+``verify`` re-parses both blobs, checks the magic, walks every entry/glyph,
+asserts that every offset stays in bounds and prints the summary tables.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Format constants (nds/FORMATS.md)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ART_MAGIC = 0x42525441        # 'ARTB'
+ART_VERSION = 1
+ART_ENTRY_SIZE = 28
+ART_HEADER_SIZE = 12          # u32 magic, u16 version, u16 count, u32 entrySize
+
+FONT_MAGIC = 0x53544E46       # 'FNTS'
+FONT_HEADER_SIZE = 8          # u32 magic, u8 count, u8 reserved[3]
+FONT_RECORD_SIZE = 20         # see bake_fonts() for the layout deviation
+# FORMATS.md lists six fields for Glyph, which sum to 14 bytes but are declared
+# 16.  x and y must be signed - the drawing rule places ink *above* the pen
+# baseline - so the record is laid out as:
+#   u32 codepoint, u16 advance, s16 x, s16 y, u16 w, u16 h, u16 reserved
+GLYPH_SIZE = 16
+
+
+def plane_stride(w):
+    """Row stride of a 1bpp plane in bytes: whole 32-bit words, so the C side
+    can walk the plane with a ``const u32 *``."""
+    return ((w + 31) // 32) * 4
+
+
+# Bit order inside a 1bpp plane.
+#
+# FORMATS.md says "LSB = leftmost pixel" and include/gfx.h repeats it
+# (``const u32 *mask; // w*h bits, row major, LSB = leftmost pixel``), so pixel
+# (x, y) lives in bit ``x`` of byte ``x >> 3`` of row ``y``.  The font atlas is
+# written the same way; FORMATS.md does not state an order for it.
+def plane_bit(x):
+    return 1 << (x & 7)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Canonical texture set.  Names and order are normative (FORMATS.md); the sizes
+# are the rectangles the LibGDX build stretched each source texture into, which
+# is exactly what the NDS blitter draws into.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+TEXTURES = [
+    ("grass", 32, 32),
+    ("dirt", 32, 32),
+    ("stone", 32, 32),
+    ("ice", 32, 32),
+    ("snow", 32, 32),
+    ("brick", 32, 32),
+    ("lavaA", 32, 32),
+    ("lavaB", 32, 32),
+    ("water", 32, 32),
+    ("platform", 32, 14),
+    ("crystal", 24, 30),
+    ("tree", 32, 48),
+    ("chest", 28, 24),
+    ("hero", 56, 76),
+    ("slime", 44, 38),
+    ("wisp", 16, 14),
+    ("golem", 56, 52),
+    ("boss", 88, 76),
+    ("waypoint", 40, 56),
+]
+
+FONT_SIZES = (12, 20, 32)     # FONT_SMALL, FONT_BODY, FONT_TITLE
+
+# Alpha ramp for the coverage plane.
+#
+# The AI generated sprites have soft, antialiased edges.  A hard ``alpha >= 128``
+# cut would chew holes in them, so coverage is remapped so that anything below
+# ALPHA_FLOOR is fully transparent and anything above ALPHA_CEIL fully opaque,
+# with a linear ramp between:
+#
+#     coverage = clamp((alpha - 40) * 255 / 168, 0, 255)
+#
+# i.e. fully transparent below alpha 40, fully opaque above alpha 208.  The
+# plane is still a hard 1bpp mask; the ramp only decides where the cut falls.
+ALPHA_FLOOR = 40
+ALPHA_CEIL = 208
+
+
+class BakeError(Exception):
+    """Recoverable problem with one asset; the caller warns and continues."""
+
+
+def warn(msg):
+    sys.stderr.write("nds_bake: warning: %s\n" % msg)
+
+
+def _floor(v):
+    return int(v // 1)
+
+
+def _ceil(v):
+    return -int(-v // 1)
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# PNG decoder
+# ===========================================================================
+
+PNG_SIG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
+
+# Adam7: (x_start, y_start, x_step, y_step) per pass.
+_ADAM7 = (
+    (0, 0, 8, 8), (4, 0, 8, 8), (0, 4, 4, 8), (2, 0, 4, 4),
+    (0, 2, 2, 4), (1, 0, 2, 2), (0, 1, 1, 2),
+)
+
+_CHANNELS = {0: 1, 2: 3, 3: 1, 4: 2, 6: 4}
+
+
+def _paeth(a, b, c):
+    p = a + b - c
+    pa = abs(p - a)
+    pb = abs(p - b)
+    pc = abs(p - c)
+    if pa <= pb and pa <= pc:
+        return a
+    if pb <= pc:
+        return b
+    return c
+
+
+def _unfilter(raw, height, stride, bpp):
+    """Reverse the per-scanline PNG filters (None/Sub/Up/Average/Paeth)."""
+    out = bytearray(stride * height)
+    prev = bytearray(stride)
+    pos = 0
+    for y in range(height):
+        if pos + 1 + stride > len(raw):
+            raise BakeError("truncated image data (row %d of %d)" % (y, height))
+        ft = raw[pos]
+        pos += 1
+        line = bytearray(raw[pos:pos + stride])
+        pos += stride
+
+        if ft == 0:
+            pass
+        elif ft == 1:
+            for i in range(bpp, stride):
+                line[i] = (line[i] + line[i - bpp]) & 0xFF
+        elif ft == 2:
+            for i in range(stride):
+                line[i] = (line[i] + prev[i]) & 0xFF
+        elif ft == 3:
+            for i in range(stride):
+                left = line[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
+                line[i] = (line[i] + ((left + prev[i]) >> 1)) & 0xFF
+        elif ft == 4:
+            for i in range(stride):
+                left = line[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
+                upleft = prev[i - bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
+                line[i] = (line[i] + _paeth(left, prev[i], upleft)) & 0xFF
+        else:
+            raise BakeError("unknown scanline filter %d" % ft)
+
+        out[y * stride:(y + 1) * stride] = line
+        prev = line
+    return out
+
+
+def _expand_samples(line, count, depth):
+    """Turn unfiltered scanline bytes into a flat list of 0..255 samples."""
+    if depth == 8:
+        return list(line[:count])
+    if depth == 16:
+        return [line[i * 2] for i in range(count)]      # take the high byte
+    maxval = (1 << depth) - 1
+    per_byte = 8 // depth
+    out = []
+    for i in range(count):
+        byte = line[i // per_byte]
+        shift = 8 - depth * ((i % per_byte) + 1)
+        out.append(((byte >> shift) & maxval) * 255 // maxval)
+    return out
+
+
+def decode_png(path):
+    """Decode a PNG into ``(width, height, bytearray of RGBA8 rows)``.
+
+    Handles colour types 0/2/3/4/6, bit depths 1/2/4/8/16, all five scanline
+    filters and Adam7 interlacing.  Anything genuinely unsupported raises
+    BakeError so the caller can skip the texture instead of crashing.
+    """
+    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
+        data = fh.read()
+    if data[:8] != PNG_SIG:
+        raise BakeError("not a PNG file")
+
+    pos = 8
+    width = height = depth = ctype = None
+    interlace = 0
+    palette = None
+    trns = None
+    idat = []
+
+    while pos + 8 <= len(data):
+        (length,) = struct.unpack(">I", data[pos:pos + 4])
+        ctag = data[pos + 4:pos + 8]
+        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + length]
+        pos += 12 + length
+        if ctag == b"IHDR":
+            (width, height, depth, ctype, _comp, _filt,
+             interlace) = struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", body[:13])
+        elif ctag == b"PLTE":
+            palette = body
+        elif ctag == b"tRNS":
+            trns = body
+        elif ctag == b"IDAT":
+            idat.append(body)
+        elif ctag == b"IEND":
+            break
+
+    if width is None or not idat:
+        raise BakeError("missing IHDR or IDAT")
+    if ctype not in _CHANNELS:
+        raise BakeError("unsupported colour type %d" % ctype)
+    if depth not in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16):
+        raise BakeError("unsupported bit depth %d" % depth)
+    if interlace not in (0, 1):
+        raise BakeError("unsupported interlace method %d" % interlace)
+    if ctype == 3 and palette is None:
+        raise BakeError("palette image without PLTE")
+
+    raw = zlib.decompress(b"".join(idat))
+    channels = _CHANNELS[ctype]
+    rgba = bytearray(width * height * 4)
+
+    def emit(dx, dy, samples, count):
+        """Write `count` consecutive pixels starting at column dx of row dy."""
+        base = dy * width * 4 + dx * 4
+        if ctype == 3:
+            for i in range(count):
+                idx = samples[i]
+                o = base + i * 4
+                p = idx * 3
+                if p + 2 < len(palette):
+                    rgba[o] = palette[p]
+                    rgba[o + 1] = palette[p + 1]
+                    rgba[o + 2] = palette[p + 2]
+                if trns is not None and idx < len(trns):
+                    rgba[o + 3] = trns[idx]
+                else:
+                    rgba[o + 3] = 255
+            return
+        step = channels
+        for i in range(count):
+            o = base + i * 4
+            s = i * step
+            if channels >= 3:
+                rgba[o] = samples[s]
+                rgba[o + 1] = samples[s + 1]
+                rgba[o + 2] = samples[s + 2]
+            else:
+                rgba[o] = rgba[o + 1] = rgba[o + 2] = samples[s]
+            rgba[o + 3] = samples[s + channels - 1] if channels >= 2 else 255
+
+    if interlace == 0:
+        stride = (width * channels * depth + 7) // 8
+        bpp = max(1, channels * depth // 8)
+        pixels = _unfilter(raw, height, stride, bpp)
+        for y in range(height):
+            line = pixels[y * stride:(y + 1) * stride]
+            emit(0, y, _expand_samples(line, width * channels, depth), width)
+    else:
+        off = 0
+        for (xs, ys, xstep, ystep) in _ADAM7:
+            pw = (width - xs + xstep - 1) // xstep
+            ph = (height - ys + ystep - 1) // ystep
+            if pw <= 0 or ph <= 0:
+                continue
+            stride = (pw * channels * depth + 7) // 8
+            bpp = max(1, channels * depth // 8)
+            chunk = raw[off:off + (stride + 1) * ph]
+            off += (stride + 1) * ph
+            pixels = _unfilter(chunk, ph, stride, bpp)
+            for py in range(ph):
+                line = pixels[py * stride:(py + 1) * stride]
+                samples = _expand_samples(line, pw * channels, depth)
+                y = ys + py * ystep
+                for px in range(pw):
+                    x = xs + px * xstep
+                    emit(x, y, samples[px * channels:(px + 1) * channels], 1)
+
+    if width <= 0 or height <= 0:
+        raise BakeError("degenerate image size")
+    return width, height, rgba
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Resampling
+# ===========================================================================
+
+def resample(sw, sh, src, dw, dh):
+    """Area-average (box filter) resize of an RGBA8 buffer.
+
+    LibGDX stretched the *whole* source texture into the target rectangle, so
+    the NDS build downscales the whole image too - never a centre crop.  At a
+    1:1 ratio (or when the source is smaller than the destination, where a box
+    filter degenerates) it falls back to nearest neighbour.
+    """
+    if sw == dw and sh == dh:
+        return bytearray(src)
+    if sw <= dw or sh <= dh:
+        return _resample_nearest(sw, sh, src, dw, dh)
+
+    out = bytearray(dw * dh * 4)
+    xr = sw / float(dw)
+    yr = sh / float(dh)
+    for dy in range(dh):
+        sy0 = dy * yr
+        sy1 = sy0 + yr
+        iy0 = int(sy0)
+        iy1 = min(sh, _ceil(sy1))
+        ybase = dy * dw * 4
+        for dx in range(dw):
+            sx0 = dx * xr
+            sx1 = sx0 + xr
+            ix0 = int(sx0)
+            ix1 = min(sw, _ceil(sx1))
+
+            rsum = gsum = bsum = 0.0
+            asum = 0.0      # sum(w * a)
+            wsum = 0.0      # sum(w)
+            war = wag = wab = 0.0
+            for iy in range(iy0, iy1):
+                lo = sy0 if iy < sy0 else iy
+                hi = sy1 if iy + 1 > sy1 else iy + 1
+                wy = hi - lo
+                if wy <= 0.0:
+                    continue
+                row = (iy * sw) * 4
+                for ix in range(ix0, ix1):
+                    lo = sx0 if ix < sx0 else ix
+                    hi = sx1 if ix + 1 > sx1 else ix + 1
+                    wx = hi - lo
+                    if wx <= 0.0:
+                        continue
+                    w = wx * wy
+                    o = row + ix * 4
+                    a = src[o + 3]
+                    rsum += w * src[o]
+                    gsum += w * src[o + 1]
+                    bsum += w * src[o + 2]
+                    asum += w * a
+                    wsum += w
+                    war += w * a * src[o]
+                    wag += w * a * src[o + 1]
+                    wab += w * a * src[o + 2]
+
+            o = ybase + dx * 4
+            if wsum <= 0.0:
+                wsum = 1.0
+            out[o + 3] = _clamp8(asum / wsum)
+            if asum > 0.0:
+                # Alpha-weighted average keeps antialiased edges from being
+                # dragged towards the RGB of fully transparent neighbours.
+                out[o] = _clamp8(war / asum)
+                out[o + 1] = _clamp8(wag / asum)
+                out[o + 2] = _clamp8(wab / asum)
+            else:
+                out[o] = _clamp8(rsum / wsum)
+                out[o + 1] = _clamp8(gsum / wsum)
+                out[o + 2] = _clamp8(bsum / wsum)
+    return out
+
+
+def _resample_nearest(sw, sh, src, dw, dh):
+    out = bytearray(dw * dh * 4)
+    for dy in range(dh):
+        sy = min(sh - 1, (dy * sh) // dh)
+        for dx in range(dw):
+            sx = min(sw - 1, (dx * sw) // dw)
+            o = (dy * dw + dx) * 4
+            s = (sy * sw + sx) * 4
+            out[o:o + 4] = src[s:s + 4]
+    return out
+
+
+def _clamp8(v):
+    i = int(v)
+    return 0 if i < 0 else (255 if i > 255 else i)
+
+
+def coverage(alpha):
+    """Smooth alpha -> coverage ramp; see ALPHA_FLOOR / ALPHA_CEIL."""
+    c = (alpha - ALPHA_FLOOR) * 255 // (ALPHA_CEIL - ALPHA_FLOOR)
+    return 0 if c < 0 else (255 if c > 255 else c)
+
+
+def rgb555(r, g, b):
+    """Mirror of the C side's rgb555(): R in bits 0-4, G in 5-9, B in 10-14."""
+    return ((r >> 3) << 0) | ((g >> 3) << 5) | ((b >> 3) << 10)
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# art.bin
+# ===========================================================================
+
+def bake_art(src_dir, out_path):
+    if not os.path.isdir(src_dir):
+        raise BakeError("art source directory not found: %s" % src_dir)
+
+    entries = []
+    for name, tw, th in TEXTURES:
+        path = _find_png(src_dir, name)
+        if path is None:
+            warn("%s: source PNG not found, skipping texture (the C side "
+                 "falls back to a procedural one)" % name)
+            continue
+        try:
+            sw, sh, rgba = decode_png(path)
+        except BakeError as exc:
+            warn("%s: %s, skipping texture" % (name, exc))
+            continue
+        except Exception as exc:                    # pragma: no cover
+            warn("%s: cannot decode (%s), skipping texture" % (name, exc))
+            continue
+
+        small = resample(sw, sh, rgba, tw, th)
+        stride = plane_stride(tw)
+        pixels = bytearray(tw * th * 2)
+        masks = bytearray(stride * th)
+        for y in range(th):
+            row = y * tw * 4
+            for x in range(tw):
+                o = row + x * 4
+                r, g, b, a = small[o], small[o + 1], small[o + 2], small[o + 3]
+                # The blitter indexes colour and mask independently, so the
+                # colour of a transparent pixel must still be written out.
+                struct.pack_into("<H", pixels, (y * tw + x) * 2,
+                                 rgb555(r, g, b))
+                if coverage(a) >= 128:
+                    masks[y * stride + (x >> 3)] |= plane_bit(x)
+        entries.append((name, tw, th, pixels, masks))
+
+    if not entries:
+        raise BakeError("no usable source art found in %s" % src_dir)
+
+    pixel_bytes = sum(len(e[3]) for e in entries)
+    # FORMATS.md declares the mask region as `u32 masks[pixelBytes*2/8]`, i.e.
+    # exactly as many bytes as the colour plane.  Every texture row is already a
+    # whole number of 32-bit words, so that is always >= the mask data actually
+    # written; the tail is zero filled so the declared bound holds and the C
+    # side can derive masksAt = tableEnd + pixelBytes without a stored field.
+    mask_bytes = pixel_bytes
+    if sum(len(e[4]) for e in entries) > mask_bytes:
+        raise BakeError("internal error: mask region overflow")
+
+    table_end = ART_HEADER_SIZE + ART_ENTRY_SIZE * len(entries)
+    pixels_at = table_end
+    masks_at = pixels_at + pixel_bytes
+
+    out = bytearray(masks_at + mask_bytes)
+    struct.pack_into("<IHHI", out, 0, ART_MAGIC, ART_VERSION,
+                     len(entries), ART_ENTRY_SIZE)
+
+    po = mo = 0
+    for i, (name, tw, th, pixels, masks) in enumerate(entries):
+        nm = name.encode("ascii")
+        if len(nm) + 1 > ART_ENTRY_SIZE - 14:
+            raise BakeError("texture name %r too long for Entry" % name)
+        e = ART_HEADER_SIZE + i * ART_ENTRY_SIZE
+        out[e] = len(nm)
+        out[e + 1] = 0
+        struct.pack_into("<HHII", out, e + 2, tw, th, po, mo)
+        out[e + 14:e + 14 + len(nm)] = nm
+        out[pixels_at + po:pixels_at + po + len(pixels)] = pixels
+        out[masks_at + mo:masks_at + mo + len(masks)] = masks
+        po += len(pixels)
+        mo += len(masks)
+
+    _write(out_path, bytes(out))
+    return [_tex_stats(e) for e in entries], len(out)
+
+
+def _find_png(src_dir, name):
+    for cand in (name + ".png", name.lower() + ".png", name.upper() + ".png"):
+        p = os.path.join(src_dir, cand)
+        if os.path.isfile(p):
+            return p
+    want = (name + ".png").lower()
+    for fn in sorted(os.listdir(src_dir)):
+        if fn.lower() == want:
+            return os.path.join(src_dir, fn)
+    return None
+
+
+def _tex_stats(entry):
+    name, tw, th, _pixels, masks = entry
+    stride = plane_stride(tw)
+    opaque = 0
+    for y in range(th):
+        row = masks[y * stride:(y + 1) * stride]
+        for x in range(tw):
+            if row[x >> 3] & plane_bit(x):
+                opaque += 1
+    return (name, tw, th, opaque, tw * th)
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# TrueType
+# ===========================================================================
+
+_F2DOT14 = 1.0 / 16384.0
+
+_CMP_ARGS_ARE_WORDS = 0x0001
+_CMP_ARGS_ARE_XY = 0x0002
+_CMP_WE_HAVE_A_SCALE = 0x0008
+_CMP_MORE = 0x0020
+_CMP_WE_HAVE_XY_SCALE = 0x0040
+_CMP_WE_HAVE_2X2 = 0x0080
+_CMP_UNSCALED_OFFSET = 0x1000
+
+
+class TrueTypeFont(object):
+    """Just enough of the spec to rasterise a bitmap font: head, maxp, hhea,
+    hmtx, cmap, loca and glyf (including composite glyphs)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path):
+        self.path = path
+        self.advance = []
+        self.lsb = []
+        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
+            self.data = fh.read()
+        if len(self.data) < 12:
+            raise BakeError("%s: truncated font file" % path)
+        if self.data[:4] not in (b"\x00\x01\x00\x00", b"true", b"OTTO"):
+            raise BakeError("%s: not a TrueType/OpenType font" % path)
+
+        num = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[4:6])[0]
+        self.tables = {}
+        for i in range(num):
+            o = 12 + 16 * i
+            tag = self.data[o:o + 4].decode("latin-1")
+            off, ln = struct.unpack(">II", self.data[o + 8:o + 16])
+            self.tables[tag] = (off, ln)
+        for req in ("head", "maxp", "hhea", "hmtx", "cmap", "loca", "glyf"):
+            if req not in self.tables:
+                raise BakeError("%s: missing '%s' table" % (path, req))
+
+        h = self.tables["head"][0]
+        (self.units_per_em,) = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[h + 18:h + 20])
+        (self.x_min, self.y_min, self.x_max,
+         self.y_max) = struct.unpack(">hhhh", self.data[h + 36:h + 44])
+        (self.mac_style,) = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[h + 44:h + 46])
+        (self.loc_fmt,) = struct.unpack(">h", self.data[h + 50:h + 52])
+        if self.units_per_em <= 0:
+            raise BakeError("%s: bad unitsPerEm" % path)
+        if self.loc_fmt not in (0, 1):
+            raise BakeError("%s: unsupported loca format %d" % (path, self.loc_fmt))
+
+        mp = self.tables["maxp"][0]
+        self.num_glyphs = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[mp + 4:mp + 6])[0]
+
+        hh = self.tables["hhea"][0]
+        (self.hhea_ascent, self.hhea_descent,
+         self.line_gap) = struct.unpack(">hhh", self.data[hh + 4:hh + 10])
+        self.num_h_metrics = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[hh + 34:hh + 36])[0]
+
+        # USE_TYPO_METRICS (OS/2 fsSelection bit 7) wins over hhea.
+        self.ascent_units = self.hhea_ascent
+        self.descent_units = self.hhea_descent
+        if "OS/2" in self.tables and self.tables["OS/2"][1] >= 74:
+            oo = self.tables["OS/2"][0]
+            if struct.unpack(">H", self.data[oo + 62:oo + 64])[0] & 0x0080:
+                ta, td, _tg = struct.unpack(">hhh", self.data[oo + 68:oo + 74])
+                self.ascent_units, self.descent_units = ta, td
+
+        self._read_loca()
+        self._read_hmtx()
+        self.cmap = self._read_cmap()
+
+    # -- tables ------------------------------------------------------------
+    def _read_loca(self):
+        off, ln = self.tables["loca"]
+        n = min(self.num_glyphs + 1, ln // (4 if self.loc_fmt else 2))
+        if self.loc_fmt == 0:
+            raw = struct.unpack(">%dH" % n, self.data[off:off + 2 * n])
+            self.loca = [v * 2 for v in raw]
+        else:
+            self.loca = list(struct.unpack(">%dI" % n, self.data[off:off + 4 * n]))
+        self.glyf_off = self.tables["glyf"][0]
+
+    def _read_hmtx(self):
+        off, ln = self.tables["hmtx"]
+        for i in range(self.num_h_metrics):
+            o = off + i * 4
+            if o + 4 > off + ln:
+                break
+            a, l = struct.unpack(">Hh", self.data[o:o + 4])
+            self.advance.append(a)
+            self.lsb.append(l)
+        if not self.advance:
+            raise BakeError("empty hmtx table")
+
+    def _read_cmap(self):
+        base = self.tables["cmap"][0]
+        n = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[base + 2:base + 4])[0]
+        subs = []
+        for i in range(n):
+            pid, eid, off = struct.unpack(">HHI", self.data[base + 4 + 8 * i:
+                                                          base + 12 + 8 * i])
+            fmt = struct.unpack(">H", self.data[base + off:base + off + 2])[0]
+            if (pid, eid) in ((3, 10), (0, 4), (0, 6), (3, 1), (0, 3), (0, 0),
+                              (3, 0)):
+                subs.append((pid, eid, fmt, base + off))
+        rank = {12: 0, 4: 1, 6: 2, 0: 3}
+        subs.sort(key=lambda s: (rank.get(s[2], 9), 0 if s[0] == 3 else 1))
+
+        table = {}
+        for _pid, _eid, fmt, off in subs:
+            table = self._parse_cmap_subtable(fmt, off)
+            if table:
+                break
+        if not table:
+            raise BakeError("%s: no usable cmap subtable" % self.path)
+        return table
+
+    def _parse_cmap_subtable(self, fmt, off):
+        d = self.data
+        table = {}
+        if fmt == 12:
+            ngroups = struct.unpack(">I", d[off + 12:off + 16])[0]
+            for g in range(ngroups):
+                o = off + 16 + 12 * g
+                s, e, gid = struct.unpack(">III", d[o:o + 12])
+                if e < s or e - s > 0x20000:
+                    continue
+                for c in range(s, e + 1):
+                    table[c] = gid + (c - s)
+        elif fmt == 4:
+            segx2 = struct.unpack(">H", d[off + 6:off + 8])[0]
+            seg = segx2 // 2
+            ends = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, d[off + 14:off + 14 + segx2])
+            so = off + 16 + segx2
+            starts = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, d[so:so + segx2])
+            do = so + segx2
+            deltas = struct.unpack(">%dh" % seg, d[do:do + segx2])
+            ro = do + segx2
+            ranges = struct.unpack(">%dH" % seg, d[ro:ro + segx2])
+            for i in range(seg):
+                if ranges[i] == 0 or starts[i] > ends[i]:
+                    continue
+                for c in range(starts[i], min(ends[i], 0xFFFE) + 1):
+                    gi = ro + i * 2 + ranges[i] + (c - starts[i]) * 2
+                    if gi + 2 > len(d):
+                        continue
+                    gid = struct.unpack(">H", d[gi:gi + 2])[0]
+                    if gid:
+                        table[c] = (gid + deltas[i]) & 0xFFFF
+        elif fmt == 6:
+            first, cnt = struct.unpack(">HH", d[off + 6:off + 10])
+            for i in range(cnt):
+                gid = struct.unpack(">H", d[off + 10 + i * 2:off + 12 + i * 2])[0]
+                if gid:
+                    table[first + i] = gid
+        elif fmt == 0:
+            for c in range(256):
+                gid = d[off + 6 + c]
+                if gid:
+                    table[c] = gid
+        return table
+
+    # -- outlines ----------------------------------------------------------
+    def glyph_contours(self, gid, _depth=0):
+        """List of contours, each a list of (x, y, on_curve) in font units."""
+        if _depth > 5 or gid < 0 or gid + 1 >= len(self.loca):
+            return []
+        start, end = self.loca[gid], self.loca[gid + 1]
+        if end <= start:
+            return []
+        o = self.glyf_off + start
+        ncont = struct.unpack(">h", self.data[o:o + 2])[0]
+        o += 10                                    # skip xMin/yMin/xMax/yMax
+        if ncont >= 0:
+            return self._simple_glyph(o, ncont)
+        return self._composite_glyph(o + 2, _depth)
+
+    def _simple_glyph(self, o, ncont):
+        d = self.data
+        if ncont <= 0:
+            return []
+        ends = struct.unpack(">%dH" % ncont, d[o:o + 2 * ncont])
+        o += 2 * ncont
+        ilen = struct.unpack(">H", d[o:o + 2])[0]
+        o += 2 + ilen
+        npts = ends[-1] + 1
+
+        flags = []
+        while len(flags) < npts:
+            f = d[o]
+            o += 1
+            flags.append(f)
+            if f & 0x08:
+                flags.extend([f] * d[o])
+                o += 1
+        del flags[npts:]
+
+        xs = []
+        x = 0
+        for f in flags:
+            if f & 0x02:
+                dx = d[o]
+                o += 1
+                x += dx if (f & 0x10) else -dx
+            elif not (f & 0x10):
+                x += struct.unpack(">h", d[o:o + 2])[0]
+                o += 2
+            xs.append(x)
+        ys = []
+        y = 0
+        for f in flags:
+            if f & 0x04:
+                dy = d[o]
+                o += 1
+                y += dy if (f & 0x20) else -dy
+            elif not (f & 0x20):
+                y += struct.unpack(">h", d[o:o + 2])[0]
+                o += 2
+            ys.append(y)
+
+        oncurve = [bool(f & 0x01) for f in flags]
+        contours = []
+        first = 0
+        for last in ends:
+            pts = [(xs[i], ys[i], oncurve[i]) for i in range(first, last + 1)]
+            first = last + 1
+            if pts:
+                contours.append(pts)
+        return contours
+
+    def _composite_glyph(self, o, depth):
+        d = self.data
+        out = []
+        while True:
+            flags, gid = struct.unpack(">HH", d[o:o + 4])
+            o += 4
+            if flags & _CMP_ARGS_ARE_WORDS:
+                a1, a2 = struct.unpack(">hh", d[o:o + 4])
+                o += 4
+            else:
+                a1, a2 = struct.unpack(">bb", d[o:o + 2])
+                o += 2
+            if flags & _CMP_WE_HAVE_A_SCALE:
+                a = b = struct.unpack(">h", d[o:o + 2])[0] * _F2DOT14
+                c, e = 0.0, 1.0
+                o += 2
+            elif flags & _CMP_WE_HAVE_XY_SCALE:
+                a, b = [v * _F2DOT14 for v in struct.unpack(">hh", d[o:o + 4])]
+                c, e = 0.0, 1.0
+                o += 4
+            elif flags & _CMP_WE_HAVE_2X2:
+                a, b, c, e = [v * _F2DOT14
+                              for v in struct.unpack(">hhhh", d[o:o + 8])]
+                o += 8
+            else:
+                a, b, c, e = 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0
+            dx, dy = (a1, a2) if (flags & _CMP_ARGS_ARE_XY) else (0, 0)
+            if not (flags & _CMP_UNSCALED_OFFSET):
+                dx, dy = a * dx + c * dy, b * dx + e * dy
+            for cont in self.glyph_contours(gid, depth + 1):
+                out.append([(x * a + c * y + dx, b * x + e * y + dy, on)
+                            for (x, y, on) in cont])
+            if not (flags & _CMP_MORE):
+                break
+        return out
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Outline -> polygon -> coverage bitmap
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def flatten_contour(pts, scale):
+    """Convert a TrueType quadratic contour into a closed polygon in pixels
+    (y up, baseline at y = 0).  Handles off-curve points and the implied
+    on-curve midpoints between two consecutive off-curve points."""
+    n = len(pts)
+    if n == 0:
+        return []
+
+    start = -1
+    for i in range(n):
+        if pts[i][2]:
+            start = i
+            break
+    if start < 0:
+        # All points are off-curve: start halfway between the last and first.
+        x0 = (pts[-1][0] + pts[0][0]) / 2.0
+        y0 = (pts[-1][1] + pts[0][1]) / 2.0
+        seq = [(x0, y0, True)] + list(pts)
+    else:
+        seq = list(pts[start:]) + list(pts[:start])
+
+    poly = [(seq[0][0] * scale, seq[0][1] * scale)]
+    m = len(seq)
+    i = 1
+    while i <= m:
+        px, py, on = seq[i % m]
+        if on:
+            poly.append((px * scale, py * scale))
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        nx, ny, non = seq[(i + 1) % m]
+        ctl = (px * scale, py * scale)
+        if non:
+            end = (nx * scale, ny * scale)
+            i += 2
+        else:
+            end = ((px + nx) / 2.0 * scale, (py + ny) / 2.0 * scale)
+            i += 1
+        poly.extend(_quad(poly[-1], ctl, end))
+        poly[-1] = end
+    return poly
+
+
+def _quad(p0, p1, p2):
+    """Flatten a quadratic bezier, stepping at most ~0.25px along the control
+    polygon so even the sharpest serifs stay smooth at 32px."""
+    lx = abs(p1[0] - p0[0]) + abs(p2[0] - p1[0])
+    ly = abs(p1[1] - p0[1]) + abs(p2[1] - p1[1])
+    n = int((lx + ly) / 0.25) + 1
+    if n > 64:
+        n = 64
+    out = []
+    for k in range(1, n + 1):
+        t = k / float(n)
+        u = 1.0 - t
+        out.append((u * u * p0[0] + 2 * u * t * p1[0] + t * t * p2[0],
+                    u * u * p0[1] + 2 * u * t * p1[1] + t * t * p2[1]))
+    return out
+
+
+def rasterize(polys, left, top, w, h, ss=4):
+    """Nonzero-winding scanline fill with ss x ss supersampling.
+
+    ``left``/``top`` are the ink box origin in pixels with y measured *upwards*
+    from the baseline, so pixel row r covers y in [top - r - 1, top - r].
+    Returns h rows of w values, each 0 or 1.
+    """
+    if w <= 0 or h <= 0:
+        return []
+
+    edges = []
+    for poly in polys:
+        n = len(poly)
+        if n < 3:
+            continue
+        for i in range(n):
+            x0, y0 = poly[i]
+            x1, y1 = poly[(i + 1) % n]
+            if y0 != y1:
+                edges.append((y0, y1, x0, y0, x1, y1))
+
+    inv = 1.0 / ss
+    xs_pos = [left + c + (j + 0.5) * inv for c in range(w) for j in range(ss)]
+    cov = [[0] * w for _ in range(h)]
+
+    for r in range(h):
+        row = cov[r]
+        for j in range(ss):
+            py = top - r - (j + 0.5) * inv
+            xs = []
+            for (y0, y1, ax, ay, bx, by) in edges:
+                if y0 <= py < y1:
+                    xs.append((ax + (py - ay) * (bx - ax) / (y1 - ay), 1))
+                elif y1 <= py < y0:
+                    xs.append((ax + (py - ay) * (bx - ax) / (y1 - ay), -1))
+            if not xs:
+                continue
+            xs.sort()
+            wind = 0
+            span_start = 0.0
+            for (xv, direction) in xs:
+                if wind == 0:
+                    span_start = xv
+                wind += direction
+                if wind != 0 or xv <= span_start:
+                    continue
+                c0 = max(0, _floor(span_start - left))
+                c1 = min(w - 1, _floor(xv - left))
+                for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
+                    base = c * ss
+                    n_hit = 0
+                    for i in range(ss):
+                        if span_start <= xs_pos[base + i] < xv:
+                            n_hit += 1
+                    row[c] += n_hit
+
+    return [[1 if v * 2 >= ss * ss else 0 for v in row] for row in cov]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Atlas packing
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def pack_shelves(items, max_w=4096, max_h=4096):
+    """Shelf-pack (w, h, key) items; returns (atlas_w, atlas_h, {key: (x, y)}).
+
+    Items are sorted tallest-first, which keeps shelf waste low.  Ties break on
+    the key so the packing is deterministic.
+    """
+    order = sorted(items, key=lambda it: (-it[1], -it[0], it[2]))
+    best = None
+    for width in range(256, max_w + 1, 128):
+        pos = {}
+        x = y = shelf = 0
+        ok = True
+        for (w, h, key) in order:
+            if x + w > width:
+                x = 0
+                y += shelf
+                shelf = 0
+            if y + h > max_h:
+                ok = False
+                break
+            pos[key] = (x, y)
+            x += w + 1
+            if h > shelf:
+                shelf = h
+        if not ok:
+            continue
+        height = y + shelf
+        cost = plane_stride(width) * height
+        if best is None or cost < best[0]:
+            best = (cost, width, height, pos)
+    if best is None:
+        raise BakeError("glyphs do not fit in a %dx%d atlas" % (max_w, max_h))
+    return best[1], best[2], best[3]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# fonts.bin
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def read_charset(path):
+    """Whitespace separated codepoints (decimal or 0x hex), '#' comments."""
+    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        lines = fh.readlines()
+    out = []
+    for tok in "".join(ln.split("#", 1)[0] for ln in lines).split():
+        try:
+            if tok.lower().startswith("0x"):
+                out.append(int(tok, 16))
+            elif tok.isdigit():
+                out.append(int(tok, 10))
+            else:
+                out.extend(ord(c) for c in tok)
+        except ValueError:
+            warn("charset: ignoring unparsable token %r" % tok)
+    return sorted(set(out))
+
+
+def build_font(font, codepoints, size):
+    """Rasterise, trim and pack one font size."""
+    scale = size / float(font.units_per_em)
+    ascent = int(round(font.ascent_units * scale))
+    descent = int(round(-font.descent_units * scale))
+    line_height = ascent + descent
+    box_top = line_height - ascent            # ink rows are offset by this
+
+    glyphs = []                 # [cp, advance, x, y, w, h, bitmap|None]
+    for cp in codepoints:
+        gid = font.cmap.get(cp, 0)
+        advance = 0
+        if gid:
+            aw = (font.advance[gid] if gid < len(font.advance)
+                  else font.advance[-1])
+            advance = int(round(aw * scale))
+        if not gid:
+            glyphs.append((cp, advance, 0, 0, 0, 0, None))
+            continue
+
+        polys = []
+        lo_x = lo_y = 1e30
+        hi_x = hi_y = -1e30
+        for cont in font.glyph_contours(gid):
+            poly = flatten_contour(cont, scale)
+            if len(poly) < 3:
+                continue
+            polys.append(poly)
+            for (px, py) in poly:
+                lo_x = min(lo_x, px)
+                hi_x = max(hi_x, px)
+                lo_y = min(lo_y, py)
+                hi_y = max(hi_y, py)
+        if not polys:
+            glyphs.append((cp, advance, 0, 0, 0, 0, None))
+            continue
+
+        left = _floor(lo_x)
+        top = _ceil(hi_y)
+        w = _ceil(hi_x) - left
+        h = top - _floor(lo_y)
+        if w <= 0 or h <= 0:
+            glyphs.append((cp, advance, 0, 0, 0, 0, None))
+            continue
+
+        shifted = [[(px - left, py) for (px, py) in poly] for poly in polys]
+        bitmap = rasterize(shifted, 0.0, float(top), w, h)
+        # Drawing rule from FORMATS.md:
+        #   ink top left = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y)
+        # so g.y is the ink top measured from (baseline - box_top).
+        glyphs.append((cp, advance, left, top - box_top, w, h, bitmap))
+
+    nonempty = [(g[4], g[5], i) for i, g in enumerate(glyphs) if g[4] > 0]
+    if nonempty:
+        aw, ah, pos = pack_shelves(nonempty)
+    else:
+        aw, ah, pos = 32, 32, {}
+    ah = (ah + 3) & ~3
+
+    stride = plane_stride(aw)
+    atlas = bytearray(stride * ah)
+    for (w, h, i) in nonempty:
+        g = glyphs[i]
+        x, y = pos[i]
+        for r in range(h):
+            row = g[6][r]
+            base = (y + r) * stride + (x >> 3)
+            for c in range(w):
+                if row[c]:
+                    atlas[base + (c >> 3)] |= plane_bit(x + c)
+
+    return {
+        "glyphs": glyphs,
+        "atlas": bytes(atlas),
+        "stats": {
+            "size": size,
+            "glyphs": len(glyphs),
+            "ink": len(nonempty),
+            "atlas_w": aw,
+            "atlas_h": ah,
+            "atlas_bytes": stride * ah,
+            "line_height": line_height,
+            "ascent": ascent,
+            "descent": descent,
+            "blank": len(glyphs) - len(nonempty),
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def bake_fonts(ttf_path, charset_path, out_path, sizes=FONT_SIZES,
+               glyph_count_bits=32):
+    codepoints = read_charset(charset_path)
+    if not codepoints:
+        raise BakeError("charset %s is empty" % charset_path)
+    font = TrueTypeFont(ttf_path)
+    built = [build_font(font, codepoints, size) for size in sizes]
+
+    if glyph_count_bits == 8:
+        for b in built:
+            if len(b["glyphs"]) > 255:
+                raise BakeError(
+                    "font at %dpx needs %d glyphs but the format declares "
+                    "u8 glyphCount; re-run with --glyph-count-bits 32"
+                    % (b["stats"]["size"], len(b["glyphs"])))
+
+    tables_at = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * len(built)
+    data_at = tables_at + GLYPH_SIZE * sum(len(b["glyphs"]) for b in built)
+
+    out = bytearray()
+    out += struct.pack("<IB3s", FONT_MAGIC, len(built), b"\0\0\0")
+    off = data_at
+    for b in built:
+        st = b["stats"]
+        if glyph_count_bits == 8:
+            rec = struct.pack("<BBBBIII", len(st["glyphs"]) & 0xFF,
+                              st["line_height"], st["ascent"], 0,
+                              off, st["atlas_w"], st["atlas_h"])
+        else:
+            # FORMATS.md declares `u8 glyphCount`, which caps a font at 255
+            # glyphs.  The required charset (ASCII printable + U+0400..U+04FF +
+            # the quotes and arrows) is 361, so the field is widened to u32 and
+            # the record padded from 16 to 20 bytes; every other field keeps its
+            # documented order and size.
+            rec = struct.pack("<IBBBBIII", st["glyphs"], st["line_height"],
+                              st["ascent"], 0, 0, off, st["atlas_w"],
+                              st["atlas_h"])
+        if len(rec) != FONT_RECORD_SIZE:
+            raise BakeError("internal error: font record is %d bytes" % len(rec))
+        out += rec
+    out += b"\0" * (tables_at - len(out))
+    for b in built:
+        for (cp, advance, x, y, w, h, _bm) in b["glyphs"]:
+            if not (-32768 <= x < 32768 and -32768 <= y < 32768):
+                raise BakeError("glyph U+%04X offset (%d, %d) does not fit "
+                                "in s16" % (cp, x, y))
+            out += struct.pack("<IHhhHHH", cp, advance, x, y, w, h, 0)
+    out += b"\0" * (data_at - len(out))
+    for b in built:
+        out += b["atlas"]
+
+    _write(out_path, bytes(out))
+    return [b["stats"] for b in built], len(out)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# IO
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+def _write(path, blob):
+    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
+    if directory and not os.path.isdir(directory):
+        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(path, "wb") as fh:
+        fh.write(blob)
+
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Verification / summary
+# ===========================================================================
+
+def _check(cond, msg):
+    if not cond:
+        raise BakeError("verify: " + msg)
+
+
+def verify_art(blob):
+    _check(len(blob) >= ART_HEADER_SIZE, "art.bin shorter than its header")
+    magic, version, count, entry_size = struct.unpack_from("<IHHI", blob, 0)
+    _check(magic == ART_MAGIC,
+           "art.bin magic is 0x%08X, want 0x%08X" % (magic, ART_MAGIC))
+    _check(version == ART_VERSION, "art.bin version is %d" % version)
+    _check(entry_size == ART_ENTRY_SIZE, "art.bin entrySize is %d" % entry_size)
+    table_end = ART_HEADER_SIZE + ART_ENTRY_SIZE * count
+    _check(len(blob) >= table_end, "art.bin table runs past end of file")
+
+    raw = []
+    for i in range(count):
+        e = ART_HEADER_SIZE + i * ART_ENTRY_SIZE
+        struct_end = ART_HEADER_SIZE + ART_ENTRY_SIZE * (i + 1)
+        name_len = blob[e]
+        _check(blob[e + 1] == 0, "entry %d has a non-zero reserved byte" % i)
+        _check(14 + name_len <= ART_ENTRY_SIZE,
+               "entry %d nameLen %d does not fit in the struct" % (i, name_len))
+        _check(struct_end <= len(blob), "entry %d runs past end of file" % i)
+        w, h, pixel_off, mask_off = struct.unpack_from("<HHII", blob, e + 2)
+        name = blob[e + 14:e + 14 + name_len].decode("ascii", "replace")
+        _check(blob[e + 14 + name_len] == 0,
+               "entry %s name is not NUL terminated" % name)
+        _check(0 < w <= 1024 and 0 < h <= 1024,
+               "entry %s has size %dx%d" % (name, w, h))
+        _check(14 + name_len + 1 <= ART_ENTRY_SIZE,
+               "entry %s name overruns the struct" % name)
+        _check(pixel_off % 2 == 0,
+               "entry %s pixelOff %d is not 2-byte aligned" % (name, pixel_off))
+        _check(mask_off % 4 == 0,
+               "entry %s maskOff %d is not word aligned" % (name, mask_off))
+        raw.append((name, w, h, pixel_off, mask_off))
+
+    names = [r[0] for r in raw]
+    _check(len(set(names)) == len(names), "duplicate texture names")
+
+    # Colour planes are packed in table order with no padding, so the colour
+    # region is exactly sum(w*h*2) bytes and the mask region starts right after.
+    pixel_bytes = sum(w * h * 2 for (_, w, h, _, _) in raw)
+    masks_at = table_end + pixel_bytes
+    _check(masks_at + pixel_bytes == len(blob),
+           "blob is %d bytes, expected %d (header+table, colour, mask)"
+           % (len(blob), masks_at + pixel_bytes))
+
+    prev_po = prev_mo = -1
+    rows = []
+    for (name, w, h, po, mo) in raw:
+        _check(po >= prev_po,
+               "entry %s colour planes are out of table order" % name)
+        _check(mo >= prev_mo,
+               "entry %s mask planes are out of table order" % name)
+        prev_po, prev_mo = po, mo
+        _check(table_end + po + w * h * 2 <= masks_at,
+               "entry %s colour plane runs past the colour region" % name)
+        stride = plane_stride(w)
+        _check(mo + h * stride <= pixel_bytes,
+               "entry %s mask plane runs past the mask region" % name)
+
+        base = masks_at + mo
+        opaque = 0
+        for y in range(h):
+            row = blob[base + y * stride:base + y * stride + stride]
+            for x in range(w):
+                if row[x >> 3] & plane_bit(x):
+                    opaque += 1
+        rows.append((name, w, h, opaque, w * h, po, mo))
+
+    print("art.bin  OK   version=%d  textures=%d  entrySize=%d"
+          % (version, count, entry_size))
+    print("         header+table %dB, colour plane %dB, mask region %dB "
+          "(%dB used), blob %dB"
+          % (table_end, pixel_bytes, pixel_bytes,
+             sum(h * plane_stride(w) for (_, w, h, _, _, _, _) in rows),
+             len(blob)))
+    print()
+    print("  %-10s %5s %5s %9s   %-10s %-10s"
+          % ("texture", "w", "h", "opaque", "pixelOff", "maskOff"))
+    for (name, w, h, o, n, po, mo) in rows:
+        print("  %-10s %5d %5d %8.1f%%   %-10d %-10d"
+              % (name, w, h, 100.0 * o / n, po, mo))
+    print()
+    return rows
+
+
+def verify_fonts(blob):
+    _check(len(blob) >= FONT_HEADER_SIZE, "fonts.bin shorter than its header")
+    magic, count = struct.unpack_from("<IB", blob, 0)
+    _check(magic == FONT_MAGIC,
+           "fonts.bin magic is 0x%08X, want 0x%08X" % (magic, FONT_MAGIC))
+    _check(1 <= count <= 255, "fonts.bin declares %d fonts" % count)
+    table_end = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * count
+    _check(len(blob) >= table_end, "fonts.bin table runs past end of file")
+
+    pos = table_end
+    rows = []
+    for i in range(count):
+        r = FONT_HEADER_SIZE + FONT_RECORD_SIZE * i
+        raw = blob[r:r + FONT_RECORD_SIZE]
+        # FORMATS.md declares u8 glyphCount; this baker emits u32 because the
+        # required charset is larger than 255.  Accept both on read.
+        glyph_count = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw, 0)[0]
+        if glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE > len(blob) - pos:
+            glyph_count = raw[0]
+        line_height, ascent = raw[4], raw[5]
+        atlas_off, atlas_w, atlas_h = struct.unpack_from("<III", raw, 8)
+        _check(0 < glyph_count, "font %d has no glyphs" % i)
+        _check(0 < ascent <= line_height <= 255,
+               "font %d has lineHeight=%d ascent=%d" % (i, line_height, ascent))
+        _check(atlas_off % 4 == 0,
+               "font %d atlasOff %d is not word aligned" % (i, atlas_off))
+        _check(atlas_w % 32 == 0,
+               "font %d atlas width %d is not a multiple of 32" % (i, atlas_w))
+        stride = plane_stride(atlas_w)
+        _check(atlas_off + stride * atlas_h <= len(blob),
+               "font %d atlas runs past the end of the blob" % i)
+        _check(pos + glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE <= len(blob),
+               "font %d glyph table runs past the end of the blob" % i)
+
+        prev_cp = -1
+        inks = 0
+        for g in range(glyph_count):
+            cp, advance, x, y, w, h = struct.unpack_from(
+                "<IHhhHH", blob, pos + g * GLYPH_SIZE)
+            _check(cp > prev_cp,
+                   "font %d glyph %d: codepoints are not sorted ascending" % (i, g))
+            prev_cp = cp
+            _check(advance < 4096,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X advance %d is implausible" % (i, cp, advance))
+            if w == 0 or h == 0:
+                _check(w == 0 and h == 0,
+                       "font %d glyph U+%04X has a half-empty box" % (i, cp))
+                continue
+            inks += 1
+            _check(x + w <= atlas_w,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: x+w=%d exceeds atlas width %d"
+                   % (i, cp, x + w, atlas_w))
+            _check(y + h <= atlas_h,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X: y+h=%d exceeds atlas height %d"
+                   % (i, cp, y + h, atlas_h))
+            _check((x + w + 7) // 8 <= stride,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X crosses the row stride" % (i, cp))
+            _check(-line_height <= y + line_height - ascent - h <= line_height,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X box is implausibly far from the baseline"
+                   % (i, cp))
+            has_ink = False
+            for row_i in range(h):
+                base = atlas_off + (y + row_i) * stride
+                for c in range(w):
+                    if (blob[base + ((x + c) >> 3)] >> ((x + c) & 7)) & 1:
+                        has_ink = True
+                        break
+                if has_ink:
+                    break
+            _check(has_ink,
+                   "font %d glyph U+%04X has a %dx%d box containing no ink"
+                   % (i, cp, w, h))
+        pos += glyph_count * GLYPH_SIZE
+        rows.append((i, glyph_count, inks, atlas_w, atlas_h, atlas_off,
+                     stride * atlas_h, line_height, ascent))
+
+    _check(pos <= len(blob), "font glyph tables overrun the blob")
+    print("fonts.bin  OK   fonts=%d  record=%dB  glyph tables end at %d/%dB"
+          % (count, FONT_RECORD_SIZE, pos, len(blob)))
+    print()
+    names = ["FONT_SMALL", "FONT_BODY", "FONT_TITLE"]
+    print("  %-4s %-11s %7s %7s %-11s %7s %7s %7s %10s"
+          % ("idx", "enum", "glyphs", "ink", "atlas", "lineH", "ascent",
+             "atlasOff", "bytes"))
+    for (i, gc, inks, aw, ah, ao, ab, lh, asc) in rows:
+        print("  %-4d %-11s %7d %7d %4dx%-6d %7d %7d %7d %10d"
+              % (i, names[i] if i < 3 else "?", gc, inks, aw, ah, lh, asc, ao, ab))
+    print()
+    return rows
+

+def cmd_art(args):
+    rows, size = bake_art(args.src, args.out)
+    print("art.bin   %d textures, %d bytes -> %s" % (len(rows), size, args.out))
+    print()
+    print("  %-10s %5s %5s %9s" % ("texture", "w", "h", "opaque"))
+    for (name, w, h, o, t) in rows:
+        print("  %-10s %5d %5d %8.1f%%" % (name, w, h, 100.0 * o / t))
+    print()
+    return 0
+
+
+def cmd_fonts(args):
+    sizes = tuple(int(s) for s in args.sizes.split(",") if s.strip())
+    stats, size = bake_fonts(args.font, args.charset, args.out, sizes,
+                             glyph_count_bits=args.glyph_count_bits)
+    print("fonts.bin %d fonts, %d bytes -> %s" % (len(stats), size, args.out))
+    print()
+    print("  %-5s %7s %7s %-11s %8s %7s %7s"
+          % ("size", "glyphs", "ink", "atlas", "bytes", "lineH", "ascent"))
+    for st in stats:
+        print("  %-5d %7d %7d %5dx%-5d %8d %7d %7d"
+              % (st["size"], st["glyphs"], st["ink"], st["atlas_w"],
+                 st["atlas_h"], st["atlas_bytes"], st["line_height"],
+                 st["ascent"]))
+    print()
+    return 0
+
+
+def cmd_verify(args):
+    for path in args.files:
+        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
+            blob = fh.read()
+        if blob[:4] == struct.pack("<I", ART_MAGIC):
+            verify_art(blob)
+        elif blob[:4] == struct.pack("<I", FONT_MAGIC):
+            verify_fonts(blob)
+        else:
+            raise BakeError("verify: %s is neither an ARTB nor an FNTS blob"
+                            % path)
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv=None):
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="nds_bake.py",
+        description="Bake gen/art.bin and gen/fonts.bin from the LibGDX assets.")
+    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")
+
+    p = sub.add_parser("art", help="bake the texture blob")
+    p.add_argument("--src", required=True, help="directory holding the source PNGs")
+    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
+    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_art)
+
+    p = sub.add_parser("fonts", help="bake the bitmap font blob")
+    p.add_argument("--font", required=True, help="source TTF")
+    p.add_argument("--charset", required=True, help="codepoint whitelist file")
+    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
+    p.add_argument("--sizes", default=",".join(str(s) for s in FONT_SIZES))
+    p.add_argument("--glyph-count-bits", type=int, choices=(8, 32), default=32,
+                   help="width of Font.glyphCount; FORMATS.md says u8 but the "
+                        "required charset needs 32")
+    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_fonts)
+
+    p = sub.add_parser("verify", help="re-parse blobs and check every offset")
+    p.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
+    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_verify)
+
+    p = sub.add_parser("summary", help="alias for verify")
+    p.add_argument("files", nargs="+")
+    p.set_defaults(func=cmd_verify)
+
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    if not getattr(args, "cmd", None):
+        ap.print_help()
+        return 2
+    try:
+        return args.func(args)
+    except BakeError as exc:
+        sys.stderr.write("nds_bake: error: %s\n" % exc)
+        return 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

You are porting an existing LibGDX Java game to a real Nintendo DS ROM in C.

REPO: /home/runner/hub-work/elementia/code
Original Java (read for reference): core/src/main/java/com/elementia/**
Your output: nds/source/gfx.c and nds/source/font.c  (CREATE BOTH)

=== ENVIRONMENT ===
* libnds 2.0 + calico + devkitARM. Build whole ROM with `./nds/build.sh` (Docker, 1-2 min).
* Syntax check ONE file (fast, ~15s):
    /home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp/synx.sh nds/source/gfx.c
  It runs arm-none-eabi-gcc -fsyntax-only with the right -I/-iquote paths, prints diagnostics, always exits 0.
* libnds APIs you may use: <nds.h>, vramSetBankA(VRAM_A_MAIN_BG), dmaCopy, DMA3, DMA_SRC_INC/DMA_DST_INC/DMA32,
  swiWaitForVBlank, powerOn(POWER_ALL_2D), lcdMainOnTop(), consoleDemoInit not needed.
* Do NOT write comments unless they carry non-obvious information (no "// loop", no "// init").

=== DESIGN (already fixed, do not change) ===
* DS native resolution 256x192. The whole game renders into a software framebuffer `u16 fb[256*192]`
  in main RAM, DMA'd to VRAM once per frame during vblank (Mode 3, VRAM_A_MAIN_BG).
* ALL coordinates use a BOTTOM-LEFT origin (same convention as LibGDX SpriteBatch), so you convert:
  screen row = SCRH-1-y.
* Two coordinate spaces:
  - world space (default for the game world): gfxSetWorld(camX, camY) then draw calls take WORLD
    coordinates; the renderer maps them to screen with  (sx = round((wx - camX) / WORLD_SCALE)),
    i.e. the world is rendered at HALF scale (WORLD_SCALE == 2 from nds/include/config.h).
    A 32px world tile therefore lands on 16 screen pixels.
  - screen space: gfxResetWorld() then draw calls take raw screen pixels, no camera, no scaling.
  A "draw" call receives world or screen coords depending on the current transform. Implement this as
  a single helper `map(float *sx, float *sy, float x, float y)` that converts + clamps.
* Draw calls take FLOAT coords (world coords are fractional), so round to integers once per call, never
  inside the inner pixel loop.

=== FILES ALREADY WRITTEN - READ THEM, THEY ARE THE CONTRACT ===
* nds/include/config.h   - constants, WORLD_SCALE
* nds/include/gfx.h     - the EXACT API you must implement (do not change the signatures)
* nds/include/font.h    - the EXACT API you must implement
* nds/FORMATS.md        - binary layout of the baked asset blobs (fonts.bin) - follow it exactly
* nds/include/element.h - rgb555() helper for 0xRRGGBB -> 15bpp

NEVER edit anything in nds/include/. If you are convinced a header must change, report it instead.

=== TASK 1: nds/source/gfx.c ===
Implement everything declared in nds/include/gfx.h:

* `gfxInit()` - powerOn(POWER_ALL_2D), lcdMainOnTop(), vramSetBankA(VRAM_A_MAIN_BG), zero the framebuffer,
  reset the transform and the tint to opaque white.
* `gfxBeginFrame()` - reset the transform to screen space, tint to opaque white, and clear the whole
  buffer to the last colour passed to gfxClear (or black). Do NOT DMA anything.
* `gfxFlip()` - swiWaitForVBlank() then dmaCopy the 256*192 halfwords to VRAM_A.
  Important for bandwidth: only copy the rows that actually changed since the previous flip. Keep a
  shadow copy of what was last sent (256*192 halfwords of main RAM is fine, we have ~3.5MB) plus a
  per-row "dirty" byte array; compare rows and only DMA the contiguous spans that differ. When the whole
  screen changes, that degenerates to one DMA of the full buffer, which is acceptable.
* `gfxClear(u16)`.
* `gfxSetWorld(float camX, float camY)` / `gfxResetWorld()`.
* `gfxSetTint(u16, u8)` - global modulate applied to textured draws (and to alpha-blended solid draws
  when the caller passes alpha < 255 and no explicit colour... keep it simple: the tint only affects the
  textured paths, exactly like SpriteBatch#setColor).
* `gfxRect/gfxRectA/gfxLine/gfxCircle` - solid geometry, clipped to the framebuffer, no transform
  surprises (they obey the current transform too, because the world renderer draws thousands of
  solid-coloured quads in world space - that is the whole point).
  `gfxRectA` alpha blends: out = (dst*(255-a) + colour*a) / 255.
  `gfxCircle` is a filled circle with a simple midpoint/span rasteriser.
* `gfxTex/gfxTexFlipX/gfxTexRegion/gfxTexRegionFlipX` - scaled, tinted, alpha-blended textured quads.
  The Tex is `{u16 w,h; const u16 *px; const u32 *mask;}`: px is a 15bpp colour plane (row major,
  top-left origin inside the texture) and mask is a 1bpp coverage plane (1 = opaque, LSB = leftmost).
  Sampling is NEAREST with a per-pixel bilinear-free step, so any destination size works.
  Alpha blending of a tinted sprite: t = (texel & 0x7fff) tinted by `tint` channel-wise
  ((texel_r * tint_r + 127) / 255 etc.), a = coverage255 * tintAlpha / 255, then blend into dst.
  Clipping must be exact: a quad partially off screen must not wrap.
* `gfxTexRot(t, cx, cy, size, angle)` - inverse-rotate each destination pixel back into texture space
  and nearest-sample; pixels outside the unit square are skipped. Only used for the melee slash arc,
  at most a couple per frame, so a slow implementation is fine.

PERFORMANCE - this matters. A single frame issues up to ~2500 quads. Requirements:
* No floating point inside pixel loops: precompute integer source step (fixed point 16.16),
  destination bounds, and the per-channel tint lookup.
* Early-out empty rectangles.
* Build with -O2 (the project does).

=== TASK 2: nds/source/font.c ===
Implement everything declared in nds/include/font.h, reading `fonts.bin` (see nds/FORMATS.md).

The blob is linked into the ROM. bin2o (re-implemented in nds/tools/bin2o.py) emits this header, which
you include:
    #include "fonts_bin.h"        // declares _fonts_bin_start[] / _fonts_bin_size
(the ARM9 Makefile has nds/gen on its include path, so `#include "fonts_bin.h"` resolves.)
The generated header also defines the convenience macro `fonts_bin`.

* `fontInit()` - validate the magic ('FNTS'), parse the 3 font tables, copy the atlas bitmaps into a
  static buffer (the ROM blob is in the cartridge/NitroFS address space which IS directly readable on
  DS for the ARM9 image, but copying to main RAM makes random access uniform - a plain memcpy is fine).
  Build per-font a sorted array of glyphs and a direct-mapped cache for codepoints (Cyrillic block plus
  Latin/digits/punctuation: a 512-entry u16 table indexed by (cp & 0x1FF) is plenty, fall back to a
  linear/binary search otherwise).
* UTF-8 DECODE: `textDraw` takes UTF-8 and must decode multi-byte sequences correctly. The game text
  is Russian, so this is not optional.
* `fontSetTint(u16, u8)`.
* `textDraw(x, y, font, utf8)` - draws with the pen baseline at (x, y) (LibGDX BitmapFont convention,
  the caller passes the baseline y). Returns the total advance in SCREEN pixels (float for API
  compatibility, but the value is integral).
* `textWidth(utf8, font)` and `textHeight(font)`.
* Newlines inside the string must advance to the next line (advance = 0, y -= lineHeight). The dialogue
  box relies on this.
* Unknown codepoints render as nothing and advance by the font's average advance.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
* Both files must pass `/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp/synx.sh <file>` with ZERO errors and zero
  warnings from -Wall -Wextra (warnings are printed but make the result unacceptable).
* No undefined symbols beyond the two blob symbols above.
* Do not touch any other file in the repo.

=== REPORT ===
Return: the two file paths, a 5-10 line summary of the blitter/dirty-row strategy, the final blob
symbol names you rely on, and anything in the headers you had to work around.

# Binary asset formats

Two blobs are produced offline by `nds/tools/nds_bake.py` (run by
`nds/gen/Makefile`) and linked into the ARM9 image with `bin2o`:

* `gen/art.bin`   – sprites and tiles
* `gen/fonts.bin` – three baked bitmap fonts (Latin + Cyrillic)

Both are little-endian and addressed from the start of the blob.

---

## art.bin

```
u32  magic     = 'ARTB' (0x42525441)
u16  version   = 1
u16  count     number of textures
u32  entrySize = 28
Entry entries[count]        // no padding, tightly packed
u16  pixelBytes             // total, multiple of 4
u16  pad0
u8   nameLen
u8   reserved
Entry entry[count]
--- data follows the table, in table order ---
u16  pixels[pixelBytes/2]   // RGB555, row major, top-left origin
u32  masks[pixelBytes*2/8]  // 1bpp coverage, row major, LSB = leftmost pixel
```

`Entry` (28 bytes):

```
u8   nameLen    length of the NUL terminated ASCII name that follows
u8   reserved
u16  w
u16  h
u32  pixelOff   byte offset of the colour plane inside `pixels`
u32  maskOff    byte offset of the coverage plane inside `masks`
u8   name[nameLen] (padded so the struct is exactly 28 bytes)
```

Canonical names, in the order the baker emits them:

```
grass dirt stone ice snow brick lavaA lavaB water
platform crystal tree chest hero slime wisp golem boss waypoint
```

Anything missing from the PNG set is simply absent; the C side falls back to a
procedurally painted texture.

---

## fonts.bin

```
u32  magic    = 'FNTS' (0x53544e46)
u8   count    number of fonts (3)
u8   reserved[3]
Font fonts[count]
--- data follows the table, in table order ---
```

`Font` header:

```
u8   glyphCount
u8   lineHeight   pixels between baselines
u8   ascent       pixels above the baseline to the cap line
u8   reserved
u32  atlasOff     byte offset of the 1bpp atlas inside the blob
u32  atlasW
u32  atlasH
Glyph glyphs[glyphCount]   // sorted ascending by codepoint
```

`Glyph` (16 bytes):

```
u32  codepoint   UTF-8 decoded
u16  advance     pen movement in pixels (unsigned, 8.8 would be nicer but the
                 font is baked at one size so integers are enough)
u16  x           ink box inside the atlas
u16  y
u16  w
u16  h
```

The atlas is 1bpp, row stride `(atlasW + 31) / 32 * 4` bytes, 1 = ink.

Drawing rule (see `font.c`):

```
pen baseline = (x, y)              // same convention as LibGDX BitmapFont#draw
ink top left  = (x + g.x, y + lineHeight - ascent + g.y)
```

Fonts are emitted in this order and bound to the `FONT_*` enum:

| index | enum         | point size |
|-------|--------------|------------|
| 0     | `FONT_SMALL` | 12         |
| 1     | `FONT_BODY`  | 20         |
| 2     | `FONT_TITLE` | 32         |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal bin2o replacement (the devkitPro container has bin2s but not bin2o).

Usage: bin2o.py <input.bin> <output.s> [symbol]

Emits an assembly stub that pulls the blob into .rodata and exports:

    _<sym>_start   .rodata address of the first byte
    _<sym>_end     .rodata address one past the last byte
    _<sym>_size    byte length

`<sym>` defaults to the input basename with dots turned into underscores.
"""
import os
import sys


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) < 3:
        sys.stderr.write(__doc__)
        return 2

    src, dst = argv[1], argv[2]
    sym = argv[3] if len(argv) > 3 else os.path.basename(src).replace(".", "_")

    with open(src, "rb") as fh:
        size = len(fh.read())
    inc = os.path.abspath(src)

    with open(dst, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("\t.section .rodata\n")
        fh.write("\t.balign 4\n")
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_start:\n")
        fh.write('\t.incbin "{inc}"\n')
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_end\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_end:\n")
        fh.write("\t.global _{sym}_size\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_size:\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_end - _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("\t.global {sym}\n")
        fh.write("\t.section .rodata\n")
        fh.write("_{sym}_data:\n")
        fh.write("\t.balign 4\n")
        fh.write("{sym}:\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_start\n")
        fh.write("\t.word _{sym}_size\n")
        fh.write(f"\t.size {sym}, 8\n")

    hdr = os.path.splitext(src)[0].replace(".", "_") + ".h"
    with open(hdr, "w") as fh:
        fh.write("/* generated by nds/tools/bin2o.py - do not edit */\n")
        fh.write("#pragma once\n\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned char _{sym}_start[];\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned char _{sym}_end[];\n")
        fh.write(f"extern const unsigned int _{sym}_size;\n")
        fh.write(f"#define {sym} ((const void *)_{sym}_start)\n")
        fh.write(f"#define {sym}_SIZE ((unsigned)_{sym}_size)\n")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

export OFILES := $(OFILES_BIN) $(OFILES_SOURCES)

		--manifest $(GEN)/art_manifest.h

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the Nintendo DS ROM (nds/elementia.nds) inside the official devkitPro
# container, so no local devkitARM install is required.
#
#   ./nds/build.sh            build the ROM
#   ./nds/build.sh clean      remove build output
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
IMAGE="${DEVKITPRO_IMAGE:-devkitpro/devkitarm:latest}"
ARTIFACTS="${ELEMENTIA_ARTIFACTS:-/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/tmp}"

if ! docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	echo ">> pulling $IMAGE"
	docker pull "$IMAGE"
fi

run() {
	docker run --rm \
		-u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
		-e HOME=/tmp \
		-e DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro \
		-e DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM \
		-v "$REPO:/work" \
		-v "$ARTIFACTS:/out" \
		-w /work/nds \
		"$IMAGE" \
		bash -c 'source /opt/devkitpro/devkitarm.sh && exec "$@"' bash "$@"
}

case "${1:-all}" in
	clean)
		run make clean
		;;
	assets)
		run make -C gen
		;;
	*)
		shift 2>/dev/null || true
		run make "$@"
		cp -f "$HERE/elementia.nds" "$ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
		echo ">> $ARTIFACTS/elementia.nds"
		;;
esac

- powerOn(POWER_ALL_2D)
- lcdMainOnTop()
- vramSetBankA(VRAM_A_MAIN_BG)
- zero the framebuffer

In calico, `pmGfxSetLcdLayout(PmLcdLayout_TopIsA)` sets DISPCNT bits for which display is on top, and I believe it also sets the display mode to 0 (off) by default. Actually let me check the calico implementation.

static inline void lcdMainOnTop(void) { REG_DISPCNT = (REG_DISPCNT & ~DISPLAY_1) | (DISPLAY_0 << 16) | ... }
```

`lcdMainOnTop()` only sets POWCNT_LCD_SWAP; it does NOT set the display mode. So to actually display VRAM_A in mode 3, gfxInit should also set `REG_DISPCNT = MODE_FB0` (0x00020000) or MODE_3_DISPLAY.

The task says gfxInit should do those 4 things, but it doesn't forbid setting the display mode. Without it, nothing appears on screen. The design mentions "DMA'd to VRAM once per frame during vblank (Mode 3, VRAM_A_MAIN_BG)". So setting the mode is required by the design intent. I'll add `REG_DISPCNT = MODE_FB0;` — wait, which macro? In libnds video.h: `MODE_FB0 = 0x00020000` ("video display directly from VRAM_A in LCD mode"). And MODE_3_DISPLAY = 0x00040000 ("frame buffer display (mode 3)" = direct VRAM display). Let me check the enum names available.

From the grep earlier: `MODE_FB0     = (0x00020000), /**< \brief  video display directly from VRAM_A in LCD mode */`. Let me look for MODE_3_DISPLAY / MODE_3.

Index: nds/gen/Makefile
===================================================================
--- nds/gen/Makefile	
+++ nds/gen/Makefile	
@@ -1,50 +1,60 @@
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Asset generation for the NDS build.
 #
 # Everything in here is produced on the host (inside the devkitPro container) and
-# ends up as a raw blob in ../gen, which the ARM9 Makefile turns into an object
-# with bin2o.
+# ends up as a raw blob in this directory, which the ARM9 Makefile turns into an
+# object with tools/bin2o.py.
+#
+# The baker is plain python3 + stdlib: it decodes the PNGs and the TTF itself, so
+# it does not need PIL, numpy, FreeType or mkbcfnt.
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-.PHONY: all clean fonts art
+.PHONY: all clean verify fonts art
 
-TOPDIR := $(CURDIR)/..
-REPO   := $(TOPDIR)/..
+TOPDIR := $(realpath $(CURDIR)/..)
+REPO   := $(realpath $(TOPDIR)/..)
 PY     := python3
 
 SRC_FONT := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf
 SRC_ART  := $(REPO)/core/src/main/resources/art
 
 GEN      := $(CURDIR)
-BLITTER  := $(CURDIR)/_stub.py
+BAKER    := $(TOPDIR)/tools/nds_bake.py
+WHITELIST := $(GEN)/charset.txt
 
-WHITELIST := $(CURDIR)/charset.txt
+FONT_SIZES := 12,20,32
 
-all: $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin
+all: $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin
 
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Bitmap font: mkbcfnt rasterises the TTF into BCFNT containers, the baker
-# trims every glyph and repacks them into a tight 1bpp atlas.
+# Bitmap fonts: nds_bake.py reads the TTF directly (head/maxp/hhea/hmtx/cmap/
+# loca/glyf, composite glyphs included), scan-converts the quadratic outlines at
+# 4x4 supersampling, trims each glyph to its ink box and shelf packs the 1bpp
+# atlas.  Output order is FONT_SMALL, FONT_BODY, FONT_TITLE.
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-$(GEN)/fonts.bin: $(SRC_FONT) $(WHITELIST) $(BLITTER)
+$(GEN)/fonts.bin: $(SRC_FONT) $(WHITELIST) $(BAKER)
 	@echo "baking fonts"
-	@$(PY) $(CURDIR)/_stub.py \
+	@$(PY) $(BAKER) fonts \
 		--font $(SRC_FONT) \
 		--charset $(WHITELIST) \
-		--out $(GEN)/fonts.bin \
-		--tmp $(GEN) \
-		--sizes 12,20,32
+		--sizes $(FONT_SIZES) \
+		--out $(GEN)/fonts.bin
 
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-# Sprites/tiles: the AI generated PNGs are cropped to the regions the game
-# actually uses and packed into 4bpp atlases.
+# Sprites/tiles: every source PNG is area-averaged down to the rectangle the
+# LibGDX build stretched it into, then split into an RGB555 colour plane and a
+# 1bpp coverage plane.  A missing PNG only warns; the C side has a procedural
+# fallback for it.
 #---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-$(GEN)/art.bin: $(SRC_ART)/*.png $(BLITTER)
+$(GEN)/art.bin: $(wildcard $(SRC_ART)/*.png) $(BAKER)
 	@echo "baking art"
-	@$(PY) $(CURDIR)/_stub.py \
+	@$(PY) $(BAKER) art \
 		--src $(SRC_ART) \
-		--out $(GEN)/art.bin \
-		--manifest $(GEN)/art_manifest.h
+		--out $(GEN)/art.bin
 
+#---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+verify: all
+	@$(PY) $(BAKER) verify $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin
+
 clean:
-	@rm -f $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/art_manifest.h
-	@rm -f $(GEN)/bc_*.bcfnt
+	@rm -f $(GEN)/art.bin $(GEN)/fonts.bin $(GEN)/art.bin.h $(GEN)/fonts.bin.h
+	@rm -rf $(GEN)/gen

Index: nds/tools/nds_bake.py
===================================================================
--- nds/tools/nds_bake.py	
+++ nds/tools/nds_bake.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,1420 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Offline asset baker for the Nintendo DS port of Elementia.
+
+Reads the LibGDX source assets
+
+    core/src/main/resources/art/*.png
+    core/src/main/resources/fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf
+
+and writes the two blobs described in ``nds/FORMATS.md``:
+
+    nds/gen/art.bin     ARTB  -- RGB555 colour plane + 1bpp coverage plane
+    nds/gen/fonts.bin   FNTS  -- three baked 1bpp bitmap fonts
+
+Both blobs are consumed by C code that this script must not have to know
+about, so the layout is fixed here and never guessed at runtime.
+
+Standard library only: no PIL, no numpy, no FreeType, no mkbcfnt.  PNG and
+TrueType decoding are both implemented here from scratch, so the pipeline runs
+under a plain ``python3`` on the host as well as inside the devkitPro
+container.
+
+Usage
+-----
+    nds_bake.py art    --src <dir> --out art.bin
+    nds_bake.py fonts  --font <ttf> --charset charset.txt --out fonts.bin
+                      [--sizes 12,20,32]
+    nds_bake.py verify art.bin fonts.bin
+    nds_bake.py summary art.bin fonts.bin
+
+``verify`` re-parses both blobs, checks the magic, walks every entry/glyph,
+asserts that every offset stays in bounds and prints the summary tables.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import struct
+import sys
+import zlib
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Format constants (nds/FORMATS.md)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ART_MAGIC = 0x42525441        # 'ARTB'
+ART_VERSION = 1
+ART_ENTRY_SIZE = 28
+ART_HEADER_SIZE = 12          # u32 magic, u16 version, u16 count, u32 entrySize
+
+FONT_MAGIC = 0x53544E46       # 'FNTS'
+FONT_HEADER_SIZE = 8          # u32 magic, u8 count, u8 reserved[3]
+FONT_RECORD_SIZE = 20         # see bake_fonts() for the layout deviation
+# FORMATS.md lists six fields for Glyph, which sum to 14 bytes but are declared
+# 16.  x and y must be signed - the drawing rule places ink *above* the pen
+# baseline - so the record is laid out as:
+#   u32 codepoint, u16 advance, s16 x, s16 y, u16 w, u16 h, u16 reserved
+GLYPH_SIZE = 16
+
+
+def plane_stride(w):
+    """Row stride of a 1bpp plane in bytes: whole 32-bit words, so the C side
+    can walk the plane with a ``const u32 *``."""
+    return ((w + 31) // 32) * 4
+
+
+# Bit order inside a 1bpp plane.
+#
+# FORMATS.md says "LSB = leftmost pixel" and include/gfx.h repeats it
+# (``const u32 *mask; // w*h bits, row major, LSB = leftmost pixel``), so pixel
+# (x, y) lives in bit ``x`` of byte ``x >> 3`` of row ``y``.  The font atlas is
+# written the same way; FORMATS.md does not state an order for it.
+def plane_bit(x):
+    return 1 << (x & 7)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Canonical texture set.  Names and order are normative (FORMATS.md); the sizes
+# are the rectangles the LibGDX build stretched each source texture into, which
+# is exactly what the NDS blitter draws into.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+TEXTURES = [
+    ("grass", 32, 32),
+    ("dirt", 32, 32),

+# Alpha ramp for the coverage plane.
+#
+# The AI generated sprites have soft, antialiased edges.  A hard ``alpha >= 128``
+# cut would chew holes in them, so coverage is remapped so that anything below
+# ALPHA_FLOOR is fully transparent and anything above ALPHA_CEIL fully opaque,
+# with a linear ramp between:
+#
+#     coverage = clamp((alpha - 40) * 255 / 168, 0, 255)
+#
+# i.e. fully transparent below alpha 40, fully opaque above alpha 208.  The
+# plane is still a hard 1bpp mask; the ramp only decides where the cut falls.
+ALPHA_FLOOR = 40
+ALPHA_CEIL = 208
+

+class BakeError(Exception):
+    """Recoverable problem with one asset; the caller warns and continues."""
+
+
+def warn(msg):
+    sys.stderr.write("nds_bake: warning: %s\n" % msg)
+
+
+def _floor(v):
+    return int(v // 1)
+
+
+def _ceil(v):
+    return -int(-v // 1)
