35:     public static void init() {
36:         try {
37:             if (Gdx.audio == null) { available = false; return; }
38:             FileHandle dir = Gdx.files.local("audio");
39:             dir.mkdirs();
40:             for (String n : NAMES) {
41:                 FileHandle f = dir.child(n + ".wav");
42:                 if (!f.exists()) f.writeBytes(wavPcm(sfxFor(n)), false);
43:                 sfx.put(n, Gdx.audio.newSound(f));
44:             }
45:             FileHandle mf = dir.child("music.wav");
46:             if (!mf.exists()) mf.writeBytes(wavPcm(musicSamples()), false);
47:             music = Gdx.audio.newMusic(mf);
48:             music.setLooping(true);
49:             available = true;
50:         } catch (Throwable t) {
51:             available = false;
52:         }
53:     }
54: 
55:     public static void play(String name) { play(name, sfxVolume, 1f); }
56: 
57:     public static void play(String name, float vol, float pitch) {
58:         if (!available) return;
59:         Sound s = sfx.get(name);

61:         long id = s.play(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, vol)));
62:         if (pitch != 1f) s.setPitch(id, pitch);

67:         musicStarted = true;

69:         music.play();

377:             for (double f : chord) {

387:             double root = chord[0] / 2;
388:             for (int beat = 0; beat < 4; beat++) {
389:                 float[] n = sweep(0.4, root, root, 0.16, 1);
390:                 envFade(n, 0.02, 0.36);

399:                 add(out, n, base + e * (RATE / 4));

401:         }

7: /** Simple pooled particle system with additive-ish glow dots. */
8: public class Particles {
9:     public static final int N = 320;
10: 
11:     public float[] x = new float[N], y = new float[N], vx = new float[N], vy = new float[N];
12:     public float[] life = new float[N], maxLife = new float[N], size = new float[N];
13:     public int[] color = new int[N];
14:     public boolean[] gravity = new boolean[N];
15:     int head;
16: 
17:     World world;
18: 
19:     public Particles(World world) { this.world = world; }
20: 
21:     public void emit(float px, float py, float vx, float vy, int color, float size, float life, boolean gravity) {
22:         int i = head;
23:         head = (head + 1) % N;
24:         x[i] = px; y[i] = py; this.vx[i] = vx; this.vy[i] = vy;
25:         this.color[i] = color; this.size[i] = size; this.life[i] = life; this.maxLife[i] = life;
26:         this.gravity[i] = gravity;
27:     }
28: 
29:     public void emitBurst(float px, float py, int color, int count, float speed, float size, float life) {
30:         for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
31:             float a = (float) (Math.random() * Math.PI * 2);
32:             float sp = speed * (0.4f + (float) Math.random() * 0.6f);
33:             emit(px, py, (float) Math.cos(a) * sp, (float) Math.sin(a) * sp, color,
34:                     size * (0.7f + (float) Math.random() * 0.6f), life * (0.5f + (float) Math.random()), true);
35:         }
36:     }
37: 
38:     public void emitSparks(float px, float py, int color, int count, float speed) {
39:         emitBurst(px, py, color, count, speed, 4f, 0.4f);
40:     }
41: 
42:     public void update(float dt) {
43:         for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
44:             if (life[i] <= 0) continue;
45:             life[i] -= dt;
46:             if (gravity[i]) vy[i] -= 900f * dt;
47:             x[i] += vx[i] * dt;
48:             y[i] += vy[i] * dt;
49:             if (world != null) {
50:                 // splash on ground
51:                 if (gravity[i] && y[i] < world.tileToWorldY(0) + 2 && vy[i] < 0 && life[i] > 0 && life[i] < maxLife[i] * 0.3f) {
52:                     vy[i] *= -0.3f;
53:                 }
54:             }
55:         }
56:     }
57: 
58:     public void render(SpriteBatch batch) {
59:         for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
60:             if (life[i] <= 0) continue;
61:             float t = life[i] / maxLife[i];
62:             int col = Art.mix(color[i] & 0x00ffffff, 0x00000000, (1f - t) * 0.6f);
63:             batch.setColor(((col >> 16) & 0xff) / 255f, ((col >> 8) & 0xff) / 255f, (col & 0xff) / 255f, t);
64:             float s = size[i] * 2f;
65:             batch.draw(Assets.glowDot, x[i] - s / 2, y[i] - s / 2, s, s);
66:         }
67:         batch.setColor(1, 1, 1, 1);
68:     }
69: }

display.text:
# Elementia

A compact anime-style Metroidvania for Android, built with [LibGDX](https://libgdx.com/).
Play as the heroine **Aria**, explore four elemental zones, unlock abilities and
defeat the Ice Lion.

## Zones & progression

| Area       | Theme    | Gating ability            |
|------------|----------|---------------------------|
| Meadow      | grass/sky | DASH (start)             |
| Cavern      | stone     | PYRO (chest) → burns vine |
| Frost Shrine| ice/snow  | CRYO (chest) → melts frost |
| Sanctum     | boss arena| DOUBLE_JUMP + BURST (boss)|

Combos, dash, elemental skill shots and reactions (vaporize ×1.6, melt ×2,
swirl ×1.3) are all in. One-way platforms, checkpoints (waypoint statues),
dialogue NPCs and auto-save included.

## Modules

- `core`    – game logic + art (Pollinations AI sprites/tiles optional,
  procedural fallback, see `tools/refresh_assets.py`)
- `desktop` – desktop backend for local testing
- `android` – Android application module
- `test`    – headless smoke tests

## Requirements

- JDK 17
- Android SDK (compileSdk 34, build-tools 35.0.0, minSdk 24)

## Build

```bash
# compile + headless test
./gradlew core:compileJava :test:run

# desktop launcher
./gradlew :desktop:run

# Android debug APK
./gradlew :android:assembleDebug
# output: android/build/outputs/apk/debug/android-debug.apk
```

> If the project ships `local.properties` it already contains your SDK path;
> otherwise create it with `sdk.dir=/path/to/android-sdk`.

## Controls

| Desktop                     | Touch (Android)             |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| WASD/arrows move            | Left/right on-screen pad    |
| SPACE jump (×2)             | Jump/skill buttons          |
| J attack (3-hit)            | Attack button               |
| K elemental skill           | Element switch via HUD      |
| L dash                      | Dash button                 |

The on-screen pad and buttons are visible on every platform (mouse-clickable on
desktop), and the in-game hints adjust to the platform automatically.

## Art assets

Environment tiles, characters and props are drawn by Pollinations AI
(`tools/refresh_assets.py` regenerates them into `core/src/main/resources/art/`)
and smoothed at render time. Any asset that is missing or failed to generate
cleanly falls back to the built-in procedural cel-shaded art, so the game
always runs offline.

## Render modes & audio

- **Visual modes** — cycle with `P` or the round **MODE** button (top right):
  `2D` (flat, no parallax) → `2.5D` (default: parallax ridges + zone fog +
  vignette) → `3D` (deeper parallax, zoomed-out pseudoperspective, handheld sway).
  The active mode is shown in the top-center HUD badge.
- **Sound & music** — all audio is synthesized at first launch (no asset files):
  music loops in the game screen, and one-shot effects cover jump, double-jump,
  dash, slash, melee/projectile hits, enemy death, skill shots, burst nova,
  chests, waypoints, burning/melting gates, NPC chatter, boss roar and victory.
  WAV files are cached under `audio/` in the local storage. On headless runs all
  audio calls are no-ops.

156: def largest_component(mask):

163:     size = [1] * (h * w)

204: def key_bg(img):

206:     Turn a near-uniform background (whatever hue the model produced) into
207:     transparency by colour distance to the border colour. Returns an RGBA
208:     image, or None when the background does not look uniform enough to key
209:     reliably (caller then keeps the procedural asset).

211:     arr = np.asarray(img).astype(np.int16)
212:     h, w = arr.shape[:2]
213:     m = max(6, h // 16)
214:     border = np.concatenate([arr[:m].reshape(-1, 3),
215:                              arr[-m:].reshape(-1, 3),
216:                              arr[:, :max(2, w // 24)].reshape(-1, 3),
217:                              arr[:, -max(2, w // 24):].reshape(-1, 3)])
218:     ref = np.median(border, axis=0)
219:     std = border.std(axis=0).mean()
220:     if std > 26:
221:         return None
222: 
223:     dist = np.linalg.norm(arr - ref, axis=2)
224:     threshold = max(54, std * 5 + 22)
225:     alpha = np.clip((dist - threshold) / 26.0, 0.0, 1.0) * 255
226:     alpha = alpha.astype(np.uint8)
227:

229:     if subject.mean() < 0.008 or subject.mean() > 0.92:
230:         return None
231:     alpha = np.where(subject, alpha, 0).astype(np.uint8)
232: 
233:     r, g, b = arr[..., 0], arr[..., 1], arr[..., 2]
234:     spill = (dist < threshold + 60) & (alpha > 0)
235:     avg = ((r + b) / 2).astype(np.int16)
236:     return Image.fromarray(np.dstack([
237:         np.where(spill, (r * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), r).clip(0, 255),
238:         np.where(spill, (g * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), g).clip(0, 255),
239:         np.where(spill, (b * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), b).clip(0, 255),
240:         alpha]).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA")
241: 
242: 
243: def key_white(img):
244:     """
245:     Key a pure-white (or near-white) background out. White = high luminance,
246:     low saturation, so the subject's own saturation keeps it intact.
247:     """
248:     arr = np.asarray(img).astype(np.int16)
249:     r, g, b = arr[..., 0], arr[..., 1], arr[..., 2]
250:     lo = np.minimum(np.minimum(r, g), b)
251:     hi = np.maximum(np.maximum(r, g), b)
252:     sat = hi - lo
253:     # alpha ramps 0 (distinctly white) -> 255 (subject) across the range lo 220..180
254:     alpha = np.clip((220 - lo) / 40.0, 0.0, 1.0)
255:     alpha = np.where(sat > 55, 1.0, alpha)  # colourful pixels are never background
256:     alpha = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8)

258:     subject = largest_component(alpha > 80)
259:     if subject.mean() < 0.008 or subject.mean() > 0.92:
260:         return None
261:     alpha = np.where(subject, alpha, 0).astype(np.uint8)
262:     return Image.fromarray(np.dstack([r.clip(0, 255), g.clip(0, 255), b.clip(0, 255), alpha]).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA")
263: 
264: 
265: def crop_to_alpha(img, margin=8):
266:     a = np.asarray(img)[..., 3]
267:     ys, xs = np.where(a > 40)
268:     if ys.size == 0:
269:         return None
270:     x0, x1 = xs.min(), xs.max()
271:     y0, y1 = ys.min(), ys.max()
272:     x0 = max(0, x0 - margin)
273:     y0 = max(0, y0 - margin)
274:     x1 = min(img.width, x1 + margin)
275:     y1 = min(img.height, y1 + margin)
276:     return img.crop((x0, y0, x1, y1))
277: 
278: 
279: # in-game drawing size per sprite -> aspect ratio width/height
280: DRAW_ASPECT = {
281:     "hero": 56 / 76.0,
282:     "boss": 88 / 76.0,
283:     "golem": 48 / 44.0,
284:     "slime": 44 / 38.0,
285:     "wisp": 48 / 40.0,
286:     "waypoint": 40 / 56.0,
287:     "tree": 32 / 48.0,
288:     "chest": 28 / 24.0,
289: }
290: 
291: 
292: def fit_ratio(img, ratio, size=512):
293:     """
294:     Resize keeping aspect, then pad transparent so the canvas has the same
295:     width:height `ratio` the game draws this sprite with.
296:     """
297:     w, h = img.size
298:     scale = min(size / w, (size / ratio) / h)
299:     nw, nh = max(1, round(w * scale)), max(1, round(h * scale))
300:     img = img.resize((nw, nh), Image.LANCZOS)
301:     cw = max(1, round(size)) if ratio >= 1 else max(1, round(size * ratio))
302:     ch = max(1, round(size / ratio)) if ratio >= 1 else max(1, round(size))
303:     canvas = Image.new("RGBA", (cw, ch), (0, 0, 0, 0))
304:     canvas.paste(img, ((cw - nw) // 2, (ch - nh) // 2), img)
305:     return canvas
306: 
307: 
308: def process(name, mode, bg, data):
309:     img = load_rgb(data)
310:     if mode == TILE_DONE:
311:         return img.convert("RGB").resize((256, 256), Image.LANCZOS).convert("RGBA")
312: 
313:     rgba = key_white(img) if bg == "white" else key_bg(img)
314:     if rgba is None:
315:         print("    background not uniform - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
316:         return None
317:     subject = crop_to_alpha(rgba)
318:     if subject is None:
319:         return None
320: 
321:     if mode == "wide":
322:         w, h = subject.size
323:         target = 16 / 7.0
324:         if w / h > target:
325:             band_h = int(w / target)
326:             y0 = max(0, (h - band_h) // 2)
327:             subject = subject.crop((0, y0, w, min(h, y0 + band_h)))
328:         else:
329:             need_w = int(h * target)
330:             canvas = Image.new("RGBA", (need_w, h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
331:             canvas.paste(subject, ((need_w - w) // 2, 0), subject)
332:             subject = canvas
333:         return subject.resize((512, 224), Image.LANCZOS)
334: 
335:     ratio = DRAW_ASPECT.get(name, 1.0)
336:     return fit_ratio(subject, ratio, 512)
337: 
338: 
339: def main():
340:     only = set(sys.argv[1:])
341:     jobs = [(n, ASSETS[n]) for n in ASSETS if not only or n in only]
342:     os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
343: 
344:     ok, failed = [], []
345:     for name, (prompt, mode, bg) in jobs:
346:         suffix = TILE_DONE if mode == "tile" else (KEY_WHITE if bg == "white" else KEY_GREEN)
347:         print(f"[{name}] fetching...", flush=True)
348:         data = fetch(prompt + suffix)
349:         if data is None:
350:             print("  FAILED fetch - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
351:             failed.append(name)
352:             continue
353:         out = process(name, mode, bg, data)
354:         if out is None:
355:             print("  FAILED post-process - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
356:             failed.append(name)
357:             continue
358:         path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name + ".png")
359:         out.save(path)
360:         print(f"  saved {os.path.relpath(path, os.path.dirname(OUT_DIR))} "
361:               f"({out.size[0]}x{out.size[1]} mode={mode}/bg={bg})", flush=True)
362:         ok.append(name)
363:         time.sleep(2)
364: 
365:     print(f"\nDone: {len(ok)} ok, {len(failed)} failed.")
366:     for f in failed:
367:         print(f"  missing (procedural fallback used): {f}")
368:     return 0 if not failed else 1
369: 
370: 
371: if __name__ == "__main__":
372:     sys.exit(main())

        "grey blue slate flagstones with moss in the cracks, " + STYLE,
        "tile", "tile"),

        "pale blue translucide ice with white frost cracks and sparkles, " + STYLE,

        "seamless tileable top-down red brick floor tile texture for a 2D platformer "

        "tile", "tile"),

        "seamless tileable top-down molten lava tile texture for a 2D platformer volcano, "
        "bright bubbling lava with red hot channels, second frame, " + STYLE,
        "tile", "tile"),
    "water": (
        "seamless tileable top-down water tile texture for a 2D platformer lake, "
        "clear blue water with soft ripples and reflections, " + STYLE,
        "tile", "tile"),
    "crystal": (
        "seamless tileable crystal gemstone block tile texture for a 2D platformer, "
        "glowing amber yellow crystal cluster with dark stone gaps, " + STYLE,
        "tile", "tile"),
    # ---- one-way wooden platform (keyed wide slab) ----
    "platform": (
        "single horizontal wooden plank platform prop for a 2D platformer, "
        "woven brown planks with rope and nails, side view slab, " + STYLE,

    # ---- background props (keyed sprites) ----

        "sprite", "green"),
    "chest": (

        "sprite", "white"),

    # ---- characters / monsters (keyed sprites) ----
    "hero": (
        "full body anime chibi heroine game character, silver-white bob haircut, "

        "standing centered, " + STYLE,

        "glowing golden orb, centered, " + STYLE,
        "sprite", "green"),
}

KEY_GREEN = " the subject fills most of the frame, uniform solid lime green "
KEY_GREEN += "background #00FF00, no scenery, no ground, no shadow, no text"
KEY_WHITE = " the subject fills most of the frame, isolated on a flat pure white "
KEY_WHITE += "background, no scenery, no ground, no shadow, no text, no watermark"

TILE_DONE = "tile"


def fetch(prompt, tries=6):
    url = BASE_URL + urllib.parse.quote(prompt)

def load_rgb(data):
    return Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)).convert("RGB")


def largest_component(mask):
    """Return only the biggest 8-connected component of a boolean mask."""
    idx = np.argwhere(mask)
    if idx.size == 0:
        return mask
    h, w = mask.shape
    parent = list(np.arange(h * w))
    size = [1] * (h * w)

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    def union(a, b):
        ra, rb = find(a), find(b)
        if ra == rb:
            return
        if size[ra] < size[rb]:
            ra, rb = rb, ra
        parent[rb] = ra
        size[ra] += size[rb]

    px, py = idx[:, 0], idx[:, 1]
    for k in range(len(px)):
        x, y = int(px[k]), int(py[k])
        base = x * w + y
        for dx in (-1, 0, 1):
            for dy in (-1, 0, 1):
                if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
                    continue
                nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
                if 0 <= nx < h and 0 <= ny < w and mask[nx, ny]:
                    union(base, nx * w + ny)

    root_sizes = {}
    for k in range(len(px)):
        r = find(int(px[k]) * w + int(py[k]))
        root_sizes[r] = root_sizes.get(r, 0) + 1
    best = max(root_sizes, key=root_sizes.get)
    best_mask = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=bool)
    for k in range(len(px)):
        if find(int(px[k]) * w + int(py[k])) == best:
            best_mask[int(px[k]), int(py[k])] = True
    return best_mask


def key_bg(img):
    """
    Turn a near-uniform background (whatever hue the model produced) into
    transparency by colour distance to the border colour. Returns an RGBA
    image, or None when the background does not look uniform enough to key
    reliably (caller then keeps the procedural asset).
    """
    arr = np.asarray(img).astype(np.int16)
    h, w = arr.shape[:2]
    m = max(6, h // 16)
    border = np.concatenate([arr[:m].reshape(-1, 3),
                             arr[-m:].reshape(-1, 3),
                             arr[:, :max(2, w // 24)].reshape(-1, 3),
                             arr[:, -max(2, w // 24):].reshape(-1, 3)])
    ref = np.median(border, axis=0)
    std = border.std(axis=0).mean()
    if std > 26:
        return None

    dist = np.linalg.norm(arr - ref, axis=2)
    threshold = max(54, std * 5 + 22)
    alpha = np.clip((dist - threshold) / 26.0, 0.0, 1.0) * 255
    alpha = alpha.astype(np.uint8)

    subject = largest_component(alpha > 60)
    if subject.mean() < 0.008 or subject.mean() > 0.92:
        return None
    alpha = np.where(subject, alpha, 0).astype(np.uint8)

    r, g, b = arr[..., 0], arr[..., 1], arr[..., 2]
    spill = (dist < threshold + 60) & (alpha > 0)
    avg = ((r + b) / 2).astype(np.int16)
    return Image.fromarray(np.dstack([
        np.where(spill, (r * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), r).clip(0, 255),
        np.where(spill, (g * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), g).clip(0, 255),
        np.where(spill, (b * 0.5 + avg * 0.5).astype(np.int16), b).clip(0, 255),
        alpha]).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA")


def key_white(img):
    """
    Key a pure-white (or near-white) background out. White = high luminance,
    low saturation, so the subject's own saturation keeps it intact.
    """
    arr = np.asarray(img).astype(np.int16)
    r, g, b = arr[..., 0], arr[..., 1], arr[..., 2]
    lo = np.minimum(np.minimum(r, g), b)
    hi = np.maximum(np.maximum(r, g), b)
    sat = hi - lo
    # alpha ramps 0 (distinctly white) -> 255 (subject) across the range lo 220..180
    alpha = np.clip((220 - lo) / 40.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    alpha = np.where(sat > 55, 1.0, alpha)  # colourful pixels are never background
    alpha = (alpha * 255).astype(np.uint8)

    subject = largest_component(alpha > 80)
    if subject.mean() < 0.008 or subject.mean() > 0.92:
        return None
    alpha = np.where(subject, alpha, 0).astype(np.uint8)
    return Image.fromarray(np.dstack([r.clip(0, 255), g.clip(0, 255), b.clip(0, 255), alpha]).astype(np.uint8), "RGBA")


def crop_to_alpha(img, margin=8):
    a = np.asarray(img)[..., 3]
    ys, xs = np.where(a > 40)
    if ys.size == 0:
        return None
    x0, x1 = xs.min(), xs.max()
    y0, y1 = ys.min(), ys.max()
    x0 = max(0, x0 - margin)
    y0 = max(0, y0 - margin)
    x1 = min(img.width, x1 + margin)
    y1 = min(img.height, y1 + margin)
    return img.crop((x0, y0, x1, y1))


# in-game drawing size per sprite -> aspect ratio width/height
DRAW_ASPECT = {
    "hero": 56 / 76.0,
    "boss": 88 / 76.0,
    "golem": 48 / 44.0,
    "slime": 44 / 38.0,
    "wisp": 48 / 40.0,
    "waypoint": 40 / 56.0,
    "tree": 32 / 48.0,
    "chest": 28 / 24.0,
}


def fit_ratio(img, ratio, size=512):
    """
    Resize keeping aspect, then pad transparent so the canvas has the same
    width:height `ratio` the game draws this sprite with.
    """
    w, h = img.size
    scale = min(size / w, (size / ratio) / h)
    nw, nh = max(1, round(w * scale)), max(1, round(h * scale))
    img = img.resize((nw, nh), Image.LANCZOS)
    cw = max(1, round(size)) if ratio >= 1 else max(1, round(size * ratio))
    ch = max(1, round(size / ratio)) if ratio >= 1 else max(1, round(size))
    canvas = Image.new("RGBA", (cw, ch), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    canvas.paste(img, ((cw - nw) // 2, (ch - nh) // 2), img)
    return canvas


def process(name, mode, bg, data):
    img = load_rgb(data)
    if mode == TILE_DONE:
        return img.convert("RGB").resize((256, 256), Image.LANCZOS).convert("RGBA")

    rgba = key_white(img) if bg == "white" else key_bg(img)
    if rgba is None:
        print("    background not uniform - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
        return None
    subject = crop_to_alpha(rgba)
    if subject is None:
        return None

    if mode == "wide":
        w, h = subject.size
        target = 16 / 7.0
        if w / h > target:
            band_h = int(w / target)
            y0 = max(0, (h - band_h) // 2)
            subject = subject.crop((0, y0, w, min(h, y0 + band_h)))
        else:
            need_w = int(h * target)
            canvas = Image.new("RGBA", (need_w, h), (0, 0, 0, 0))
            canvas.paste(subject, ((need_w - w) // 2, 0), subject)
            subject = canvas
        return subject.resize((512, 224), Image.LANCZOS)

    ratio = DRAW_ASPECT.get(name, 1.0)
    return fit_ratio(subject, ratio, 512)


def main():
    only = set(sys.argv[1:])
    jobs = [(n, ASSETS[n]) for n in ASSETS if not only or n in only]
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    ok, failed = [], []
    for name, (prompt, mode, bg) in jobs:
        suffix = TILE_DONE if mode == "tile" else (KEY_WHITE if bg == "white" else KEY_GREEN)
        print(f"[{name}] fetching...", flush=True)
        data = fetch(prompt + suffix)
        if data is None:
            print("  FAILED fetch - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
            failed.append(name)
            continue
        out = process(name, mode, bg, data)
        if out is None:
            print("  FAILED post-process - keeping procedural fallback", flush=True)
            failed.append(name)
            continue
        path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, name + ".png")
        out.save(path)
        print(f"  saved {os.path.relpath(path, os.path.dirname(OUT_DIR))} "
              f"({out.size[0]}x{out.size[1]} mode={mode}/bg={bg})", flush=True)
        ok.append(name)
        time.sleep(2)

    print(f"\nDone: {len(ok)} ok, {len(failed)} failed.")
    for f in failed:
        print(f"  missing (procedural fallback used): {f}")
    return 0 if not failed else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build a tagged Elementia release APK.
#
# Usage:
#   tools/release.sh                # bump minor version (x.y -> x.(y+1))
#   tools/release.sh 1.6.0          # explicit version name
#
# Bumps versionCode/versionName in android/build.gradle, commits them,
# tags v<version>, builds the signed release APK and pushes tag + branch.
# Release signing uses android/keystore.properties (gitignored); CI restores
# the same keys from GitHub secrets. On tag push, .github/workflows/release.yml
# rebuilds the APK and publishes a GitHub Release.

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ -z "$(git config user.email)" ]; then
    git config user.name "elementia dev"
    git config user.email "dev@elementia.local"
fi

BG="android/build.gradle"

vc=$(sed -nE "s/.*versionCode ([0-9]+).*/\1/p" "$BG")
vn=$(sed -nE "s/.*versionName '([^']+)'.*/\1/p" "$BG")
new_vc=$((vc + 1))

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    new_vn="$1"
else
    if [[ "$vn" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        new_vn="${vn%.*}.$(( ${vn##*.} + 1 ))"
    else
        new_vn="${vn%.*.*}.$(( ${vn##*.} + 1 ))"
    fi
fi
tag="v$new_vn"

echo "Release: $vn (code $vc) -> $new_vn (code $new_vc), tag $tag"

if ! git diff --quiet -- android/build.gradle; then
    echo "error: android/build.gradle has uncommitted changes; commit them first" >&2
    exit 1
fi

sed -i "s/versionCode $vc/versionCode $new_vc/; s/versionName '$vn'/versionName '$new_vn'/" "$BG"

git add "$BG"
git commit -m "release: $new_vn" >/dev/null
git tag "$tag"

./gradlew :android:assembleRelease

echo ""
echo "Tag: $tag"
echo "APK: android/build/outputs/apk/release/android-release.apk"
echo "Pushing branch + tag..."
git push origin HEAD
git push origin "$tag"

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 17

      - name: Restore signing keys from secrets
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.UPLOAD_KEYSTORE }}" | base64 -d > android/elementia-release.keystore
          printf 'storePassword=%s\nkeyAlias=%s\nkeyPassword=%s\n' \
            '${{ secrets.STORE_PASSWORD }}' \
            '${{ secrets.KEY_ALIAS }}' \
            '${{ secrets.KEY_PASSWORD }}' > android/keystore.properties

      - name: Set up Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4
        with:
          gradle-version: 9.7.1

      - name: Assemble release APK
        run: ./gradlew :android:assembleRelease

      - name: Publish GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          body: |
            Automated release build of Elementia.
          files: android/build/outputs/apk/release/android-release.apk

Excellent. Now let me compute per-zone visible draws. Let me simulate what a typical frame looks like.

Let me also compute gate draw counts precisely.

Gate definitions:
- VINE: x = 50*32 = 1600, y = tileToWorldY(27) = (46-1-27)*32 = 18*32 = 576, w = 2*32 = 64, h = 11*32 = 352
- FROST: x = 97*32 = 3104, y = (46-1-27)*32 = 576, w = 32, h = 22*32 = 704
- MAGMA: x = 111*32 = 3552, y = tileToWorldY(33) = (46-1-33)*32 = 12*32 = 384, w = 64, h = 5*32 = 160
- FIRE: x = 118*32 = 3776, y = tileToWorldY(43) = (46-1-43)*32 = 2*32 = 64, w = 32, h = 7*32 = 224

Wait — MAGMA gate y = tileToWorldY(33) = 12*32 = 384, h=160, so it spans world y 384..544. But the shaft is rows 29-33 → world y from tileToWorldY(33)=384 up to tileToWorldY(29)=512. So gate covers 384..544 which covers the shaft. OK.

Hmm, but the FIRE gate at x=3776, y=64, h=224 → world y 64..288. Row = 46-1-(wy/32): wy=64 → row 44; wy=288 → row 37. So rows 37..44 at col 118. That matches the comment "col 118, rows 37-43".

Gate overlay loop counts:
- VINE: w=64 → i=0,6,...,60 = 11; h=352 → j=0,6,...,348 = 59 → 11*59 = 649
- FROST: w=32 → i=0,6,...,30 = 6; h=704 → j=0,...,702 = 118 → 6*118 = 708
- MAGMA: w=64 → 11; h=160 → j=0,...,156 = 27 → 11*27 = 297
- FIRE: w=32 → 6; h=224 → j=0,...,222 = 38 → 6*38 = 228; plus flames j=0,10,...,220 = 23
Total = 649+708+297+228+23 = 1905 + 4 base gate draws = 1909.

That's the single biggest draw cost in the game. Good finding.

Parallax: 62 columns × 3 layers = 186.

Let me now write a simulation of the exact render() draw-call count for a few camera positions. Actually, let me do it approximately by hand but verify with a script.

Let me write the script.

Also, VRAM budget consideration for DS. Let's compute what textures are needed:
- whiteDot 2x2, glowDot 32x32, sparkDot 16x16
- tiles: 32x32 each (grass, dirt, stone, ice, snow, brick, lavaA, lavaB, water, crystal) — crystal is 24x30 procedural but AI version is 256x256
- platform 32x14
- bgGrass 32x48, bgChest 28x24
- hero frames: 13 x 56x76 in one strip = 728x76 procedural (AI hero.png 377x512 reused for ALL frames)
- slime 4x44x38 strip = 176x38
- wisp 48x40, golem 56x52, boss 88x76, waypoint 40x56
- slashTex 96x96, projTex 96x40 (6 projectiles)
- elementIcons 7x24x24 = 168x24

- facDay[6] + facNight[6] 64x64 each = 12 textures x 64x64

AI art: 19 PNGs totaling 2,461,184 texels. At 4bpp that's ~1.23 MB — way over DS VRAM (128 KB main + 128 KB extended = 256 KB, or 4 MB with main-card RAM for textures... actually main RAM can be used as texture memory in "main RAM texture" mode = 4 MB, but that's slow). Better: downscale AI art to native draw size (e.g., 32x32 tiles → 4bpp = 512 B each).

Let me compute the downscale-to-native-size budget:
tiles at 32x32 4bpp = 512 B each × 10 = 5 KB
platform 32x14 4bpp = 224 B
hero 56x76 4bpp = 2,128 B (×13 frames if we keep the strip = 27.6 KB)
slime 4x44x38 = 6,688 B
wisp 48x40 = 960 B
golem 56x52 = 1,456 B
boss 88x76 = 3,344 B
waypoint 40x56 = 1,120 B
chest 28x24 = 336 B
tree 32x48 = 768 B
slash 96x96 = 4,608 B
proj strip 96x40 = 1,920 B
icons 168x24 = 2,016 B
glow 32x32 = 512 B
Total ≈ 55 KB at 4bpp. Very manageable.

At 8bpp: ~110 KB. Also feasible in extended VRAM.

Fonts: ~170 glyphs. At 54px 4bpp: 170 × 64×64×0.5 = 348 KB — too big for one size. But we can use the DS's native font (8x16 4bpp) scaled 2x/3x, or use libnds font with "fontDefault" + custom. Realistic: subset to the ~74 non-ASCII + ~40 used Latin → ~120 glyphs, and limit sizes to {12, 18, 24} with nearest-neighbor integer scaling. 120 glyphs × 32×32 4bpp (for 24px) = 61 KB. Hmm still large. Use 3 font sheets: 8x12, 12x16, 16x24 → 120 × (8*12/2 + 12*16/2 + 16*24/2) = 120 × (48+96+192) = 120 × 336 = 40 KB. OK.

I have a complete picture. Here is the full architectural map.

---

# Elementia — Complete Architectural Map (LibGDX → NDS port prep)

**Repo root:** `/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/code`
**Build:** Gradle multi-module (`core`, `desktop`, `android`, `test`), LibGDX **1.13.1**, `gdx-freetype`, Java 17
**Git:** single commit `c8ab760 release: 1.6.1` (no history to mine)
**No devkitPro / Makefile / NDS scaffolding exists anywhere in the tree.**

---

## 0. File inventory (LOC)

| File | LOC | code-only | libGDX imports |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/code/core/src/main/java/com/elementia/world/World.java` | **1351** | 1131 | 5 |
| `…/core/Assets.java` | **960** | 732 | 6 |
| `…/core/Sfx.java` | **408** | 359 | 4 |
| `…/core/GameScreen.java` | **220** | 183 | 8 |
| `…/world/Enemy.java` | **216** | 189 | 1 |
| `…/core/Art.java` | **201** | 165 | 2 (1 unused) |
| `…/ui/TouchControls.java` | **188** | 153 | 4 |
| `…/ui/DialogueBox.java` | **155** | 126 | 6 |
| `…/ui/Hud.java` | **153** | 131 | 6 |
| `…/world/Player.java` | **139** | 114 | 2 |
| `…/world/Boss.java` | **136** | 115 | 1 |
| `…/core/TitleScreen.java` | **92** | 74 | 7 |
| `…/world/Entity.java` | **75** | 60 | 1 |
| `…/ui/Fonts.java` | **71** | 52 | 3 |
| `…/world/Particles.java` | **69** | 57 | 1 |
| `…/world/Projectile.java` | **50** | 43 | 1 |
| `…/core/ElementiaGame.java` | **41** | 32 | 1 |
| `…/core/Config.java` | **40** | 30 | 0 |
| `…/desktop/DesktopLauncher.java` | **38** | — | backend |
| `…/core/Element.java` | **22** | 18 | 0 |
| `…/core/InputState.java` | **21** | 15 | 0 |
| `…/android/AndroidLauncher.java` | **20** | — | backend |
| `…/core/Ability.java` | **19** | 15 | 0 |
| **core total** | **4606** | **3774** | — |
| `…/test/HeadlessTest.java` | **169** | — | headless backend |

**Rendering reality check:** there is **no `ShapeRenderer`, no `GLScreen`, no `GL30`, no `ModelBuilder`/`ModelInstance`, no `ShaderProgram`, no `ParticleEffect`, no `FrameBuffer` usage** anywhere. Despite `README.md:73-76` claiming a `2D / 2.5D / 3D` mode cycle with a **MODE button**, **that feature does not exist in the code** — grep for `MODE`, `2.5D`, `visualMode`, `renderMode`, `3D` finds only the vestigial `buildCityTex()` block in `Assets.java:867-956` (unused "3D city" textures). **The game is purely 2D `SpriteBatch` + `BitmapFont`.** This is very good news for the NDS port.

---

## 1. Per-file architectural summary

### 1.1 `core/Config.java` (40 LOC) — **PURE JAVA, 0 libGDX**
Every tuning constant in the game. Fully portable; becomes a `config.h`.

```
VIEW_W 960f  VIEW_H 540f            // world-space viewport (16:9)
GRAVITY 2100f  TILE 32f  MAX_FALL 1200f
PLAYER_W 22f  PLAYER_H 34f
MOVE_SPEED 260f  ACCEL 1800f  GROUND_DECEL 2600f  AIR_DECEL 900f
JUMP_VEL 700f  JUMP_CUT 0.45f  COYOTE_TIME 0.1f  JUMP_BUFFER 0.12f
DASH_SPEED 720f  DASH_TIME 0.16f  DASH_CD 0.5f
COMBO_WINDOW 0.5f  COMBAT_KNOCKBACK 220f  MAX_HP 100f  MAX_BURST 100f
SKILL_CD 1.4f  STATUS_DURATION 4f
CAM_LERP 4.5f   CAM_LOOKAHEAD 60f   <-- DEAD: 0 references in code
```

**Derived physics numbers (useful for the port):**
- Single-jump apex height = `JUMP_VEL²/(2·GRAVITY)` = **116.7 px = 3.65 tiles**; airtime ≈ **0.667 s**
- Double jump uses `JUMP_VEL*0.88 = 616` → **90.3 px = 2.82 tiles**
- Dash distance = `720 * 0.16` = **115.2 px = 3.6 tiles**
- Run speed = **260 px/s = 8.125 tiles/s**; ~5.4 tiles of horizontal travel per full jump arc
- Max fall = 1200 px/s = 37.5 tiles/s

---

### 1.2 `core/Element.java` (22 LOC) — **PURE JAVA**
7-value enum, each with `int bright` (ARGB), `int deep` (ARGB), `String name` (Russian, used directly in HUD):
`ANEMO(0xff81d4fa)` «Анемо», `PYRO(0xffff8a65)` «Пиро», `CRYO(0xffb3e5fc)` «Крио», `HYDRO(0xff4dd0e1)` «Гидро», `ELECTRO(0xffb39ddb)`, `GEO(0xffffd54f)`, `DENDRO(0xff66bb6a)`.
Ordinal order matters: `Hud.java:67` uses `activeElement.ordinal()` to index `Assets.elementIcons[]`.

### 1.3 `core/Ability.java` (19 LOC) — **PURE JAVA**
`enum { DASH, DOUBLE_JUMP, PYRO, CRYO, HYDRO, BURST }`, `starting()` returns `{DASH}`. Uses `java.util.EnumSet` → in C, a `u8` bitmask.

### 1.4 `core/InputState.java` (21 LOC) — **PURE JAVA**
7 continuous booleans (`left,right,up,down,jumpHeld`) + 4 edge-triggered (`jumpPressed, attackPressed, skillPressed, dashPressed`), cleared by `reset()` each frame. `up`/`down` are never read by any system.

---

### 1.5 `core/Art.java` (201 LOC) — **PORTABLE (Pixmap-only)**
Pure pixel-painting primitives writing into a `Pixmap` (RGBA8888). Imports `Color` but **never uses it** (dead import). Every method is trivially reimplementable against a `u16*` framebuffer:

`set, fillRect, outlineRect, fillCircle, outlineCircle, fillEllipse, outlineEllipse, fillTriangle (+inTri/sign), fillPoly (even-odd scanline), fillSector (angle sweep), vGrad, glow (radial, alpha-blended), blend (source-over), noise (deterministic integer hash), shade, mix, rgb, rgba, newPix`.
`blend()` at line 185 uses integer `/255` (non-normalized) — port verbatim to keep pixel-identical output.

### 1.6 `core/Assets.java` (960 LOC) — **PORTABLE if baked offline**
Builds **every** texture at boot. Two paths per asset:
- `aiTex(name)` (line 96): loads `art/<name>.png` via `Gdx.files.internal` if it exists, sets **`TextureFilter.Linear/Linear`**; returns `null` on any failure.
- `or(ai, fallback)` (line 109): AI texture if present, else a procedurally `Pixmap`-painted one via `makeTex()` which sets **`TextureFilter.Nearest/Nearest`**.

→ **Filter is a mixed bag: AI art = Linear (smoothed), procedural = Nearest.** On NDS you must pick one; use 2× nearest-in-a-256px-tile setup.

**Texture inventory created by `init()` (line 70):**

| Field | Proc. size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `whiteDot` | 2×2 | the universal solid/rect primitive — used for ~95 % of draw calls |
| `glowDot` | 32×32 | radial soft dot (particles, UI buttons) |
| `sparkDot` | 16×16 | **never referenced** — dead |
| `t_grass/dirt/stone/ice/snow/brick/lavaA/lavaB/water` | 32×32 | AI-overridable |
| `t_platform` | 32×14 | drawn as a 14-px-tall slab |
| `t_crystal` | 24×30 | solid decor |
| `t_bgGrass` | 32×48 | tree (from `tree.png`) |
| `t_bgChest` | 28×24 | chest (from `chest.png`) |
| `charFrames` + regions | **13 cols × 56×76 = 728×76** | idle[0,1], run[2..5], jump(6), fall(7), atk1(8), atk2(9), atk3(10), slide(11), hurt(12). With `hero.png` present, **all 13 slots alias the single AI region**. |
| `slimeTex` + `slimeFrames[4]` | 4×44×38 = 176×38 | squash cycle |
| `wispTex`/`wispReg` | 48×40 | |
| `golemTex`/`golemReg` | 56×52 | |
| `bossTex`/`bossReg` | 88×76 | |
| `slashTex`/`slashReg` | 96×96 | melee crescent |
| `projTex` + `proj[6]` | 96×40 strip, 16×40 cells | fire/ice/water/electro/wind/geo — **`proj[]` is never drawn** (`Projectile.render` uses `slashTex` instead) |
| `waypointTex`/`wpReg` | 40×56 | |
| `iconTex` + `elementIcons[7]` | 7×24×24 = 168×24 | |
| `t_road, t_sidewalk, t_grass3, t_park, t_plaza` | 64×64 | **DEAD** |
| `t_roof` | 32×32 | **DEAD** |
| `facDay[6]`, `facNight[6]` | 64×64 each | **DEAD** (12 textures wasted) |

Hero character painting (`drawChar` + `drawBackHair/drawFrontHair/drawHead/drawFace/drawTorso/drawArm/drawLeg/drawSword`, lines 323–542) is a chibi anime figure built from `fillCircle/fillEllipse/fillPoly/fillTriangle/thickLine` — ~220 lines that would become an **offline baked sprite sheet**, never runtime code on NDS.

`buildCityTex()`/`facade()` (lines 869–956) is ~88 LOC of dead weight you can delete outright in the port.

### 1.7 `core/Sfx.java` (408 LOC) — **PURE MATH, portable**
See §2.7.

### 1.8 `core/ElementiaGame.java` (41 LOC) — **libGDX-bound**
`extends com.badlogic.gdx.Game`. `create()` → `Assets.init(); Fonts.init(); Sfx.init(); setScreen(new TitleScreen(this))`. `pause()/resume()` → `Sfx.pauseMusic()/resumeMusic()`. `dispose()` → Sfx + Fonts.

### 1.9 `core/TitleScreen.java` (92 LOC) — **libGDX-bound**
`extends ScreenAdapter`. Own `SpriteBatch` + `OrthographicCamera(960,540)` centred at (480,270).
- `Gdx.gl.glClearColor(0.12,0.12,0.2,1)` + `glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT)` (lines 32–33)
- Background: rotating 7-element wheel — `for i in 0..6`: `batch.setColor(r,g,b,0.7f)`, `batch.draw(Assets.glowDot, x-14,y-14, 28,28)` on a circle of radius `120+sin(t*1.5)*8` → **7 draws + 7 setColor**
  ⚠ **Bug:** `setColor((col>>>16)&0xff, ...)` passes **ints 0-255** instead of `/255f` (line 54) → every wheel orb renders blown-out white.
- **Strings drawn (all Russian):** `"ЭЛЕМЕНТИЯ"` (title, 54 px), `"Аниме-метроидвания о стихий"` (28 px), `"Коснись экрана, чтобы начать"` / `"Нажми ENTER, чтобы начать"` (26 px), controls line (18 px, mobile vs desktop variants), `"Исследуй шесть миров стихий и верни свет Кристаллу Судьбы!"` (18 px)
- `batch.draw(Assets.heroIdle[(int)(t*2)%2], cx-28, 60, 56, 76)`
- Advance: `ENTER`/`SPACE` key-press **or** `Gdx.input.justTouched()` → `game.setScreen(game.newGameScreen(mobile))`
- **Total: ~8 sprite draws + ~5 text draws per frame.**

### 1.10 `core/GameScreen.java` (220 LOC) — **libGDX-bound (the only screen/controller)**
Fields: `world, batch (SpriteBatch), cam (OrthographicCamera 960×540), hud, dlg, touch, InputState state, onMobile, dieMsg, dialogOpen, camX, camY, Preferences prefs ("elementia-save"), inited`.

`show()` (39–64): opens `Gdx.app.getPreferences("elementia-save")`; on re-entry re-attaches input + music and **keeps the existing `world`**; on first entry builds `World`, loads `prefs.getString("save01","")`, creates `SpriteBatch`, `OrthographicCamera`, `Hud`, `DialogueBox`, `TouchControls`, `Gdx.input.setInputProcessor(touch)`, `Sfx.startMusic()`.

`render(float dt)` (72–164) order — **exact frame loop:**
1. `glClearColor(0,0,0,1)` + `glClear`
2. **Win-and-restart check first:** `world.gameWon && (ENTER | justTouched() | touch.tapConsumed)` → new `GameScreen` (full restart)
3. `dt = min(dt, 0.05f)` (20 FPS floor)
4. desktop: `updateKbd()`; then always `touch.update()`
5. intro dialogue if `world.introPending`
6. `world.update(state, dt)` **or** `dlg.update(dt)` when a dialog is open (world frozen)
7. if `world.saveDirty` → `prefs.putString("save01", world.save()); prefs.flush();`
8. dialog open/close latch; NPC dialogue pickup from `world.pendingNpc`
9. advance dialogue (`Z`/`ENTER`/`justTouched()`/`tapConsumed`), `touch.resetTap()`
10. `dieMsg` countdown when `!player.alive`
11. `state.reset()` (clears edge flags)
12. `cam.update()`
13. `batch.setProjectionMatrix(cam.combined); batch.begin(); world.render(batch, shakeX+camX, shakeY+camX…); batch.end();`
14. `hud.render(world, world.time, onMobile)` (own batch/camera)
15. `touch.render()` unless dialogue open (own batch/camera)
16. `dlg.render(world.time)` (own batch/camera)
17. if `dieMsg>0`: `hudDrawDeath()` — `"ТЫ ПАЛА!"` (54 px, red) + `"Возвращение к точке сохранения..."` (26 px)

`updateCamera(dt)` (166–180) — **manual camera; the `OrthographicCamera` is pinned at screen centre and the world is offset by hand in `render()`**:
```java
look = clamp(p.vx * 0.14f, -80f, 80f);          // Config.CAM_LOOKAHEAD (60f) is UNUSED
tx = p.x + p.w/2 + look - VIEW_W/2;
ty = p.y + p.h/2 - VIEW_H/2;
t  = min(1, dt * Config.CAM_LERP);              // 4.5
camX = lerp(camX, tx, t);  camY = lerp(camY, ty, t);
camX = clamp(camX, 0, 150*32 - 960);           // [0, 3840]
camY = clamp(camY, 0, max(0, 46*32 - 540));     // [0, 932]
cam.position.set(480, 270, 0);
```
Screen shake is added at draw time: `shX = world.getShakeX() + camX` where `getShakeX/Y()` returns `rand(-amt, +amt)` while `shakeTimer > 0`.

`updateKbd()` (182–190): `A/LEFT`, `D/RIGHT`, `SPACE`(held + just), `J`=attack, `K`=skill, `L`=dash.

**Camera clamp consequence:** world is **4800 × 1472 px**; a 960×540 window means the camera y can never go below 932 and never above 0 — so the top 44 rows and the deep volcano rows are only partly reachable. On a 256×192 DS screen the natural mapping is **256×144** (scale 0.2667 of 960×540) letterboxed 24 px top/bottom; that exactly preserves the same framing.

`resize(w,h)` (204–211): sets `cam.viewportWidth/Height` back to 960/540 (so **the game camera never adapts to aspect** — black bars will appear on non-16:9), and forwards to `hud/touch/dlg.resize(w,h)` which use **real device pixels**.

---

### 1.11 `world/Entity.java` (75 LOC) — **near-PURE**
Fields: `x,y,w,h` (AABB, origin = bottom-left), `vx,vy`, `grounded`, `int facing(±1)`, `hp,maxHp` (int), `alive`, `hitFlash` (0.16 s white flash), `statusLife`, `Element status`, `deadTimer` (0.4 s), and `final com.badlogic.gdx.math.Rectangle rect` — **the only libGDX type; used in `World.applyMeleeHits()` for `e.rect.contains(...)`. Replace with an inline AABB test.**
`applyDamage(dmg, crit, knockX, knockY)` → crit ×1.8, sets `vx=knockX; vy=knockY`, on death `alive=false; deadTimer=0.4f; onDie()`.
`tick(dt)` decays hitFlash/statusLife/deadTimer. `heal`, `clearStatus`, `isPlayer()` (always false, unused).

### 1.12 `world/Player.java` (139 LOC) — **PURE (2 libGDX calls)**
Only uses `MathUtils.clamp(v,lo,hi)` (trivially portable) and a `Vector2 atkCenter` (→ `struct {float x,y;}`).

**Fields:** `EnumSet<Ability> abilities` (starts `{DASH}`), `Element activeElement=null`, `skillCd`, `burstGauge`, `burstReady`, `burstPower=100`, `int comboStep`, `comboWindow`, `attackTimer`, `atkCenter`, `atkRadius=18`, `atkHitApplied`, `coyote`, `jumpBuffer`, `dashTimer`, `dashCd`, `jumpsUsed`, `invuln`.
**Dead fields:** `animTimer` (never incremented → always 0), `atkDuration`, `summonTimer`, `holdDown`, `slideTimer`, `prevFacing`.

`enum State { IDLE, RUN, JUMP, FALL, DASH, ATTACK, HURT, DEAD }`.

**`moveAndCollide(world, dt)` (78–123)** — swept in fixed **4 px sub-steps**:
- Horizontal: advance `dx = clamp(remaining, ±4)`; probe 4 corners at `y+2` and `y+h-2` against `solidAt`; on hit → undo, `vx=0`, break.
- Vertical: `dy` in 4 px steps; falling probes `solidAt` **and** `platformAt` at `x+2` and `x+w-2` (one-way platforms); rising probes only `solidAt` at `y+h`. On landing, snaps `y = max(groundTopAt(x+2, y-1), groundTopAt(x+w-2, y-1))`.
- `grounded` recomputed from `solidAt(x+1, y-2) || solidAt(x+w-1, y-2) || platformAt(x+w/2, y-2)`; `if (grounded) jumpsUsed = 0`.

`updateState()` (130–138): ATTACK/DASH short-circuits; else `!grounded → (vy>40 ? JUMP : FALL)`, `|vx|>40 → RUN`, else IDLE.

Abilities: `canDoubleJump() = has(DOUBLE_JUMP) && jumpsUsed == 1`; `unlock(BURST)` refills `burstGauge` to 100.

## 2. Game systems in depth

### 2.1 `world/World.java` (1351 LOC) — the hub

#### Level / map format
**Procedural, not data-driven.** There is **no level string/array/asset file**. The world is built by imperative calls in `build()` (107–116) → `buildTerrain(); addGates(); addWaypoints(); addNpcs(); addChests(); addEnemies(); new Player(...)`.

- `int[][] tiles = new int[46][150]` — **indexed `[row][col]`, row 0 = TOP of the world, row 45 = bottom.**
- `MW = 150`, `MH = 46`, `T = Config.TILE = 32`
- **World size = 4800 × 1472 px = 6900 tile cells (5,670 AIR / 1,230 non-air).**
- Coordinate mapping: `tileToWorldX(col) = col*32`, `tileToWorldY(row) = (46-1-row)*32` → **row 45 = y 0 (bottom), row 0 = y 1440 (top).**
- Inverse: `col = (int)(wx/32)`, `row = (int)ceil(MH - 2 - wy/32)` — i.e. `ceil(44 - wy/32)`. The `ceil` makes a point exactly on a tile's **top face belong to the cell above**.

**Tile codes (line 22):** `AIR 0, GRASS 1, DIRT 2, STONE 3, ICE_T 4, SNOW 5, BRICK 6, PLAT 7, WATER_T 8, CRYST 9, LAVA_T 10`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cells | 5670 | 40 | 200 | 446 | 27 | 138 | 220 | **133** | 6 | 5 | 15 |

#### Collision
```java
solidAt(wx,wy):
  c = (int)(wx/T); r = rowAt(wy)
  if c<0 || c>=MW -> true          // side walls are solid
  if r<0           -> false         // sky is open
  if r>=MH         -> true          // bottom of world is solid
  t = tiles[r][c]
  if t in {GRASS,DIRT,STONE,ICE,SNOW,BRICK,CRYST}  -> checkGates(), else true
  // AIR, PLAT, WATER, LAVA fall through
  checkGates()                      // a gate block makes ANY tile solid
```
`platformAt()` → `tiles[r][c] == PLAT` only (one-way, downward only).
`supportAt(c,r)` (366) → true for any solid tile, PLAT, or an overlapping active gate.
`groundTopAt(wx,wy)` (356) → scans rows downward from `rowAt(wy)` and returns the first `tileToWorldY(rr)` that `supportAt`, else `-1`.
`tileAt(wx,wy)` returns `-1` out of bounds, else the raw tile code.
`rectsOverlap` (1345) is the standard 4-comparison AABB test; `dist` is plain Euclidean.

#### Camera
Camera lives in **`GameScreen`**, not `World` (see §1.10). `World` only supplies `getShakeX()/getShakeY()` (1349–1350) = `Math.random()*2*amt - amt` while `shakeTimer>0`. `screenShake(dur, amt)` takes `max` of both current values.

#### Update loop order — `World.update(InputState in, float dt)` (397–435)
```
1  time += dt ; shakeTimer -= dt
2  snapshot wasGrounded, vyBefore, wasInWater
3  handlePlayerInput(in, dt)     // movement, gravity, jump/coyote/buffer, jump-cut, dash, attack
4  player.moveAndCollide(this, dt)
5  player.updateState()
6  player.invuln -= dt
7  updateAttack(dt)               // combo timer + melee hits
8  updatePlayerSkill(in, dt)      // elemental projectile + burst nova
9  updateEnemies(dt)              // iterate backwards; drop + remove on death
10 updateProjectiles(dt)          // integrate, life cull, player/enemy hit, gate reaction
11 checkInteractions(dt)          // contact dmg, water, lava, death zone, chests, waypoints, NPCs, boss
12 emitAmbient()
13 cleanup()                      // removeIf dead / !alive
14 animation polish: dash trail, landing dust (+shake), water splash (+Sfx), run dust
```
`handlePlayerInput` detail (437–489): DASH is a hard state lock that skips everything but the dash timer; horizontal velocity uses **`MathUtils.lerp(vx, target, min(1, dt*accel/400))`** with `accel = ACCEL/AIR_DECEL/GROUND_DECEL` chosen by grounded/target state and `vx=0` snap below 5 px/s; gravity applied directly to `vy` with `-MAX_FALL` clamp; coyote/jump-buffer windows; jump-cut multiplies `vy *= 0.45` on release; dash sets `invuln = DASH_TIME + 0.05`.

Combat: melee `dmg = 8 + comboStep*4` (8/12/16) over a 3-hit combo, `atkCenter = (x+w/2+facing*20, y+h*0.6)`, `atkRadius=18`, `COMBO_WINDOW=0.5 s`, `comboStep = (comboStep+1)%3`, knockback `±220`. Skill projectile: `speed 380`, `dmg 14`, `radius 6`, `SKILL_CD 1.4`, spawned at `(x+w/2+facing*18, y+h*0.65)`, `vy = -114` when jumping. Burst nova: `40 dmg`, radius `180`, 40 particles, shake 0.5/8, requires `BURST`.

**Elemental reactions** (`applyElementToEnemy`, 569–588) — only when the enemy *already* carries a different element:
`PYRO↔HYRO ×1.6` (vaporize) · `PYRO↔CRYO ×2.0` (melt) · either side ANEMO `×1.3` (swirl) · base `20` damage, 14-particle burst, shake 0.2/4 when mult ≥ 1.5. Otherwise just applies `status = element, statusLife = 4 s`.

Hazards: water caps `vy ≤ 80` and heals 1 HP per 0.8 s while grounded; lava sets `vy ≥ 300` and deals 12 dmg per 0.5 s; `y < -40` = death zone → full damage + respawn.

#### Save/load
`save()` (1245) writes a **hand-rolled `;`-delimited string**: `{x:…;y:…;hp:…;mx:…;ab:DASH,BURST;vine:true;frost:…;fire:…;bd:…;tr:…;won:…;rx:…;ry:…;ch:0101010}`. `load()` (1271) re-parses with `split(";")` + `indexOf(':')` into a `HashMap`, clamps `maxHp ≤ 200`, validates `respawn` against `tileAt(...)==AIR`, restores gate actives from the flags, re-unlocks DOUBLE_JUMP+BURST if the boss died, and forces `activeElement = ANEMO`. Wrapped in `try/catch` → on failure prints to stderr and marks `saveDirty` to rewrite. Persisted through `Gdx.app.getPreferences("elementia-save").putString("save01", …)` + `flush()` **every frame in which `saveDirty` is set**.

`NPC_TEXT` (65–103) is a `static HashMap<String,String[]>` with **12 Russian entries** (`intro, elder, keeper, sage, witch, s_dash, s_vine, s_frost, s_boss, s_lava, s_hydro, s_win`). Each is `{speaker, body-with-\n}`.

Flags: `vineBurned, frostMelted, fireDoused, bossStarted, bossDefeated, trophyClaimed, gameWon, introPending`.

| 3 | tile pass: 32 cols × 19 rows scanned (608 cells), 1 `batch.draw(tex, wx-camX, wy-camY, 32,32)` per non-AIR cell, `setColor(zoneColor(zx,0.95))` each | **~56–140** |
| 4 | platform pass: rescan same 608 cells, `draw(t_platform, wx-camX, wy+T-14-camY, 32, 14)` for PLAT only | **~12–36** (platforms are *also* drawn in pass 3 via `texForTile`→`whiteDot`) |
| 5 | water pass: 608 cells, `draw(whiteDot, wx-camX, wy+T-20+sin(time*3+c)*2-camY, 32, 20)` | 0–6 |
| 6 | lava pass: 608 cells, 1 surface strip + 50 % chance of a full-cell flicker | 0–30 |
| 7 | **gates (NO camera culling, all 4 active)** | **1909** ⚠ |
| 8 | 4 waypoint statues (+4 glow when active) | 4–8 |
| 9 | 11 NPC speech bubbles (6×6 `whiteDot`) | 11 |
| 10 | 7 chests | 7 |
| 11 | 4 background trees (column-culled) | 0–4 |
| 12 | enemies (x-culled ±100 px; golem draws 2× when angered) | 0–~22 |
| 13 | player (1 draw; negative-width trick for facing; optional rotated slash crescent) | 1–2 |
| 14 | projectiles | n |
| 15 | particles (ring buffer never drains) | **320** |
| 16 | boss HP bar (220×8 at `VIEW_W/2-110`, `VIEW_H-36`) | 2 |
| 17 | `drawImmersion`: 1 tint quad + 4 vignette bars (`vm=14`) | 5 |

**Pass 7 breakdown (the dominant cost):** the gate "overlay pattern" loop draws a 2×2 `whiteDot` on a 6-px grid over the *entire* gate rect:
```
VINE   64x352  -> 11 x 59 = 649
FROST  32x704  ->  6 x 118 = 708
MAGMA  64x160  -> 11 x 27 = 297
FIRE   32x224  ->  6 x 38 = 228   + 23 flame quads
+ 4 base gate quads
                     TOTAL = 1909
```
**Total ≈ 2,500–2,650 sprite quads per frame**, of which ~**73 % is gate overlay**, ~**13 % particles**, ~**7 % parallax**. The 4-px `setColor`/`draw` granularity also means **~38 `setColor` calls inside `World.render` alone** (so ~80+ per frame across all systems). This is the single biggest NDS porting risk: the DS 2D engine (VRAM-affine sprites) caps out around 128–256 hardware sprites, so you must **convert the whole renderer to a software framebuffer** (256×192 `u16` VRAM buffer → `dmaCopy` / `swiWaitForVBlank`) and keep quads cheap, or aggressively batch (merge all same-texture, same-color quads; replace the 1909 gate dots with a pre-tiled texture; drop per-particle quads).

### 2.3 `renderParallax` / `drawImmersion` — the "2.5D"
There is **no camera-scrolling parallax** — `P_LAYERS` (line 856) are three *static screen-space* sine ridges:
```java
static final float[][] P_LAYERS = { {0.58f, 18f, 0.011f}, {0.50f, 26f, 0.008f}, {0.42f, 34f, 0.006f} };
//  {baseYfrac of VIEW_H, ampPx, wavelength}
y = VIEW_H*baseYfrac + amp*sin(sx*k + seed) + amp*0.5*sin(sx*k*2.2 + seed*1.7)
```
`parallaxCol(zone)` returns 3 `Color`s per zone (zone 0 meadow green … zone 4 volcanic red) at alphas 0.35/0.42/0.52. `drawImmersion` adds a zone tint quad at α 0.08 and a 14-px black vignette on all 4 edges at α 0.26. **This is the entirety of the "2.5D" look and it is trivially portable.**

### 2.4 `core/Sfx.java` — procedural audio (408 LOC)

**Format:** 16-bit signed **mono PCM WAV**, **22050 Hz**, standard 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header, `byteRate = RATE*2`, `blockAlign = 2`, `bitsPerSample = 16` (`wavPcm()` line 172, hand-written with `putStr/putLE/putLE16`).
**Synth primitives:** `rng = 987654321` LCG (`rng = rng*1103515245 + 12345`, bits 8..23), `silent, add, tone(len,f,amp)`, `sweep(len,f0,f1,amp,wave)` with `wave` 0=sine / 1=square (`signum(sin)`) / 2=triangle, `noise(len,amp)`, `envFade(in,out)`, `scale`, `envSwell`.
**Deployment:** `init()` writes each missing WAV to `Gdx.files.local("audio/<name>.wav")` (gitignored — see `.gitignore` "Runtime-generated audio cache"), then `Gdx.audio.newSound(file)`. Music is `Gdx.audio.newMusic("audio/music.wav")` with `setLooping(true)`. If `Gdx.audio == null` (headless) `available=false` and **every call is a no-op**.
Volumes: `sfxVolume = 0.6`, `musicVolume = 0.35`. `play(name, vol, pitch)` clamps vol to [0,1] and calls `Sound.setPitch(id, pitch)`.

**23 synthesized sounds** (`NAMES`, line 28) — 16 are actually called from gameplay:

| name | synthesis | called? |
|---|---|---|
| `jump` | sweep 0.18 s, 280→680 Hz, sine, amp 0.5 | ✅ ×2 (vol .7 pitch .9 / vol .6 pitch 1.3) |
| `dash` | sweep 0.28 s 500→900 + noise 0.28 | ✅ |
| `slash` | sweep 0.14 s 700→220 **square** + noise 0.1 | ✅ |
| `hit` | sweep 0.10 s 240→110 square | ✅ ×2 |
| `enemyDie` | sweep 0.30 s 430→70 **triangle** | ✅ |
| `hurt` | sweep 0.26 s 300→90 triangle, amp 0.7 | ✅ ×4 |
| `skill` | sweep 0.22 s 500→1200 square + noise 0.18 | ✅ ×4 |
| `burst` | sweep 0.50 s 150→45 sine + noise, ×0.75 | ✅ |
| `chest` | tone 660 → 990 | ❌ (chests reuse `skill`) |
| `waypoint` | arpeggio 660/880/1320 | ✅ ×2 |
| `talk` | tone 0.06 s 780 Hz | ✅ |
| `burn` | noise 0.55 (randomized gain) + square sweep 380→160 | ✅ ×3 |
| `melt` | sweep 0.50 s 900→200 | ✅ |
| `roar` | sweep 0.70 s 170→60 triangle + noise | ✅ |
| `victory` | 4-tone arpeggio C-E-G-C (523/659/784/1047) | ✅ ×2 |
| `coin`, `honk`, `cash`, `achieve`, `interact`, `portal`, `crash` | misc | ❌ unused |
| `splash` | square sweep 0.35 s 900→220 + noise 0.22 | ✅ |

**Music** (`musicSamples()`, line 360): **8.0 seconds = 176,400 samples**, normalized to 0.85 peak, looped. Structure: a low noise air bed (amp 0.012) + 4 two-second chords — **Cm (130.81/155.56/196.00), Ab (103.83/207.65/261.63), Fm (174.61/207.65/261.63), G (98.00/233.08/293.66)** — each with (a) a detuned ±0.1 % 2 s sine pad at amp 0.05 with a 0.45 s attack and a half-cycle envelope, (b) **4 square-wave quarter-note bass notes** at `root/2`, `sweep(0.4, root, root, 0.16, square)`, (c) an 8-note eighth arpeggio `{0,1,2,1}` ×2 for the first 4.

**NDS mapping:** all of this is trivially portable to `mmSound`/`soundPlaySample` — or better, keep the **generator** as a PC-side offline baker emitting 8-bit `raw` PCM8 at 8–16 kHz (8 kHz mono = 16 KB/s; the music would be 64 KB, sfx ~50 KB total). NDS hardware is fine at 22050 Hz too.

**Per-file classification:**

| Class | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Config` | **PURE** | 40 LOC, constants only |
| `Element`, `Ability`, `InputState` | **PURE** | 62 LOC total |
| `Art` | **PORTABLE** | Pixmap-only; retarget to `u16*` |
| `Sfx` (synthesis half) | **PORTABLE** | only WAV writing + `Sound.play` is libGDX |
| `World` logic (`update`, build, collision, save) | **PURE** | ~1,090 LOC |
| `World.render` + parallax + immersion + drawPlayer + heroFrame | **BOUND** | 262 LOC |
| `Player`, `Entity` | **PURE** | `MathUtils.clamp` + `Vector2`/`Rectangle` are the only libGDX touches |
| `Enemy` | **PURE** logic / **BOUND** render | 189 / 32 |
| `Boss` | **PURE** logic / **BOUND** render | 115 / 9 |
| `Projectile` | **PURE** / 7 LOC render | |
| `Particles` | **PURE** / 11 LOC render | |
| `Assets` | **PORTABLE if baked offline** | 757 of 960 LOC is art generation; ~88 LOC is dead city textures |
| `GameScreen`, `TitleScreen`, `ElementiaGame`, `Hud`, `Fonts` | **100 % BOUND** | 656 LOC total, must be rewritten against libnds |
| `DialogueBox` | **PARTIAL** | typewriter `update`/`advance`/`show` portable; `render`+`drawWrapped` bound |
| `TouchControls` | **PARTIAL** | button-coordinate math + `inCircle` + edge-detection portable; `InputAdapter` + `SpriteBatch` bound |

**Quantitative estimate:**

| Bucket | LOC | % of core (4606) |
|---|---|---|
| **Pure logic / simulation** (Config, Element, Ability, InputState, Entity, Player, Enemy logic, Boss logic, Projectile logic, Particles logic, World logic) | **~2,000** | **~43 %** |
| **Portable-but-render-adjacent** (`Art` 200, `Sfx` synth ~360, `Assets` 757 bakeable, `World.render` 262, `DialogueBox` logic ~50, `TouchControls` layout ~40) | **~1,670** | **~36 %** |
| **Hard libGDX-bound** (`GameScreen` 220, `TitleScreen` 92, `ElementiaGame` 41, `Hud` 153, `Fonts` 71, `Enemy.render` 32, `DialogueBox.render` 61, `TouchControls.render` 40, `Boss/Projectile/Particles.render` 27) | **~737** | **~16 %** |

**Net:** roughly **80 % of the codebase is platform-independent logic or offline-bakeable asset generation**, and only ~16 % needs a hand-written libnds replacement. The entire "engine surface" you must re-create in C is: a `SpriteBatch`-equivalent software blitter with `setColor` tinting + region/UV support + rotation (needed for the slash crescent), a bitmap font renderer, a WAV/`raw` sound player, a `Preferences` string store, and a `Screen` router. **None of the underlying simulation, level data, AI, or combat needs to change** — except you must decide how to reproduce `Particles` (currently broken), the 1909 gate dots, and the static 186-quad parallax.

### 2.6 Notable behaviours / latent bugs to decide on for the port
1. **`Particles.update()` is never called** → particles never move or die; steady state = 320 static full-alpha dots. *Design decision needed.*
2. **`setColor` integer bug** at `TitleScreen.java:54` and `Hud.java:100` — passes 0–255 ints instead of `/255f`.
3. **Gates are drawn with no camera culling** → 1909 of ~2500 quads per frame are off-screen.
4. **`Config.CAM_LOOKAHEAD` (60f) is unused**; camera lookahead is hardcoded `vx*0.14` clamped ±80.
5. **`OrthographicCamera` is pinned to centre and the world is offset manually** — the "camera" object is effectively a no-op projection; the port only needs `u_x = -(camX)`, `u_y = -(camY)` style offsets.
6. **Dead code to delete in the port:** `desktop/build.gradle` references a non-existent `com.elementia.desktop.HeadlessVerify` (`runHeadless` task will fail), `Assets.buildCityTex()` (~88 LOC, 18 unused textures), `Assets.sparkDot`, `Assets.proj[6]`/`projTex` (never drawn), `Assets.heroSlide`, `Sfx` names `chest/coin/honk/cash/achieve/interact/portal/crash`, `Player.{animTimer, atkDuration, summonTimer, holdDown, slideTimer, prevFacing}`, `Entity.isPlayer()/clearStatus()`, `World.CAVE_CRYSTALS`, `Fonts.controls`, `Particles.emit`'s `gravity` branch.
7. **`README.md` §"Render modes & audio" describing 2D/2.5D/3D and a MODE button is fiction** — not implemented.
8. `InputState.up/down` are declared but never read.
9. `Enemy.gravityMove` lines 158–160 (`float fall = |vx|*dt; y -= min(fall,0); y += max(0,fall);`) is a no-op.

## 4. Test module

**`/home/runner/hub-work/elementia/code/test/src/main/java/com/elementia/test/HeadlessTest.java`** (169 LOC) — a **plain `main()`**, not JUnit. Runs `HeadlessApplication` at `updatesPerSecond = 60`, does all work inside `create()`, sets `pass`, calls `Gdx.app.exit()`, then busy-waits up to **150 s** (`for i<15000 Thread.sleep(10)`) and `System.exit(pass ? 0 : 1)`. `enableAssertions = true` in `test/build.gradle`, so the `assert` statements are live.

**Assertions, in order:**
1. `new World()` constructs; logs `World: 150x46 tiles`
2. `p != null`, `p.hp > 0`, `p.alive`
3. **120-step walk** (2 s at 1/60) holding `in.right = true`; logs position/`grounded`/`vy`/`tileBelow` every 30 steps
4. `p.x > 12*32` → **"Player didn't move right"**
5. `p.alive` → "Player died during simulation"
6. `w.enemies.size() > 0`, `w.gates.size() > 0`, `w.waypoints.size() > 0`
7. **Jump test**: one `jumpPressed`+`jumpHeld` frame, then 30 more held frames (logs position; no assertion)
8. **Save/load round-trip**: `data.contains(";ab:")`; move player to (100,100); `w.load(data)`; assert `|Δx|<1`, `|Δy|<1`, `|Δhp|<1`
9. **NPC one-shot dialogue**: place player at `elder` (col 14, row 28), 1 update → `pendingNpc == "elder"`; then 120 idle updates → `pendingNpc` stays `null` ("must not re-trigger while standing in range")
10. **Touch controls edge-triggering** — the most detailed test. `resize(1280,720)` → `uiScale = 720/540 = 1.333`. Asserts baseline flags clear, then taps the **exact computed button centres**:
    - jump `(1067, 493)` → `jumpHeld` + `jumpPressed` set; second `update()` → `jumpPressed` **false** (no auto-repeat); `touchUp` → `jumpHeld` false
    - attack `(1147, 573)` → same cycle
    - dash `(1200, 467)` → `dashPressed` set on press, cleared on release
11. **Audio headless safety**: `Sfx.init(); Sfx.play("jump"); Sfx.startMusic()` must not throw (this relies on the `Gdx.audio == null` early-out)

This test is an excellent **porting acceptance suite** — every assertion is on pure logic except #10, which encodes the exact touch-layout math. Port #10 first and the rest follows.

**devkitPro-style test runner scripts: there are none.** The only scripts in the repo are `tools/release.sh` (Android APK version bump + tag + Gradle assemble + push, 60 LOC) and `tools/refresh_assets.py` (art regeneration). `.github/workflows/release.yml` only builds the signed Android APK on `v*` tags — **there is no CI test job, no Makefile, no `*.mk`, no devkitARM integration anywhere.** You will be writing the DS test harness from scratch (a natural choice is a `make -f` target running the same assertion set on top of `devkitPro/libnds` with a stubbed audio backend).

## 5. Recommended DS-port surface (derived)

| Java | Replace with |
|---|---|
| `SpriteBatch` (begin/setColor/draw/rotated draw) | one software blitter into a `u16[256*192]` VRAM buffer, `dmaCopy`/`swiWaitForVBlank` at flip |
| `Texture`, `TextureRegion` | `u16*` atlas pages + UV rects; one draw-quad primitive |
| `whiteDot`/`glowDot` quads | 1×1 / soft-dot sub-rects in the atlas (the code already funnels ~95 % of draws through these two) |
| `BitmapFont` + `GlyphLayout` | pre-baked 4-bpp glyph atlas + integer `scale = (w*scale)>>8`; word-wrap needs only advance widths |
| `Gdx.input` `InputAdapter` | `scanKeys()` + touch-screen `TouchScreen` SPI; feed the same `InputState` struct |
| `Gdx.app.getPreferences` | save string to `__EternalRom`/save file, or a 32-byte binary struct (the current format is 120 chars) |
| `Gdx.audio` `Sound`/`Music` | `soundPlaySample` / `mmStream` / `mmSound`; WAVs baked offline to `raw` PCM8 |
| `Gdx.files.internal("art/*.png")` | pre-packed atlas pages in the ROM |
| `OrthographicCamera` | trivial `ortho()` projection; world offset is already manual |
| 1909 gate overlay quads | one pre-tiled 6×6-pattern texture per gate type (4 textures, 1 draw each) |
| 320 particle quads | decide: implement real `Particles.update` (with NDS-friendly caps, e.g. 64) or drop |
